The bills span a wide set of issue areas, so an ask can connect to many of them. He takes charge of a conversation with some regularity. Dependability dips a little in shepherding bills, so a yes requires a dated check and an accountable lead to hold.

archetype.justification: Her few bills, narrow issue range and practical outlook fit an ox that works one field at a time.

Emilia Sykes.bottom_line: Bring one narrow, practical ask and a written path for it, since follow through on bills is her weak spot.
do: Bring the practical next steps written out before the meeting
Limit the ask to the one issue area her bills already cover
Offer a visible shared role, such as announcing the result together
dont: Stack a second issue onto the ask in the same meeting
Treat a polite nod as a settled commitment
Emilia Sykes.warning_sign: Usually her hearing manner runs far less confrontational, and she keeps to the questions asked. If her tone sharpens in a formal setting and she presses past the question, she is losing patience with the process. Hold to the question and confirm the next step.
Emilia Sykes.follow_up: Send her a brief written plan naming the bill step, who owns it, and the date her reply is needed.
Emilia Sykes.personality: Sykes is practical and narrowly focused, and her legislation spans a smaller set of topics than nearly any colleague's. Somewhat outgoing in public, she still trails most colleagues on follow through. Her practical streak keeps her on one plan at a time, and she represents Ohio. Concrete steps over sweeping goals suit her, so a plan with clear milestones works best.
Emilia Sykes.speaks: Pace runs a bit quicker than most, with somewhat shorter breaks between phrases and her tone sits much flatter than most. Word choices stay within a tighter set of topics than most speakers use, which keeps her talk focused. Delivery is brisk and fairly flat, so listeners hear one even line rather than shifts in tone. Short pauses keep the pace moving, so there is little room to interject.
Emilia Sykes.decides: Her test is how small and concrete a request is, and a plan that fits her narrow area of work gets a hearing. With a narrow legislative footprint, a broad request reads as a stretch for her. Pressure from outside the building shifts her more than it shifts most lawmakers, so outside backing carries real weight. Her follow through is much less dependable than most, so a yes holds only with a dated next step attached.

archetype.justification: She is very outgoing and very careful, and her floor speeches run a notch quicker than most.

Emily Randall.bottom_line: Put the people this ask helps at the center of the case. That is the frame that fits her best, so build the whole pitch around it.
do: Bring one clear story of a person the ask would help
Skip rebuttal drills if the meeting turns formal
Ask allied groups to phone her office, since outside calls move her more than most
Name the common ground with families who rely on public coverage, where it honestly fits
dont: Dismiss opposing groups as noise, when her positions move with pressure
Read her soft hearing tone as a commitment to the ask
Count on her to front the ask, though she is outgoing and much less visible
Emily Randall.warning_sign: In hearings she usually keeps a mild tone. If she presses one point across several questions, she is testing that point, not the whole ask. Ask her whether that single point is the only thing holding her back.
Emily Randall.follow_up: Email her staff a page on the people this ask helps, within two days, by email.
Emily Randall.personality: Randall stays very outgoing and she is very precise and thorough. Across her public talk, only a handful of issues come up, and her profile sits much lower than most members. Getting worked up comes much more readily to her than to most, and her speech carries an emotional charge that few match. She leans a little toward the practical, and her talk about the job is among the least careful in the House.
Emily Randall.speaks: Her pace runs a notch quick on the House floor, and her pauses come a touch short. Pitch sits much flatter than most, while the volume swings a bit more than most. Everything recorded of her is House floor speech, so read this as formal-setting delivery. In hearings she keeps a mild tone. Let each point land before you add the next.
Emily Randall.decides: Outside pressure counts for a great deal with her, more than with most House members, and her positions shift with it. Her profile is much lower than most members, so the case built on people has to do the work. In formal hearings she is one of the least combative House members. Ask which groups she hears from most, and check where they already stand on the ask.

archetype.justification: Somewhat skeptical, he gives brief answers and holds his ground under challenge more than most.

Eric Burlison.bottom_line: Lead with the outcome the policy delivers in a short, direct case. He moves less when outside pressure builds, so the facts have to carry it.
do: Lead with the outcome the policy delivers before any process
Keep your ask brief, since he answers in short replies
When he defends his position, ask for the specific source behind it
dont: Read his brief replies as a yes
Expect outside pressure to bring him around
Eric Burlison.warning_sign: He normally fills his replies with filler words, so an answer with almost none is the change to watch. It usually means he has settled on the point, so ask which result he needs to see.
Eric Burlison.follow_up: In writing, send him a short case with the outcome stated up front, and name who will confirm the next step.
Eric Burlison.personality: Burlison comes across quite reserved and somewhat skeptical, with a warm manner that stands out next to his flat delivery. Details sit loosely with him. His public talk covers a narrow range of issues, with less careful detail than most. His bills cover few issues, and he follows them through less reliably than colleagues. Short answers, plenty of filler, and a fairly visible profile mark his public style. He represents Missouri.
Eric Burlison.speaks: He speaks in short, quick runs of replies, and his longest answers stay brief. Filler and slightly longer breaks between phrases than most fill the gaps. His words come across as flat, with little focus on action, and with a little more feeling carried in them. In hearings he is far less combative than most, so his manner stays low key.
Eric Burlison.decides: How plainly a request shows what it delivers is what he weighs. Pressure from outside groups carries less weight for him, so the facts must do the persuading. Following bills through is much harder for him, so any decision must come with a named step to stick. In hearings his tone stays even, so hearing prep can stay focused on the facts.

archetype.justification: His wider issue range, looser detail, and reserved manner fit a wide ranging, loose member.

Eric Crawford.bottom_line: Send written, technical evidence early, since that framing suits him best. Outside lobbying carries less weight for him, so a clean, documented case wins.
do: Circulate the technical summary before the meeting
Keep the pace brisk, since he pauses only briefly between phrases
Ask for a clear next step with a named owner
dont: Read his even voice as a sign of agreement
Assume a bill will move on its own without follow up
Eric Crawford.warning_sign: A general meeting will not reveal where he stands on the procedural steps, so the answer lives in the bill's status. Before the meeting, confirm with staff which step is next and who owns it.
Eric Crawford.follow_up: Within two days, send his office the technical summary and the named owner for the next step.
Eric Crawford.personality: Crawford is a reserved member with a loose hand on details, and his public talk ranges across more topics than most. His description of his work is less exact than typical colleagues'. Legislation he sponsors covers a wider scope, yet bipartisan cooperation comes less readily than typical colleagues manage. Bills and votes get less follow through than typical, so a clear next step matters.
Eric Crawford.speaks: He covers more ground in a single answer than most, and his descriptions stay broad rather than exact. Talk spreads across several themes at once rather than narrowing to one. Descriptions of his work stay broad, with less exact detail than typical colleagues. Listeners get a dense run of points, each one touching a different area of policy. Each answer carries a wide frame, so the topics stack up quickly.
Eric Crawford.decides: Requests earn his support when they cleanly match the topics he already covers, and written technical proof carries them further with him. Outside voices have a modest effect on him, so a push from others does not settle things alone. He does not follow through on bills as reliably as most, so a dated next step with a named owner is what keeps a commitment in place.

archetype.justification: Among the most skeptical and least inclined to lead a room, with words sharper than nearly any colleague's and a looser grip on detail.

Eric Schmitt.bottom_line: Give him one short, specific ask he can test on his own terms. Outside voices move him a little more than most, so bring people who back it.
do: Lead with the one specific ask in the first minute
Answer his sharp questions with a concrete example, not a slogan
Expect a little more combativeness from him in hearings
dont: Pile on warmth or small talk before the ask
Assume his quiet means he has agreed
Eric Schmitt.warning_sign: He usually talks fast with an even tone and rarely pushes for the lead. When his volume starts to swing and his sentences trail off more than usual, he is irritated, so stop debating and ask one short, specific question.
Eric Schmitt.follow_up: Within two days of the meeting, send him a one page note restating the ask and the deadline.
Eric Schmitt.personality: Schmitt is somewhat reserved and a little less practical than most, and he ranks among the most skeptical members. Among the loosest members on specifics, he describes his own work in terms that are much less careful than most. Quick to flare, much more than most, he is still among the least emotional in public, so irritation shows in his sharpness rather than his tone. Sharper wording than nearly any colleague marks his public talk, and his words run much cooler than most. Taking charge of a room is something he does less than nearly anyone, and his range of topics is somewhat narrower than most.
Eric Schmitt.speaks: His delivery is much quicker than most, with pauses cut shorter than nearly anyone's and an even volume that rarely rises. Words come out flat and action focused, and he is less forceful than nearly anyone. He keeps to a somewhat narrower set of topics and goes into much less care for detail than most. Answers run long, and the longest ones stretch much longer than most, though their length varies less than nearly anyone's. In hearings he is a little more combative than most, and when he trails off, the sentence is left unfinished.
Eric Schmitt.decides: Whether an ask survives his doubt decides it for him, as he is among the most skeptical members. Outside voices move him a little more than most, so a case that arrives through people back home carries more weight than a push inside the room. His record at seeing bills through trails most members, so an ask from him sticks only with a written step behind it.

archetype.justification: His outgoing, curious manner and community focused talk fit an open, community minded operator who speaks for the people affected.

Eric Sorensen.bottom_line: Open with the people your ask reaches and the members on the other side who back it, since he cooperates with them more than almost anyone.
do: Share stories about who the policy helps
Give his slow replies room, since he speaks slowly
Name the cross party vote he can help deliver
dont: Take his long pauses as a sign the talk is over
Assume a hearing will stay friendly if he pushes
Eric Sorensen.warning_sign: He is usually slow with long pauses and a voice that rises and falls, so pauses are normal. If his pace quickens and his words turn sharp in a hearing, read it as guarded, so slow down, acknowledge the concern, and let him finish.
Eric Sorensen.follow_up: After the meeting mail him a brief note naming the cross party members and the vote you need, and ask for his answer in two days.
Eric Sorensen.personality: Sorensen is highly sociable and very curious, which makes him an eager conversationalist. Emotion comes through readily, since his public language carries much more charge than colleagues'. He builds ties across the aisle to a degree few colleagues match, and he is somewhat less dependable at following bills to a vote. Despite his sociable manner, his public profile stays quiet and his role draws little notice. He represents Illinois.
Eric Sorensen.speaks: Speech from him runs slower than nearly anyone in the chamber, with extended stretches between phrases and a voice that swells and drops more than nearly any colleague's. Descriptions of his work are a little less exact in detail than colleagues'. His public range of issues runs somewhat wider than colleagues'. Delivery samples come from House floor audio, a format different from interviews. In hearings he presses somewhat harder than colleagues.
Eric Sorensen.decides: Before a yes he asks who it helps, since the people affected carry the most weight in his framing. Colleagues across the aisle find him more willing than almost anyone, so a proposal that wins support from the other side tends to move him. Outside pressure moves him more than colleagues, so any choice must rest on a named next step.

archetype.justification: Quite reserved, among the most reliable at seeing bills through, and much slower in pace than most.

Erin Houchin.bottom_line: Bring a written, detailed brief and a single ask she can check against it. She ranks among the most dependable on bills, so a checked ask can carry.
do: Send the written brief ahead of the meeting
Confirm the owner and the date before she leaves
Take the ask to her office, since she is less visible on the floor
dont: Read her slow, careful pace as a sign she is holding back
Assume a broad, quick ask will win her over
Erin Houchin.warning_sign: In hearings she usually presses a point hard, by default. If she stops pressing and goes quiet, she is weighing the answer or losing interest. Give her the written point again and let her set the pace.
Erin Houchin.follow_up: Email her office a written recap by the second day, naming the owner and the date.
Erin Houchin.personality: Houchin reads as quite reserved yet a little practical, and her descriptions of her work are much more exact and specific than most. Her bills cover much wider ground than most, and at carrying them through she is more dependable than nearly any colleague in the chamber. She works across the lines much less than most, and she stays less visible than nearly any member in the House. In hearings she presses harder than most, which marks a member who holds her ground in formal settings.
Erin Houchin.speaks: Her pace is much slower than most, with pauses that run longer than most. Volume swings more than almost anyone's, and her pitch stays flatter than most. Her words carry a little less emotion than most, and her descriptions are careful and detailed. In hearings she presses harder than most. Her recorded delivery comes from the House floor, so compare it only with floor speech.
Erin Houchin.decides: Requests get weighed by how well the written case holds up on paper. Outside pressure registers less with her compared to most members, so pushes from beyond have a smaller effect. Her bills take up much more ground than most, so an ask can connect to several of them. At seeing bills through she is more dependable than almost any other House member, so a choice holds once an owner and a date are set.

archetype.justification: He reacts with a bit more heat than most, and his volume swings up and down more than most, which fits a protective style.

Eugene Vindman.bottom_line: Lead with the technical case in writing, and build the coalition across the aisle. Outside voices shift him more than most colleagues, so bring in voices he trusts.
do: Share the technical evidence before the meeting
Build support across the aisle first
Name a next step with a date, and keep your own volume even
dont: Assume his curious questions mean he has committed
Press him in a hearing for a yes on the spot
Eugene Vindman.warning_sign: Usually his phrasing runs a bit sharper than most, and his volume swings up and down more than most. If his pauses lengthen and his pitch flattens, he is weighing the ask or pulling back, so give him a written option.
Eugene Vindman.follow_up: After the meeting, send him the technical evidence with a dated next step and an owner, copied to his legislative director within two days.
Eugene Vindman.personality: Vindman is fairly curious, and he follows bills to the finish fairly well. Speech runs in careful detail, a little more than most, and his emotional tone sits a bit lower than most. His cross aisle work is among the highest in the House, and in hearings he runs somewhat less combative than most members. Together these traits make him a detail focused coalition builder who leads with written proof and builds support across the aisle.
Eugene Vindman.speaks: His pace runs a bit slower than most, with pauses that run much longer than most. Volume swings up and down more than most, and his pitch stays a little flatter than most. He describes his own work with somewhat more care and detail than most, and his phrasing carries a bit less emotion than most. In hearings he runs somewhat less combative than most members, so he keeps the exchange even.
Eugene Vindman.decides: Requests are judged by how closely they match his coalition work and how much proof backs them. Outside voices shift him more than most colleagues, so a coalition of trusted voices can tip him. His cross aisle work is strong, so a request built with colleagues from both sides fits him well. He follows bills through fairly well, so a commitment usually holds once made.

archetype.justification: He ranks near the bottom of the chamber for outward expression, is very careful, and speaks in precise detail.

Frank Lucas.bottom_line: Bring one ask in writing and let him study it before he decides. He follows through on what he commits to, so ask for a clear yes.
do: Ask him to name the staff member who tracks each bill
Open with a question about his bills, since he is fairly curious
In a hearing, bring precise questions, since he is far less confrontational there
dont: Count on bipartisan backing from him without asking for it
Mistake his reserve for a lack of interest in your bill
Frank Lucas.warning_sign: Normally he asks several questions, and in hearings he runs far less confrontational than most members. When his questions stop, he is losing interest, so restate the one ask and stop there.
Frank Lucas.follow_up: Send a short written memo listing each agreed step, its owner, and a due date.
Frank Lucas.personality: Lucas keeps a low outward profile, yet he is fairly curious and very careful with his work. He describes policy in exact detail, more precisely than most colleagues do. His bills take in much wider issues than typical, and he crosses party lines less often than most colleagues. Seeing bills to completion is a strength of his record, and his hearing manner is far less confrontational than usual.
Frank Lucas.speaks: He speaks in precise, detailed terms and sticks to specifics. He moves across a broader set of topics than most colleagues within a single discussion. In a hearing he is far less confrontational than most members, and he keeps the conversation factual. Careful detail is his default register, whatever the topic, and he moves between issues with the same precision.
Frank Lucas.decides: He weighs an ask against the many moving parts his bills already involve, since they span a wide spread of issues. He is fairly curious, so an unanswered question keeps him engaged. Unanswered questions keep his attention on a bill longer than most. His record of seeing bills to completion stands out, so a commitment from him holds once it is made.

archetype.justification: He leans reserved, thinks with real care, and few colleagues are less visible, which fits a patient, methodical pace.

Frank Mrvan.bottom_line: Lead with a shared role he can announce with others, and cite his reliable follow through. Outside voices shift him more than most colleagues, so a coalition carries weight.
do: Offer a shared role he can announce with others
Point to his record on carrying bills to final votes when you ask
Ask for a coalition of voices to join the ask
dont: Assume his reserve signals doubt about the ask
Rely on one sit down to settle the question
Frank Mrvan.warning_sign: A broad group session will not reveal how he handles follow up once staff change, and his careful style hides it. Ask his office who owns the file and when the next vote falls, then confirm that owner in writing.
Frank Mrvan.follow_up: Within two days, email him a written recap of the coalition and the agreed next step with its date, copied to his legislative director.
Frank Mrvan.personality: Mrvan leans reserved and thinks with real care in his own work. Working across the aisle ranks among the highest in the House, and bill follow through is among the most dependable. His account of his work is far more careful and detailed than nearly any colleague's, though few colleagues are less visible. Together these traits make him a quiet, dependable coalition builder who works through detail and keeps a low public profile.
Frank Mrvan.speaks: His account of his own work is detailed and careful, far more than nearly any colleague's. When he explains an issue, the point comes through specifics before any sweeping claim. Deliberate precision marks his manner, and the listener hears the particulars first. He keeps each claim tied to its support, so the detail arrives before the conclusion.
Frank Mrvan.decides: A request is tested on how well its details hold up and whether colleagues across the aisle share it. Outside voices shift him more than most colleagues, so a coalition of voices can change his answer. His follow through is among the most dependable, so a commitment from him holds once made. A request built on proof and shared sponsorship has the best path to his yes.

archetype.justification: Careful with details, reliable on votes, slow in speech, with long pauses between phrases.

Frank Pallone.bottom_line: Bring one clear ask and the record behind it, then give him time to decide. Pressure will not hurry him, so the case has to hold up on paper.
do: Put the full record in writing before the meeting
Give him quiet room to finish long points before you respond
Hold any ask to a clear vote he can take
dont: Read his long pauses as doubt about your ask
Count on upbeat small talk to carry the ask
Frank Pallone.warning_sign: His usual pattern is long pauses and plenty of filler. Watch for him wrapping up a point early and dropping filler, which usually means he has reached a view. Then stop, name the one choice before him, and give him time.
Frank Pallone.follow_up: Email a brief written account of the record behind your request, then invite him to confirm the vote he has in mind.
Frank Pallone.personality: Pallone explains his work with careful, detailed reasoning, and he is highly dependable on votes and in carrying bills to completion. In a conversation he tends to lead more than most, and his words come across as upbeat even on technical subjects. Those traits make him a dependable operator who wants the work done right. He follows through once he has committed, so his word carries weight.
Frank Pallone.speaks: He speaks slowly and pauses between phrases for longer stretches than almost anyone in the House, and his pitch stays flatter than most. Interview answers run briefer than most, and he fills gaps with more filler than the typical speaker. He describes his dealings with precise, detailed reasoning, so his manner is deliberate rather than quick. The gaps and filler come with careful, detailed talk, not with vagueness.
Frank Pallone.decides: How well the facts hold up is the test he applies before committing. Once he has backed a measure, he follows it to completion, so what he has committed to can be counted on. Pressure from the outside tends to change his mind less than it changes most members, so a push from outside will not carry the day. A decision with him sticks when it rests on facts he can check, so a documented case is what gets him to yes.

archetype.justification: Her curiosity runs far ahead of most colleagues, and her words carry an upbeat tone few in the chamber match.

Frederica Wilson.bottom_line: Lead with the people a bill would help, and keep the ask to one clear area. Outside pressure moves her less, so bring her own reasons.
do: Tell the stories of who a bill would help
Let her answer briefly and move on
Bring new angles, since she is very curious
Match her upbeat energy with a clear, short ask
dont: Count on her to drive a bill to the finish
Lean on dense technical detail to win her over
Frederica Wilson.warning_sign: Her usual pattern is brief, upbeat answers with an even flow and a lot of emotional charge in her words. When her answers run even shorter than usual, she is weighing the ask, so ask who it helps and let her describe that.
Frederica Wilson.follow_up: Put a short note in writing within a week that names who the change helps and the next step, with a date.
Frederica Wilson.personality: Wilson is somewhat outgoing and very curious, and her wording is among the most upbeat in the chamber. Worked up more readily than nearly anyone, she carries a great deal of emotional charge. Her own descriptions of her work lack precision more than nearly anyone's, and details get less of her attention. Her bills address far fewer issue areas than typical, and she is among the least dependable at seeing bills through.
Frederica Wilson.speaks: She gives short answers, and even her longest replies stay brief compared with nearly everyone. Answers stay even in length, and she does not often trail off or fall into quick bursts. Her word choice is upbeat and warm, and she is among the least action focused members in the chamber. In conversation she leads much less than most, so her turns tend to be brief and responsive.
Frederica Wilson.decides: She looks at who an ask helps and whether it stays in one area she can explain. Her bills span a narrow range, so an ask that sits inside her areas fits best. Follow through on her bills is weak, so a promise from her needs a date and a named owner. Outside pressure moves her far less than most members, so outside voices do not change her view much.

archetype.justification: His words are very focused on action in the House, and he reaches across the aisle far less than most.

French Hill.bottom_line: Open with the results the policy yields, and keep the request to one clear step. He is very reliable on bills, so a dated next step is worth asking for.
do: Bring the outcome figures and the bill text, so he can check the policy's effect
Open with the action the bill would take, stated in plain verbs
Put your most important question first, since his replies come in quick runs
Close by naming the next vote on the bill and when it falls
dont: Claim cross-party backing his record does not show
Let one no close it, as pressure sways him only a little less than most
Bring a hearing-style challenge into a formal session
French Hill.warning_sign: He usually replies in brisk bursts, one after another. If he stretches a reply into one long answer, the point has run out of room for now. Set the point aside, and come back to it in a later meeting.
French Hill.follow_up: Send his legislative staff a list of open questions within two days, with each item's status.
French Hill.personality: Hill brings a very curious streak to his work, and few members talk about a wider set of issues than he does. He is agreeable and easy to work with, yet he works across party lines much less than most. He is very reliable on bills and votes, and his words are warm. Careful and exact about his work in public, he is much more so than most, yet his interview answers run brisk. His words are one of the most action-focused in the House. He is hard to fluster, and in hearings he is much more combative than most. Visibility is fairly high for his role.
French Hill.speaks: In interviews his replies come in much shorter pieces than most. Even his longest ones stay brief. His pace is slow, and his volume and pitch stay more even than most. Brisk bursts of replies are how he moves through a conversation. Keep your questions simple, and let him set the rhythm of the exchange. Expect quick, short replies, one after another.
French Hill.decides: Outside voices sway him only a little less than most. His follow-through on bills means a yes from him carries weight, since he sees bills through to votes. He builds across party lines far less than most, so name the other-party bills he has joined when you ask for his vote. Close by asking what he needs to see before he commits to a vote.

archetype.justification: He trails off in conversation more than almost anyone in the House, and his public language leans much more social than most.

Gabe Amo.bottom_line: Lead with the families your plan helps, and ask one clear question at a time.
do: Bring a short case that centers on the families the plan would reach
Keep each question short so he has a clean end point
Let the social give-and-take run before you narrow to the ask
Start with a bill he has already carried, then ask for the next one
dont: Read his mild word choice as indifference to the people you describe
Wait for a long answer to arrive, since his answers stay even in length
Take an unfinished reply as his final word and move on
Gabe Amo.warning_sign: He usually lets others hold the floor, and he rarely takes charge of a conversation. If he suddenly takes over and runs the room, stop, ask one question, and wait.
Gabe Amo.follow_up: Within two days, send his office a clean page listing each step and its owner.
Gabe Amo.personality: Amo has very strong follow-through on bills and votes, and he reaches across to the other party a bit more than most. Detail work does not come easily to him, and few members hold a conversation less firmly than he does. He is a sociable speaker, far more so than most, and he takes more to rattle than most members do. Few members are less combative in hearings than he is.
Gabe Amo.speaks: Mostly on the House floor, he is quicker in speech than most, and pauses between phrases run longer. His pitch moves a great deal, and his volume rises and falls a little more than most. In interviews he trails off more than almost anyone in the House. Filler words are rare for him. His answer lengths stay even, so a question with several parts gets one even reply. Give him space to finish a thought.
Gabe Amo.decides: A plan that names the people it reaches is the case that fits him, and he reaches across to the other party a bit more than most. Bills with backing from both sides match how he works. His bill and vote follow-through is very strong. Keep the ask short, and end by naming the one commitment you want, in plain words.

archetype.justification: His detailed, careful talk, narrow issue range and very reliable follow through fit the Ox.

Gabe Evans.bottom_line: Bring a precise written case built on results, since he follows through. Outside voices sway him more than most, so his view turns on the record.
do: Lead with the written case and its results
Leave room between points, since he talks fast and pauses briefly
dont: Mistake his reserve for disinterest in your ask
Assume a low public profile means he lacks sway on the issue
Gabe Evans.warning_sign: A casual session will not reveal how he copes with a procedural snag or a missed deadline. Raise the process question early, then confirm the agreed timeline in writing.
Gabe Evans.follow_up: Send his office a written note of the agreed timeline and the staffer who owns the next step, by the date set.
Gabe Evans.personality: Evans stays quite reticent, and his attention remains narrow rather than broad. Careful and organized, he describes his work in exact, detailed terms that few colleagues match. His bills touch a far smaller set of topics than most, though he follows them through very reliably. His public visibility sits near the bottom for someone in his post, so his influence comes through quiet, careful work.
Gabe Evans.speaks: He speaks in narrow, precise terms and goes into careful detail on his work. His talk stays on the matter at hand and seldom widens into broader themes. Results and facts carry his case better than sweeping claims. In exchanges he sticks to the facts of the bill rather than the wider debate. He prefers written proof to broad claims about the bill.
Gabe Evans.decides: He weighs an ask by results and by whether it fits the narrow set of issues he already follows. Commitments he makes tend to hold, since he is very dependable on legislation. Outside sway reaches him further than most colleagues, so the request must rest on facts he can verify. So a decision from him needs a clear result he can point to.

archetype.justification: Stories about the people a bill helps and wide work across party lines fit a Hummingbird's style.

Gabe Vasquez.bottom_line: Lead with who the plan helps, then ask for one specific step and set a date for the next check in.
do: Open with one real example of who gains
Keep your pace brisk and set a date for the next check in
dont: Treat his outgoing manner as proof he will commit early
Gabe Vasquez.warning_sign: By default he speaks briskly and holds his ground in a hearing. If his manner sharpens in a hearing, he is losing patience or feels pressed. Slow down, restate the one ask, and let him answer.
Gabe Vasquez.follow_up: Within a day of the meeting, send him a short written outline of the ask with the agreed date for the next check in.
Gabe Vasquez.personality: Vasquez is detailed and deliberate about his work, speaking in careful terms rather than emotional ones. He is less easily rattled than most, and he reaches across the aisle far more than most. Bills he sponsors touch fewer subject areas than most, and follow through on them runs a little weaker than most. Among his peers his public profile sits lower than the typical member.
Gabe Vasquez.speaks: Speech comes at a brisk pace, with pauses between phrases and pitch that swings widely. His framing of issues is exact and specific, with little emotional heat in his public words. His answers cover a narrow set of subject areas, and his manner stays on substance rather than feeling. In formal hearings he tends to be more combative than colleagues.
Gabe Vasquez.decides: Who an ask helps shapes his view, and concrete stories about real residents move him more than abstract figures do. Pressure from outside shifts him more than it shifts most colleagues. His follow through is less reliable than most, so a yes can fade when no step is visible. A yes sticks only once the next step has a name and a firm date.

archetype.justification: Very practical, much looser with details, and his bills reach somewhat fewer issues, so his focus stays narrow.

Gary Palmer.bottom_line: Send written technical evidence before the meeting, since he takes a practical view and pressure moves him much more than most.
do: Test the practical effect with him before you state a conclusion
If he presses hard in a hearing, answer with facts and keep your tone even
dont: Take his short answers as the end of the discussion
Open with warm small talk, since his words are among the coolest in the House
Gary Palmer.warning_sign: By default he talks faster than nearly any member, with pauses among the shortest. If he slows down and leaves longer gaps, he is weighing the point rather than dismissing it, so stop talking and let him reach his view.
Gary Palmer.follow_up: Put the technical summary in writing for his office by day two, naming the one open question and who answers it.
Gary Palmer.personality: Palmer counts among the most reserved members in the House, and is quite practical and much looser with detail than most. He is very skeptical, and he is somewhat quicker than most to get worked up. His words are cool and not very social, so his manner reads as blunt. In hearings he pushes back much harder than colleagues do, and his bills reach somewhat fewer issues. He represents Alabama.
Gary Palmer.speaks: He talks among the fastest members, and his pitch swings more widely than nearly anyone's. Volume swings somewhat wider than most. Brief bursts of short replies mark his answers far more than most, and his longest replies are far briefer than most. In delivery his pace stays brisk, and his tone carries little warmth. Hearings bring out much more combativeness in him than in most colleagues.
Gary Palmer.decides: He weighs an ask on its practical effect, and written, technical evidence fits him best. Outside pressure moves him much more than most members, so pressure can shift his view quickly. His skepticism means the first case he hears still matters. His bills reach somewhat fewer issues, so he tends to decide within his existing areas, and a yes holds only as firm as its next step.

archetype.justification: He takes a little more charge of conversations than most, gives among the longest answers, and speaks with nearly the most force in the Senate.

Gary Peters.bottom_line: Lead with what the policy delivers in a short, direct case. Outside pressure moves him less than nearly any colleague, so the facts must carry it.
do: Point to bills he has carried to passage and those he joined across the aisle
Ask which result would count as success, then show how the bill delivers it
Let him finish each long answer before you raise the next point
dont: Count on outside pressure to change his position
Match his forceful wording with heavier language of your own
Rely on warm pleasantries to carry the meeting
Gary Peters.warning_sign: He usually keeps the floor and pushes the conversation forward. When he starts yielding the floor and his pauses grow, he is guarded or losing interest. Name the one result you still need and ask him directly if it works.
Gary Peters.follow_up: Within a week of the meeting, mail his staff a single page summing up the results the bill would deliver.
Gary Peters.personality: Peters is reserved by temperament, yet once he is talking he takes charge of the conversation and keeps the floor. He is careful, organized and a bit harder to rattle than most, and his public talk covers a wider set of issues than most colleagues. He works across the other party far more than most, and he follows bills through more reliably than nearly anyone in the Senate. A longtime member from Michigan, his manner runs a little cool, so substance counts for more with him than rapport.
Gary Peters.speaks: He talks in long, careful answers and moves across a wide range of issues. His wording is forceful, among the strongest in the Senate. Filler is much rarer in his speech than in most colleagues'. Pauses between phrases run among the shortest in the chamber, his volume holds even, and his pitch rises and falls a little more than most. His longest replies stretch well past what most colleagues offer.
Gary Peters.decides: He weighs an ask by what it delivers, so a case built on results gets his attention first. Outside pressure moves him less than nearly any colleague, so a campaign of calls rarely settles his view. A joint sponsor from the other side counts for a lot with him. Because he follows bills through so reliably, a yes from him tends to be carried all the way.

archetype.justification: Fairly outgoing and curious, focused on who is helped, and easily stirred in discussion.

George Latimer.bottom_line: Lead with who the ask helps, since that framing fits him and outside groups have a bit less pull on him than most members.
do: Bring named people the ask would help to back it up
Plan for a much less combative manner from him than from colleagues
dont: Count on a heated fight in a hearing, since he is much less combative
Rely on outside groups to reshape his view, since they have less pull on him
George Latimer.warning_sign: Usually he keeps formal settings low-key. If he turns combative in a hearing, read it as guardedness, so take it slow and name the specific people the ask would help.
George Latimer.follow_up: Send him a short note by Friday with the shared next step, naming who will report back on it.
George Latimer.personality: Latimer reads as fairly outgoing and fairly curious, and he tends to lead with people. His words sound plain rather than heated. In hearings he stays low-key, more than colleagues do, and he is easily stirred in discussion. His manner in conversation stays open, and he tends to build on what others say. He values concrete results for the people he serves.
George Latimer.speaks: He pauses somewhat longer between phrases than most, and loudness shifts much more than most across sentences. Words sound plain rather than heated, so the delivery reads as plain. His talk ranges across issues somewhat wider than most. During hearings a restrained tone shows, so questions stay on the substance. He keeps a conversational pace and tends to build on what others say.
George Latimer.decides: A request earns his support when it gives people a concrete stake, which suits how he frames issues. Outside groups have a bit less pull on him than most members, so a push from outside groups struggles to reshape his view. Because he is much less combative in formal settings, a plain case works better than a fight, so his support holds when the people it helps are named.

archetype.justification: His practical focus and narrow range of issues set him apart, along with a very outgoing manner and a fast, varied delivery.

George Whitesides.bottom_line: Keep the case practical and short, since you need a clear next step more than applause. Do not count a warm reception as a commitment.
do: Bring a practical example of how the plan would work day to day
Open with your one main point, stated in a single sentence
Offer outside voices who back the plan, since they carry extra weight with him
Close by naming one community the plan already helps
dont: Assume colleagues already know where he stands on the plan
Settle for a one-time favor when the plan needs a bill he sees through
Wait until outside pressure has moved him before you make the ask
George Whitesides.warning_sign: A lively meeting does not show whether he has weighed your ask. Ask him to name the one point he still weighs, then wait for his answer.
George Whitesides.follow_up: Within a day, email his legislative staff a short page of notes on the plan and its next action, in writing.
George Whitesides.personality: Whitesides has a strongly outgoing manner, balanced by a fairly careful, practical streak. New ideas hold less pull for him than most. His public language covers one of the narrowest ranges of issues in the House. His bills reach a few fewer issues than most, but he is fairly dependable at seeing them through. Visibility runs much lower than most, and just as low for his role.
George Whitesides.speaks: When he speaks on the House floor, he moves much faster than most, with somewhat shorter pauses between phrases. His volume swings a lot, and his pitch swings a little more than most as well. His words carry one of the lowest levels of emotional charge in the House. These are floor patterns, so read them as delivery, not as meeting pace. Keep your own points short so they are not lost.
George Whitesides.decides: Outside voices sway him more than most, so have an outside backer put the case to his office in writing, not only in the room. A written case that names the vote and its result gives his staff something to file. Once he agrees, he sees bills through fairly dependably, so keep the next vote on his calendar before the meeting ends. Then ask his staff to confirm that date.

archetype.justification: Somewhat outgoing and community focused, he speaks somewhat faster than most, and his language carries somewhat more feeling.

Gilbert Cisneros.bottom_line: Lead with the people a bill helps, then ask for one clear step. He moves more under outside pressure, so an ask with local backing carries weight.
do: Tell the story of who a bill helps, in plain terms
Match his brisk pace and keep answers tight
Let him talk through the community angle, since he is somewhat outgoing
In a hearing, expect questions that are somewhat more combative than most
dont: Treat his outgoing style as agreement with the ask
Gilbert Cisneros.warning_sign: In hearings he is normally at a somewhat higher level of combat than most, so a softer, plainer reply is a change. If he turns sharp, slow down, ask what the concern is, and give him room to finish.
Gilbert Cisneros.follow_up: By Friday, email him a single page covering the story, the ask and the next step.
Gilbert Cisneros.personality: Cisneros is somewhat outgoing and somewhat careful, and he is somewhat less easily rattled than most. His language runs somewhat warmer in feeling than most, and his talk spans somewhat more topics than most. He describes his work with somewhat more careful detail than most. Bills from him reach somewhat fewer issue areas than most, but he sees bills through somewhat more reliably than most. Public attention finds him somewhat less often than most colleagues. Hearings draw somewhat more combat from him than most colleagues. He represents a California district and sits on the House Small Business panel.
Gilbert Cisneros.speaks: He moves through his points somewhat quicker than most, and his breaks between phrases are shorter. His pitch barely rises and falls, less than almost anyone's. Volume varies somewhat less than most. When he discusses bills his terms run somewhat more exact than most. His remarks cover a wider mix of topics, and his words carry more feeling. In hearings he turns somewhat more combative than most colleagues.
Gilbert Cisneros.decides: Asks get a hearing when they show a clear community benefit, and stories about real people move him. His legislation sits in fewer issue areas than most, so an ask inside his lane fits. Pressure from outside reaches him more than most members, so local supporters can shift his view. Being somewhat outgoing, he responds to people who bring the story to him, so a decision holds when residents are part of it.

archetype.justification: His bills span wide ground, he is much less dependable on votes and bills, and details run loose.

Glenn Grothman.bottom_line: Name the next step before you leave, since seeing bills through is much less dependable for him than for most.
do: Send a written technical memo ahead, with the ask stated in one line
Ask him direct questions, since he takes charge of the talk much less than most
Answer his sharp words with a plain, even reply
Close by reading the next step back aloud, since follow-through is much weaker for him
dont: Fill the gaps between his quick replies with your own points
Keep coming back to this request once he has refused it
Dress the ask in upbeat words, since his phrasing runs much flatter than most
Glenn Grothman.warning_sign: His public words are usually sharper than nearly any colleague's. If they get sharper still and he stops engaging the point, it has lost his attention. Narrow to the one question he must answer, and hold your other points.
Glenn Grothman.follow_up: Give his office a written note within two days, with the owner and due day for the next step.
Glenn Grothman.personality: Grothman is skeptical to a degree few colleagues match. He is quite practical, and details run loose for him, much more than most House members. His bills span wide ground, more than nearly anyone's. On bills and votes, the record sits much lower than most. He runs hot far more readily than most House members. His public words are sharper than nearly any colleague's.
Glenn Grothman.speaks: His wording carries much less force than most. His interview answers come in shorter than almost anyone else in the House. Replies often come in fast clusters of brief lines, much more than most. In floor speeches his pitch holds flatter than most members do, and gaps between his phrases stretch somewhat longer than most. Keep your reply plain and short, and let his brief runs finish.
Glenn Grothman.decides: He has spoken about drinking whole milk at school lunch as a child, a story you can use as common ground where it honestly fits. Pressure from outside groups moves him slightly less than most members, which means the case must stand alone. His follow-through is weak, so treat any yes from him as provisional until the bill moves. When he raises a doubt, reply point by point from the paper you already shared.

archetype.justification: Among the least inclined to take charge of talk, and very reliable at seeing bills through.

Glenn Ivey.bottom_line: Make the case thoroughly and let him finish, since he gives long answers and outside pressure moves him much less than most members.
do: Bring the bill's record and timeline, since he is very reliable at seeing bills through
Let him speak at length without cutting in, since his answers run long
Expect him to be among the most combative members in hearings
dont: Read his fast pace as impatience, since his delivery runs quick overall
Count on him to lead the room, since he is inclined to defer
Glenn Ivey.warning_sign: Usually he talks fast, with a lot of filler and quick bursts of replies, so a shift is the cue. If his pitch flattens and he stops rushing his replies, he is weighing your case, so let him finish before you answer.
Glenn Ivey.follow_up: Send him a brief written recap by Friday, with the record and a named owner for each next step.
Glenn Ivey.personality: Ivey is very reliable at seeing bills through. He is among the least inclined to lead discussions, and his answers run long. His tone runs warmer than colleagues do. In hearings he ranks with the most combative members, and he sticks with a bill once he commits to it. He keeps his points connected from one turn to the next, so the thread holds. His manner in conversation is open.
Glenn Ivey.speaks: He speaks very fast, among the fastest in the chamber, and his pauses between phrases run somewhat shorter than most. Volume shifts far more than most, and pitch swings widely for him. Trailing off comes a little more often than most. His answers stay long even when he is pressed, and he keeps his replies moving. In a hearing he is among the most combative members.
Glenn Ivey.decides: He checks whether the record is complete and whether the next step is clear. Outside pressure moves him much less than most members, so a campaign from outside groups does not easily change his view. His bills span a few issues, so a request aimed at his core areas fits best. Because he is very reliable at seeing bills through, his yes holds once the work is followed closely.

archetype.justification: A little practical in outlook, and his bills touch somewhat fewer areas than most.

Glenn Thompson.bottom_line: Keep the ask to one clear next step, since he leans practical and sees bills through more than most.
do: Map the plan onto the specific bills it would change, not broad goals
Ask outside groups to weigh in, since outside pressure moves his positions more than most
Keep the ask out of the press, and work it through his office
Close by naming the one bill you want him to see through first
dont: Shelve the request after a first no
Treat his yes as soft, because he sees bills through more than most
Save the ask for the last session before a long recess
Glenn Thompson.warning_sign: A meeting without a clear agenda does not show where he stands on the ask. Test one point in a short follow-up, and ask his staff what he needs to see.
Glenn Thompson.follow_up: Send his staff a brief memo with one next step, an owner, and a date within a few days.
Glenn Thompson.personality: Thompson is much less easily flustered than most, and his manner is quite reserved. He keeps a practical focus, and he prefers familiar ground more than most. On the work itself, his public words are much more exact than most. The bills he carries touch a somewhat narrower set of areas. For his role, he is among the least seen members in the House. Follow-through is fairly reliable, since he sees bills through more than most.
Glenn Thompson.speaks: In his public clips his pace runs far quicker than most, and his pauses run shorter than almost anyone's. His volume barely varies, while his pitch swings more widely than nearly any colleague's. He almost never leaves long pauses, so there is almost no room between his points. Plan your turns in advance, since gaps are short, and keep your own points brief. Match his pace only where it helps you hold the room.
Glenn Thompson.decides: Outside voices sway his positions more than most members, so note which groups already reach his office before you plan the ask. His bill follow-through is more dependable than most. Name a bill he has already seen through, so the ask builds on that record. Before you leave, agree on a check-in date with him, because his follow-through makes one worth setting. End by asking which step he would take first, and when.

archetype.justification: Her gentle words, somewhat higher visibility and fit for shared announcements earn the Orca label.

Grace Meng.bottom_line: Offer her a shared public role and a clear ask, put gently. Pressure reaches her somewhat less than most, so partnership carries the weight.
do: Offer a joint announcement or event she can host with you
Keep requests gentle, specific and written in plain language
Let her set the pace and ask questions at her own speed
dont: Assume a verbal yes will survive to the vote
Press her for an answer on the spot in front of others
Grace Meng.warning_sign: Usually she is gentle and somewhat reserved, so her tone is a weak guide to her view. When her words turn sharp or she goes quiet, she feels pushed. Stop pressing, shorten the ask, and offer a written option she can review alone.
Grace Meng.follow_up: Following the meeting, give her a concise written recap naming the one next step and its date, copied to her legislative director.
Grace Meng.personality: Meng is an agreeable, careful and well organized member who keeps a reserved manner. She is somewhat hard to rattle, and she speaks about her issues more broadly than most. Broad strokes describe her own work, while her words are gentle yet carry a strong charge. She works across the aisle less than most. Follow through is among the weakest in the chamber, so she is better as a visible partner than as a closer.
Grace Meng.speaks: She speaks in a gentle, orderly way and frames issues across a fairly wide range. Her words carry strong emotional charge, yet her tone stays soft. Work gets described in broad strokes rather than close detail. In formal hearings she ranks among the least combative of members, and she steers clear of confrontation. Her manner stays civil even when she disagrees.
Grace Meng.decides: How well an ask fits a public partnership matters to her, since a shared announcement suits her. Pressure reaches her somewhat less than most, so pushing harder gets less. She is agreeable in manner but works across the aisle less than most. Her follow through lags, so her support holds only when a named next step is kept after the meeting.

archetype.justification: Very outgoing and quite skeptical, loose with details, and very combative in hearings.

Greg Casar.bottom_line: Keep the ask to one clear result and put it in writing, since he is among the least reliable at seeing bills through.
do: Put the policy facts on one page before the meeting
Track the bill's remaining steps on a dated list
In a hearing, expect combative questions and stay on the facts
Make your case on the merits, since he is quite skeptical
dont: Mistake his lively delivery for hostility
Stage a long hearing confrontation over a minor detail
Greg Casar.warning_sign: He usually talks loosely with a lively manner. In hearings, when he drifts from the detail and stops pressing, he is losing interest, so pin down the one result you need before you leave.
Greg Casar.follow_up: Email him a single page recapping the outcome, with dated steps and owners, the same day.
Greg Casar.personality: Casar presents as very outgoing and fairly curious, but quite skeptical and quick to flare up far more readily than most. He gives details far more loosely than most, and his bills take in far fewer issues than most. Ranking among the least dependable members on votes and follow through, he brings energy that often runs ahead of the facts. He is a Texas voice whose enthusiasm outruns his follow through.
Greg Casar.speaks: He talks fairly fast, with pitch that swings up and down far more than typical, and he speaks in broad strokes. A narrow set of issues fills his talk, and he stays with broad points rather than detail. In hearings he is very combative, pressing a point hard and returning to it. His delivery is quick and animated, with less of the detail that would let a listener check each claim.
Greg Casar.decides: Whether a request delivers a clear result is how he gauges it, and loose cases meet quite a skeptical reception. Outside appeals weigh less with him, so home groups rarely change his vote alone. In hearings he is combative and tests each claim. Since he is among the least reliable at seeing bills through, the next step needs an owner before he will move.

archetype.justification: Very agreeable, he works across the aisle more than most and speaks in a narrow range of issues.

Greg Landsman.bottom_line: Bring a concrete outcome and the coalition behind it, then leave with a written next step. Pressure from outside the room moves him more than most, so backing matters.
do: Keep the ask specific and short, since he gives brief answers
Bring a partner from the other side who shares the ask
If he trails off, let the sentence finish and ask him to continue
Offer a public moment he can share, since he is fairly visible
dont: Assume a friendly exchange secures the ask
Fill his pauses with more reasons while he is thinking
Greg Landsman.warning_sign: He normally trails off and answers in quick runs, so a run of finished, full answers is the change to watch. It usually means he is weighing the ask or getting impatient, so pause and ask which point needs settling.
Greg Landsman.follow_up: Shortly after you finish, mail him a written recap and copy the colleague across the aisle who backs the request.
Greg Landsman.personality: Landsman reads as rather sociable and counts among the most amiable colleagues, with a light practical streak. Public talk stays tightly focused, and his gentle phrasing comes across a bit flatter and cooler than most. He works across the aisle more than most, and he keeps a fairly visible profile for his role. Rapid replies in brief bursts, trailing off, and a heavy load of filler mark how he talks. He represents Ohio, and his public manner runs toward partnership rather than confrontation.
Greg Landsman.speaks: He talks about a narrow range of issues in gentle wording, and his words carry less force than most. Answers arrive in rapid bursts of brief replies, and his answer length swings more than most. He trails off, fills his sentences with filler, and leaves longer pauses than nearly anyone. In hearings he runs a touch more combative than most. Filler and pauses fill the gaps between his phrases.
Greg Landsman.decides: Whether the opposing side already supports it matters most to him, and he shifts more under outside push than when the case stands alone. Outside influence stirs him more often than most, so a request with endorsements earns a hearing. He answers in clipped bursts and trails off, so keep the ask short and let him finish his thought. Choices hold only when someone is named for the next action, and his partners' names should be attached.

archetype.justification: Gentle in public tone and wide in issue reach, and framing built on people fits him best.

Greg Stanton.bottom_line: Lead with the people your ask would help, then ask for one clear step, since outside pressure moves him more than most.
do: Bring one constituent story the policy would help, told briefly
Name the groups already backing the ask, since outside voices move him clearly
In a hearing, expect firmer questions, even though his tone stays gentle
dont: Read his gentle public tone as agreement with the ask
Take his animated delivery as proof of firm agreement
Greg Stanton.warning_sign: By default his public tone runs gentle, with few sharp edges. If he turns sharp and presses your figures, read it as guarded, so slow down and answer the one point he is challenging.
Greg Stanton.follow_up: Mail his office a short recap with the one ask and a date for his answer, within two days.
Greg Stanton.personality: Stanton is quite reserved but very agreeable, and his public talk covers issues much more widely than most. He is quick to flare up, far more than most, and his public words run much gentler than most colleagues. Bills he works on tend to get carried through, which gives his agreements some weight. In hearings he turns a bit sharper than most, which sets him apart from his usual tone.
Greg Stanton.speaks: He speaks fast, with a varied pitch that swings more than most, and his voice swings more widely than nearly any colleague's. His public words are gentle and wide in reach, and they carry strong feeling. In hearings he turns a bit sharper than most members, so expect firmer questions there. Even on hard topics his tone stays gentle, and in meetings he moves across many topics rather than staying on one line.
Greg Stanton.decides: Prior to committing, he gauges who it helps and whether outside voices stand behind it. Pressure from home carries real weight with him, more so than for most colleagues. Follow through on bills is fairly dependable, so an agreed step tends to hold. A decision holds only with a named next step, a date, and someone at home who will check on it.

archetype.justification: Among the most combative in hearings, among the longest interview answers, and somewhat less work across the aisle than most.

Gregory Meeks.bottom_line: Give him a firm, sourced case and let him take the floor. Challenges draw a defense from him, so expect pushback rather than quick agreement.
do: Bring a detailed case, since he follows bills closely
Let him finish his answers before you respond
In a hearing, expect sharp pushback and answer the point
Name the immediate step and who owns it before leaving
dont: Cut off a long answer before he reaches his main point
Assume quick agreement will come from a single meeting
Gregory Meeks.warning_sign: His usual pattern is wordy answers with heavy filler, by default. If the filler drops out and he goes flat and brief, he is closing off or on guard. Stop challenging, let him finish, and return to the record later.
Gregory Meeks.follow_up: Within two days, mail his office a brief written note of the commitment that names the step ahead.
Gregory Meeks.personality: Meeks ranks with the most dependable members at seeing bills through, and with the most visible for his role. His public words carry a great deal of emotional charge, while his answers run long and often trail into filler. He steers talk somewhat more than most, and pushes back when challenged. Hearings find him ranked among the most combative, a style that fits how he runs his own course.
Gregory Meeks.speaks: Talk runs long for him, with lengthy gaps between phrases and loudness that swings more than almost anyone's. Strong emotional charge runs through his words, and his manner is somewhat cooler and flatter than most. He frames issues in careful, detailed terms across a somewhat wider range than most. Hearings bring out his combative side. Filler is common, and he often trails off before he finishes.
Gregory Meeks.decides: Detail behind an ask is what he weighs first, and whether it holds up under challenge. He will hold a position under pushback, so a weak ask gets defended rather than dropped. Across his bills he touches a few more topics than most, so an ask can fit several areas he already works in. He follows bills through closely, so a commitment with a named next step tends to hold.

archetype.justification: His much sharper wording and high emotional charge fit a sharp tongued, combative style.

Gregory Murphy.bottom_line: Keep the ask short and tied to the bill, since his words run sharp under heat. He rarely sees bills through, so note the next step before you leave.
do: Lead with the concrete results of the bill, not the dispute
Name a colleague who would share the stage with him
dont: Match his sharp tone with sharper words of your own
Count on a plain ask alone to hold once he has moved on
Gregory Murphy.warning_sign: He usually keeps his words sharp and pushes his point. If the edge suddenly drops away, something has changed for him, so ask what before you go on.
Gregory Murphy.follow_up: Send him a short written note that restates the one ask and the date you agreed, within two days.
Gregory Murphy.personality: Murphy is a fairly agreeable member who gets worked up easily and is much more emotionally charged in his public words than most colleagues. His public talk runs much sharper than most, and his tone turns pointed under heat. Covering far fewer issues than most, he concentrates on a short list of causes. He is among the least reliable at seeing bills through, and his talk about work is less detailed than nearly any colleague's.
Gregory Murphy.speaks: His pace runs a bit quicker than most, with shorter pauses between phrases. His volume holds level, more consistently than nearly any colleague. Sharpness runs through his answers, more than most colleagues show. Emotion comes through strongly, with much more charge in his words than most. He covers fewer issues than most in each conversation, and he talks about his own work in less detail than nearly any colleague.
Gregory Murphy.decides: He takes on an ask most readily when a colleague shares the stage with him. Calls from the public sway him more than almost any member, so a repeated request gains force. He is among the least reliable at seeing bills through, so a decision needs more than a verbal yes. A choice stands firm for him once the next action appears in writing and a colleague is named.

archetype.justification: His bills span a bit more ground than most, but his record on finishing bills trails most colleagues, and detail work is not his strength.

Gregory Steube.bottom_line: Send written technical evidence ahead of the meeting, and set one dated next step. Outside calls count a bit less with him, so let the written case carry it.
do: Send written technical evidence well before the meeting
Point him to the one page of evidence that matters most
Keep any hearing-room version of your case formal and plain
Close by reading back any commitment he made, in his own words
dont: Treat a smaller shift under outside pressure as a firm refusal
Lead with results or people stories, since neither frame fits him
Pitch the plan as a sweeping vision, not a list of working steps
Gregory Steube.warning_sign: In formal hearings he is usually somewhat less combative than most. If he starts pressing hard on one point, he is treating that issue as a fight. Ask which point he means to settle, and let him name it.
Gregory Steube.follow_up: By Thursday, email his office a written reply to each open question, with an owner and a date listed for each.
Gregory Steube.personality: Steube is practical to a degree few House colleagues match, and he gets worked up quickly, more than most. Detail work runs much looser for him than for most colleagues. Somewhat fewer issues than most come up in his public talk, while his bills span a bit more ground. He trails most colleagues by a wide margin at casting votes and finishing bills. He is somewhat reserved, and under questioning in hearings he runs a bit milder than colleagues.
Gregory Steube.speaks: In hearings he leans a little less hard on a point than colleagues do. His public words range across fewer issues than most, and the detail he gives on his own work is somewhat thinner. His public words carry a bit less heat, too, so a plain tone suits the room. Keep your remarks concrete, and say each point once, in plain words.
Gregory Steube.decides: He trails most colleagues in the House at finishing bills, so tie the ask to one of his existing bills rather than a brand-new proposal. Before the meeting, check where that bill stands and which vote or hearing comes next. If it has stalled, find out what is holding the bill up and bring that answer to the meeting with you.

archetype.justification: His slow, careful pace and very reserved manner fit a deliberate, low key style.

Gus Bilirakis.bottom_line: Bring the community impact in writing, with the specifics laid out. Bridging the aisle is more natural for him than almost anyone, so a joint bill is a strong opening.
do: Give him room to finish, since his pauses run much longer between phrases
Bring the community impact in a written summary before the meeting
Send the next step to him afterward, so he can answer in his own time
dont: Rush him into a yes before he has worked through the details
Gus Bilirakis.warning_sign: He usually keeps a low key manner in ordinary meetings. In a hearing, if he suddenly turns sharp and presses his point, he has turned tense, so slow down and ask what concerns him.
Gus Bilirakis.follow_up: Send him a written summary of the step, its owner and its date within two days.
Gus Bilirakis.personality: Bilirakis is a reserved member who is quite practical and bridges the aisle more than almost anyone. The talk about the work itself is more precise than nearly any colleague's. Bills usually reach a finish, and he joins bills with the other party often. He represents a Florida seat in the House. Public talk stays close to the issues he already carries.
Gus Bilirakis.speaks: His pace runs slower than almost any colleague in the House, with much longer pauses between phrases. Volume swings more than nearly any colleague does, and pitch shifts somewhat more than most members do. In hearings he shows somewhat more combativeness than most members. His talk about the work is more careful than most, and he stays close to his issues. Pauses are a feature of how he talks, not a sign of hesitation.
Gus Bilirakis.decides: An ask is judged on whether it serves community needs within the bills he already carries. Bills that work across the aisle carry more weight with him, since he joins them often. He is fairly reliable on roll calls, so a plan with a written step tends to hold. Progress lands with him once the next step is in writing and its owner is clear.

archetype.justification: His skepticism runs deep, and his manner in hearings is far more combative than most.

Guy Reschenthaler.bottom_line: Put the ask in writing and settle the timing before you leave. Outside pressure has less effect on him than most, so the paper case has to do the work.
do: Set a clear deadline and send it with the ask
Check each agreed step with his office within the week
In a hearing, expect sharp questions and answer each one plainly
dont: Rely on outside pressure to carry the vote
Assume his hearing manner signals the final answer
Guy Reschenthaler.warning_sign: He usually presses a point hard in a hearing and keeps returning to it. If he stops pressing and asks a plain question instead, he is weighing your answer. Answer that plain question directly and give him the source.
Guy Reschenthaler.follow_up: Send his chief of staff a short written note with the agreed step and its deadline within two days.
Guy Reschenthaler.personality: Reschenthaler is a little reserved and quite practical, and details slip past him more readily than they do for most colleagues. Skepticism is a defining trait for him, and he heats up much more than most colleagues. His legislation spans somewhat more areas than most, and he follows bills through a bit less dependably than most. He works with the other side less than most, and hearings bring out a far more confrontational side than colleagues see.
Guy Reschenthaler.speaks: He explains his work in precise, thorough language, and his language carries somewhat less feeling than most. In a hearing he becomes much more combative than most colleagues and keeps returning to a point he has raised. His speech tends to stay close to the specifics of each bill. He keeps the conversation on the specific bill in front of him, and he does not wander into broad themes.
Guy Reschenthaler.decides: An ask gets weighed by how well it survives his skepticism, and outside pressure carries less weight with him than most. His legislation spans somewhat more areas than most, and he works with the other side less than most. Seeing bills through is less dependable for him, so a decision from him holds only when someone checks each step after it is made.

archetype.justification: She is among the most outgoing members, gives longer replies than most, and often speaks in quick bursts.

Gwen Moore.bottom_line: Let her talk at length, then answer briefly and close on one concrete ask. Her replies run long, so a short reply lands better than a rebuttal.
do: Keep points short, since her quick replies run in bursts
Open warmly, since she ranks with the most outgoing members
Put each agreed step in writing, since follow through lags
dont: Read her forceful phrasing as a settled position
Gwen Moore.warning_sign: Normally she talks at length and trails off much less than most. When she starts trailing off in the middle of a thought and her replies go unfinished, she has grown guarded. So stop pressing and ask what she needs to see.
Gwen Moore.follow_up: Send a brief written memo with the agreed step, its owner, and a due date.
Gwen Moore.personality: Moore is outgoing and gets worked up readily, and her words run more forceful and more upbeat than most colleagues. Replies run longer than most, often in quick bursts of short lines. Her language is far more emotionally intense than typical, and her follow through on bills lags well behind most colleagues. Her visibility is fairly high for her role, so her presence is felt in the room.
Gwen Moore.speaks: She speaks at length, then switches to quick bursts of brief replies, so her answer lengths swing widely. Her longest answers stretch well beyond the typical colleague's, and she leaves sentences hanging much less often than most. Word choice runs more forceful than most, and the phrasing carries much more filler. Her tone also runs a little more upbeat than most.
Gwen Moore.decides: She ranks requests by who gains, since community impact registers with her more than abstract figures. Figures alone carry less weight with her, so frame each number through the people it touches. Her work with the other party gives a bipartisan ask some footing. Bill follow through is a weak point for her, so every commitment needs a named owner who checks each next step.

archetype.justification: Quick to lead a conversation, reliable at seeing bills through, he holds his view firmly under challenge.

Hakeem Jeffries.bottom_line: Lead with the results the bill produces, in a few direct points. Once he takes a position he holds it, so secure his commitment early.
do: Put the measurable outcome first, before any background
Ask for a firm next step you can both name on the spot
If he pushes back, let him finish before you reply
Take his clean, direct answers at face value and move on
dont: Lean on shared values and trust, since he is quite skeptical
Hakeem Jeffries.warning_sign: Usually he talks in short direct answers, so a longer, more defensive reply signals he feels challenged. Let him finish, then restate the one ask in plain words.
Hakeem Jeffries.follow_up: Put the agreed next step in a written note to his staff, naming who owns it and when it falls due.
Hakeem Jeffries.personality: Jeffries is direct and dependable, and his words run on facts more than feeling. He is among the most reliable members in the House at seeing bills through. Under challenge he holds his view far more firmly than most, while taking charge of conversations somewhat more than most. His manner turns noticeably gentler in hearings, and his role keeps him highly visible.
Hakeem Jeffries.speaks: His answers come in fewer words than most, both in everyday conversation and in the interviews he gives. His word choice carries much less emotion than most, and his tone is somewhat more upbeat. Careful, detailed terms about his work keep his points specific. Under pressure he stands his ground and keeps his sentences tight, though his pitch varies more than most.
Hakeem Jeffries.decides: Firm backing and clear results are what he looks for before he takes up any request. Once he takes a position he defends it, so a yes from him tends to hold. He is highly visible, so his public record is easy to test against. Pressure from outside moves him less than most, so pressure alone will not change his mind, and a yes needs a named next step to hold.

archetype.justification: Among the most outgoing and curious colleagues, she covers many issues in gentle words with little emotional charge.

Haley Stevens.bottom_line: Lead with the broad case, since she is curious and outgoing, then pin down one concrete ask before the meeting ends.
do: Open with the wider context before the specifics
Let her finish, since her answers run long
Match her upbeat tone before you turn to the specifics
dont: Mistake her gentle tone for a firm commitment
Haley Stevens.warning_sign: By default she gives full answers and leads less than most. If she stops adding context and goes quiet, she is on guard, so ease off, restate the ask in one line, and leave room to respond.
Haley Stevens.follow_up: Put the results the ask would deliver in a plain written note, and name the date you will check back.
Haley Stevens.personality: Stevens is as curious and outgoing as almost any colleague, and she covers more topics than nearly all of them. Her tone is far softer than most, with little emotional charge, and her language runs cooler than nearly any colleague's. In interviews she answers at much greater length than most, and she leads conversations less than most. Her bills reach somewhat further than most, and in a room she is curious and wide ranging.
Haley Stevens.speaks: She gives long answers in interviews, and she trails off much more than most. Her words are upbeat, though they carry little emotional charge. Answers can arrive as rapid bursts of brief replies, a pattern seen much more than most. Tone runs much softer than most. Her recorded speech comes from the House floor, and her pace there is much slower, with somewhat longer gaps between phrases. Pitch is flatter than most.
Haley Stevens.decides: Outside pressure moves her less than nearly any colleague, so a push from a group seldom changes her mind.
