Her bills reach somewhat further than most, so she weighs an ask against the wider agenda it fits. She responds best to a brief, plain case about results, and an ask that touches several areas can gain ground with her. An ask tied to what it delivers is what moves her.

archetype.justification: Few members are more reserved than he is, he talks slowly, and his record on bills is very dependable.

Harold Rogers.bottom_line: Make the one ask concrete and small, then give him time to answer. He sees bills through reliably, so any yes he gives is one to bank.
do: Ask his office which question he needs answered before the meeting
Let his slow pace set timing, and wait for a commitment he will see through
Hold the ask out of public view while you build support
Pick a quiet room for the meeting, away from floor votes
dont: Drop the ask after one cool response, since pressure shifts his positions more than most
Let the first meeting run past the time you asked for
Walk him through a long slide deck at the first meeting
Harold Rogers.warning_sign: A general meeting cannot show whether he has settled on the request. Ask one narrow question, then give him a full minute before you add anything.
Harold Rogers.follow_up: Within two days, call his office to recap the agreed next step and the date set for it.
Harold Rogers.personality: Rogers stands out as one of the most reserved and most practical members in the House. He keeps his cool much better than most members do. Public remarks from him keep to a narrow set of topics, narrower than nearly anyone's, and few members sponsor bills across fewer policy areas. Votes and bills show a record that is much more dependable than most. He keeps a lower profile than nearly anyone, even for his role.
Harold Rogers.speaks: He talks among the slowest in the chamber, and his pauses between phrases run a little shorter than most. His pitch stays somewhat flatter than most across the whole talk. Give each point room, and keep your own pace relaxed and easy to follow. Let each reply finish before you add a second point, so the first one lands fully.
Harold Rogers.decides: Outside pressure moves him clearly more than most, so note who is weighing in around him and what they are asking of him. Ask what he needs to see before he weighs in. Once he names what he needs, answer that point alone and leave the rest for later. Keep the date visible in every follow-up you send, so it is easy to act on.

archetype.justification: Her forceful wording, skeptical stance and dependable votes fit a bull's direct, driving style closely.

Harriet Hageman.bottom_line: Lead with the detailed written case and keep your own words short. Pressure from others counts for less with her, so the case itself has to do the work.
do: Share the written technical evidence before the meeting so she can check it
Keep your words short, since her own words run sharp
dont: Let a trailing answer close the topic before she finishes
Count on outside allies to move her, since pressure counts for less
Harriet Hageman.warning_sign: She usually keeps her words even and speaks in careful detail. When her words turn sharp and she trails off mid answer, she is on guard, so slow down and ask one plain question.
Harriet Hageman.follow_up: Send her the written evidence and a short list of next steps, with a date for each, within two days.
Harriet Hageman.personality: Hageman is a skeptical and direct member who weighs claims closely and says so. Her grip on details runs loose compared with most colleagues, yet her public talk is careful and detailed, so her arguments read as precise and sharp. Easily stirred, she speaks forcefully and sounds more upbeat in print than almost anyone in her chamber, so she brings energy into most rooms. Her legislation spans much narrower ground, and she is among the most dependable members on votes, so her record stays focused rather than broad.
Harriet Hageman.speaks: Her answers vary in length much more than most, and she often trails off before a sentence ends. Wording cuts harder than almost anyone's, and emotional charge runs higher than almost anyone's. She speaks forcefully and in much more careful detail than most colleagues. Pitch sits flatter than nearly any colleague's, so emphasis comes through word choice instead. This pattern shows in most of her public exchanges.
Harriet Hageman.decides: She tests each ask against the written evidence and starts from skepticism about claims. Her legislation spans much narrower ground than most colleagues, so an ask that fits her own lines gets further. Pressure from outside counts for less with her. She is among the most reliable members on votes and in carrying bills through, so a decision holds when it has a written next step.

archetype.justification: His careful organization, firm grip on conversations and readiness to defend positions earn the Bull label.

Henry Cuellar.bottom_line: Bring a results focused case and a clear next step, since he holds the floor. Outside voices sway him clearly less, so let the facts make the case.
do: Let him take the floor first, since he tends to hold it
Answer his challenges directly, since he defends his position hard
Confirm each step in writing, since he follows bills through closely
dont: Treat his friendly demeanor as a settled yes
Assume a quiet ask will win without outside voices
Henry Cuellar.warning_sign: He usually leads talk with force and defends his position hard when challenged. If he starts conceding points and his filler drops away, he is on guard, so ease off, restate the ask plainly, and confirm the next step.
Henry Cuellar.follow_up: Shortly afterward, mail a written recap of the next move, naming the staffer who follows up and the due date.
Henry Cuellar.personality: Cuellar tends to be fairly outgoing, and his agreeable streak runs deep. Careful organization marks his detail work, and his talk reaches a little further across topics than most. He takes the lead in conversation with unusual force, and his words come across as warm yet pointed. His visibility is very high for someone in his role, and he defends a position harder than most colleagues.
Henry Cuellar.speaks: Pauses between phrases come quickly, leaving little room, and his pitch swings more than most. He fills gaps with filler more than most in the House. When pushed back on, he digs in harder than most colleagues. His words land forceful and warm, and in hearings he runs a little less combative than most. Each exchange tends to stay direct from start to finish.
Henry Cuellar.decides: Whether he can hold the floor for it and whether it fits work he already defends is what he weighs. Follow through on bills is exceptionally dependable for him, so a commitment tends to hold. Outside voices sway him clearly less, so the case itself must carry the ask. So he commits when the backing is visible and the step is written down.

archetype.justification: His replies come in quick bursts of brief answers, he builds across the other side less than most, and he is less dependable on bills than most.

Henry Johnson.bottom_line: Keep your ask brief, since his replies come in fast bursts. Follow up through his staff, since he sees bills through a little less reliably than most.
do: Send the one ask in writing to his staff a few days ahead
Open with a yes-or-no question, since his replies come back in quick short runs
Hold a short pause after each of his long answers before you speak
Schedule a check-in to see if the step moved, since follow-through runs weaker than most
dont: Read his quick replies as a final answer
Lead with numbers and results ahead of who the plan helps
Count a trailed-off sentence as agreement
Henry Johnson.warning_sign: His replies usually come in quick runs, with less filler than most. If he keeps circling one point and slows to pick each word, he has quit engaging with your ask. Keep the ask to one line, then wait for his reply.
Henry Johnson.follow_up: Ask his legislative staff for one written answer on the open point, by a day you set.
Henry Johnson.personality: Johnson stands out as one of the most curious House members, and his public talk spans more subjects than nearly anyone there. He is a bit reserved and builds with the other side less than most. On votes and bills, his follow-through runs weaker than most. His public profile is much lower than most members'. His bills touch a broader set of subjects than most members do.
Henry Johnson.speaks: In interviews his answers run far longer than most, and their length varies less than almost any House member. His replies arrive in quick runs, and that is his normal rhythm. Delivery runs somewhat faster than most, with long pauses between phrases, and his pitch swings wider than nearly anyone's. Give his long pauses room, and do not fill the gaps with your own point.
Henry Johnson.decides: A short case about who benefits fits him best. Across the aisle, he works somewhat less than most. On follow-through he is somewhat behind most members, so do not count on the bill moving by itself. Tie one new idea to the one real household it would reach, and explain it plainly, so he can picture the stake in plain terms.

archetype.justification: Very careful by temperament and a little reserved, and fairly dependable on votes and bills, with a much milder hearing tone than most.

Herbert Conaway.bottom_line: Plan for a second conversation, since outside pressure sways him more than most members do.
do: Walk his staff through the technical rules the plan changes, before the meeting
Start with the one technical change that matters most, before any background
Let him set the question pace in a formal meeting, given his mild hearing tone
Close by setting the next date with his office, given his fair follow-through
dont: Add a technical framework the plan does not use, since he leans toward familiar ground
Pack the meeting with more people than the ask needs
Let a single outside voice carry the whole case
Herbert Conaway.warning_sign: In hearings he is usually much less combative than most members. If his tone turns even milder than that usual style, he is losing interest in the point at hand. Drop that point, and ask only for what you need next.
Herbert Conaway.follow_up: Send his legislative director a written detail sheet by Thursday, with one next step and its date.
Herbert Conaway.personality: Conaway is much more careful and orderly than most colleagues, and he sees his bills through fairly reliably. He keeps to himself a little, and he prefers familiar ground more than most. The bills he carries touch far fewer areas than most, while his talk stays on a tight set of topics. His public talk is far thinner on detail than almost anyone's in the House. Hearings bring out a milder side of him than most colleagues see. He serves on the House Small Business Committee.
Herbert Conaway.speaks: On the House floor his speech comes somewhat quicker than most, his volume stays fairly even, and his pitch varies somewhat less than most. His tone in hearings comes across much milder than most House members. When he describes his work, few members in the chamber are less detailed, so bring the detail with you and fill any gap in his account yourself.
Herbert Conaway.decides: Outside groups move him more than most, so ask them to raise it with his office themselves. Give each group one clear sentence on what the plan does, so it can speak for the plan in its own words. His follow-through is more reliable than most, so his commitments generally stand once made. End by asking which outside voice he would most want to hear from.

archetype.justification: Her careful, organized work and high reliability in the House make her a diligent and thorough colleague.

Hillary Scholten.bottom_line: Bring a brief, pointed case on the results, with the details in writing and a clear ask. She is reliable and will follow through once she commits.
do: Put the facts and results in writing before the meeting
Agree the next step and its date while she is in the room
dont: Skip the written ask and rely on her reliability alone
Hillary Scholten.warning_sign: She usually keeps her tone even and her answers plain. If she turns sharper than usual, something on the ask has struck a nerve, so slow down and ask which part concerns her most.
Hillary Scholten.follow_up: Send her a one page written summary of the ask within two days, with the next step and its owner named.
Hillary Scholten.personality: Scholten is an agreeable member who is hard to rattle and is among the most dependable in the House at seeing bills through. Her public words are gentler than most, and her talk about policy is precise. She keeps track of the details of a plan, so once a plan is set she tends to keep it moving through each step.
Hillary Scholten.speaks: Her talk moves at a fairly quick pace, with shorter pauses between phrases than most. Her words are gentler than most colleagues, and her talk about policy is precise. In hearings she is far less confrontational than most colleagues. Her volume rises and falls somewhat more than most, which gives her points emphasis. Her pitch stays a little flatter than most, so her tone reads plain.
Hillary Scholten.decides: Whether the facts hold up and whether the work can be carried out decides how she weighs an ask. Her agreeable streak keeps her open to a reasonable request. Her follow-through is among the most dependable in the House, so once she commits the work tends to move forward. So a decision with a written record and a named owner tends to hold with her.

archetype.justification: Very curious and very skeptical, with a much broader issue range and somewhat more outgoing.

Ilhan Omar.bottom_line: Make the ask in short form and let her push on it, since she checks claims very hard and answers briefly.
do: Ask one question she can answer quickly
Lead with who the ask helps, in plain stories
In a hearing, expect pointed, combative questions and answer them directly
dont: Count on support from the other side of the aisle
Lean on outside pressure to carry the ask
Ilhan Omar.warning_sign: She usually keeps answers among the shortest in the House. When replies drag and wording turns much sharper, that signals guardedness, so pull back and put one plain question.
Ilhan Omar.follow_up: Within the week, email her staff a written record of the request and of each settled action, then check progress two weeks later.
Ilhan Omar.personality: Omar has a very curious and quite skeptical streak, while her public talk ranges far wider across issues than most. She is somewhat more outgoing than most, among the quickest to be worked up, and among the most visible figures in the chamber. Public wording is very cool and much sharper than most. Joint work across the aisle is still rarer for her than for almost every colleague, and her bills reach completion much less often than most. Together these make her a probing presence in the room, quicker to challenge a point than to trade for one.
Ilhan Omar.speaks: She ranges across many issues and talks about her work with much less care for detail than most. Replies are among the briefest in the House, with somewhat more filler and a somewhat faster pace than most. Public phrasing cuts much sharper than most, and her tone climbs and drops somewhat more than most. At hearings she counts among the most combative voices in the chamber.
Ilhan Omar.decides: Asks framed around who gets helped fit her best, and she checks the claims behind any ask very hard before she commits. Outside pressure has a little less sway over her than over most members. Working across the aisle is less common for her than for almost anyone, and bills stall much more than most, so each choice needs an owner.

archetype.justification: Bills he writes span many areas, and his voice stays flatter than most while he is much less visible.

Jack Bergman.bottom_line: Bring a story about who is helped, and tie the ask to one clear result. Pressure from outside has a modest pull on him, so bring voices from home.
do: Lead with who is helped, since people centered stories fit him best
Match his volume shifts, and pair with a colleague across the aisle
In a hearing, expect hard questions and answer each one plainly
dont: Count on a loud public push from him, since he is much less visible
Jack Bergman.warning_sign: In a hearing he usually becomes much more combative, and the change is easy to hear. Let him finish, keep your tone level, and return to the one plain question you need answered.
Jack Bergman.follow_up: Afterward, send a written summary tied to the people helped, with one dated next step to his office.
Jack Bergman.personality: Bergman covers many areas in his bills, much more than most colleagues. He is much less visible than most members, and he is fairly curious and a bit looser on specifics than most. Strong feelings come somewhat faster for him than for most. He reaches across the aisle, though much less than most, and his wording feels far less charged than most.
Jack Bergman.speaks: His talk touches somewhat more areas than most, and his account of his work runs somewhat more careful than most. Words carry far less charge than most, and delivery is flatter than most. His pace runs somewhat slower than most, and his volume shifts more than most. At hearings he turns much more combative than most, and that edge shows quickly.
Jack Bergman.decides: Prior to any decision he counts how many areas it touches and whether it has a people centered result. Pressure from outside has a modest pull on him, so local voices can tip a close call. He is much less visible than most, so his backing rarely shows publicly. Any yes from him holds only when a named sponsor owns the next step.

archetype.justification: He is very reserved, very careful and organized, and much less inclined than most to take charge of a conversation.

Jack Reed.bottom_line: Lead with the results and back them with a careful written case. Outside pressure moves him clearly less than most, so the facts must carry the ask.
do: Put the results and their sources in a written memo he can review
Give him room to finish, since he trails off more than most
Invite his view early, since he is very reserved
In a hearing, expect courteous questions, since he is least combative
dont: Push him for a commitment before his review is done
Fill the silences with your own talk, since he takes charge much less
Jack Reed.warning_sign: He usually lets others lead a conversation and does not push his own points early. If he suddenly takes the lead and presses a point, he has a firm view, so ask him directly what would move him.
Jack Reed.follow_up: Email his staff a brief recap within a day, naming the next step and its owner.
Jack Reed.personality: Reed is careful and methodical in his approach, and he is among the most reserved Senate members. Markedly agreeable, he takes difficult questions without being ruffled, and his public language reads as cooler than nearly any Senate colleague's. Issue range runs much broader than most, and those issues get worked through in careful detail. His bills span more issues than nearly any colleague's, and he is very reliable at seeing them through. He represents Rhode Island and serves on Senate Banking.
Jack Reed.speaks: His answers are long and often drift off before the end, more than most do. Phrasing comes across as much gentler than most, and his wording sounds cooler than nearly any colleague's, with flat excitement and little social framing. Issue range runs broad, and he works through those issues in somewhat more detailed terms than most. Filler words show up more than usual, and his answers tend to come as long single turns rather than quick runs.
Jack Reed.decides: He weighs an ask by the facts and results behind it, and he is very dependable once he has reviewed the case. His bills span more issues than nearly any colleague's, so an ask that touches several of his areas can fit. Pressure from outside has clearly less pull on him, so a case has to stand on the record rather than on urgency. So a yes from him holds when the record is in front of him and the next vote is on the calendar.

archetype.justification: Her wording is much gentler than most, she sees bills through very reliably, and impact on people fits her best.

Jacky Rosen.bottom_line: Lead with who the policy helps and bring those people in, since outside voices weigh heavier on her than on most.
do: Open with a story about a specific person the bill helps
Tie the ask to a bill already moving, since her record on bills is strong
dont: Read her gentleness as agreement already reached
Expect her support to hold once outside pressure fades
Jacky Rosen.warning_sign: She usually speaks gently and agrees easily, so a change in tone is the signal to watch. If her wording turns firmer than usual, she is on guard about the ask. Slow down, restate what the bill does for people, and give her room.
Jacky Rosen.follow_up: Within a day, send her staff a short written note on the bill's impact on one or two people it helps.
Jacky Rosen.personality: Rosen, of Nevada, is fairly curious and agreeable and a little reserved, and she is roused a bit more readily than most. Across issues, her bills range a bit wider than most, and she is very reliable at seeing them through. Her wording is notably gentle, and it carries little emotional heat compared with nearly every colleague. Senate Small Business is one of her committees, and her public profile sits about as low as it gets in the chamber. In the room she comes across as gentle and dependable.
Jacky Rosen.speaks: Her wording is gentle, and her points come across without much heat. Topics range wider than nearly any colleague's, and close, specific attention to detail runs through her descriptions of work. Particulars tend to carry her points rather than rousing language. Her gentle tone shows up across her public statements, and the manner stays consistent. Across her public remarks, the wide topic range and the careful particulars come through together.
Jacky Rosen.decides: Her test is who a request reaches, and outside voices hold more sway over her than over most colleagues in the Senate. Once a bill is hers, she stays with it, so her engagement tends to last. Being fairly agreeable, she is open to a case made on its merits, so an ask backed by people it helps gains ground with her.

archetype.justification: Community impact framing suits her best, and hearings bring out a sharper side in her.

Jahana Hayes.bottom_line: Bring one specific ask backed by voices she already trusts, since outside pressure moves her more than nearly anyone's. Ask for a dated next step before you leave.
do: Line up advocates she already listens to before the meeting
Leave room for long pauses and shifting volume, since she takes time between phrases
Confirm details in writing, since she has a weak record of seeing bills through
dont: Rely on a verbal yes to carry a bill forward
Press her hard in a hearing, since she is much more combative there
Jahana Hayes.warning_sign: Her volume usually swings a great deal, so a louder moment by itself is normal for her. If she turns combative and presses hard, the point matters to her, so slow down and answer it directly.
Jahana Hayes.follow_up: Send a written list of the commitments you agreed in the meeting to her office within two days.
Jahana Hayes.personality: Hayes is somewhat curious and somewhat agreeable, and she gets worked up a bit more readily than most. Her public talk covers a broader spread of issues, but her description of her work stays less detailed than nearly any colleague's. Speech from her carries somewhat more charge than usual, and she crosses over a little less often than most. Issue areas in her bills run somewhat wider, yet she is much less dependable at getting them across the finish line. Together these make her a broad and emotionally charged voice for Connecticut, but one whose follow-through lags her ideas.
Jahana Hayes.speaks: Her talk runs somewhat slow, with long pauses between phrases and a volume that swings more than nearly anyone's in the House. Pitch holds far flatter than most. Her words carry more emotional charge than usual, and her talk about her work is less detailed than nearly any colleague's. In a hearing she is much more combative and presses her points hard.
Jahana Hayes.decides: Who stands behind a request settles it for her, since outside forces sway her more than nearly anyone's. Her bills span somewhat more issue areas, but she is much less dependable at finishing them. So a promise made in the room needs a written trail to hold. In a hearing she is much more combative, so an ask still under review can harden there. A broad coalition of voices she respects is what moves her.

archetype.justification: He is one of the most curious members, much more careful than most colleagues, and his answers run longer than nearly any colleague's.

Jake Auchincloss.bottom_line: Lead with the result in one plain sentence, then give his long answers room. Outside voices sway him less than most, so your case has to do the work.
do: Bring a short written note on what the policy delivers
Open with a tight question, since his answers tend to run long
Let his longest answers run, then pick out the one point you need
End with a named next step and an ally from his own party
dont: Argue the same point again once he digs in
Pitch the ask in public before the details are settled
Mistake his mild word choice for a weak position
Jake Auchincloss.warning_sign: He usually lets others steer, and he rarely grabs the floor. If he suddenly takes charge and steers the room, he is holding the floor more than usual. Stop and ask him one open question.
Jake Auchincloss.follow_up: Send his legislative staff a one-page written result summary the same day, naming who owns each step.
Jake Auchincloss.personality: Auchincloss is a scholarly, organized thinker, and few match his curiosity. He is much more careful than most colleagues. Yet he is a touch reserved, and his public talk covers much more ground than most. His bills reach across far more topic areas than most. He builds across the aisle much less than most colleagues. Much less easily rattled than most colleagues, he also has a very high profile for his role.
Jake Auchincloss.speaks: Few members talk for longer in interviews than he does, and his longest ones run longer still. Answer length barely varies, a pattern few members match. He uses very little filler. His volume stays much more even than most; his pitch sits flatter than most. In hearings he leans a bit more combative than most members, so keep formal exchanges tight. When challenged he holds his ground somewhat more than most, so wait for the end of one long thought before you challenge it.
Jake Auchincloss.decides: He decides on outcomes, so a clear account of what the policy changes, with its numbers, carries the most weight. Having taken a stand, he defends it when challenged across interviews, so prepare the hardest rebuttal well before you meet. Before you leave, ask him what result would make him commit, by when, and record his answer in writing before the next meeting.

archetype.justification: Very outgoing and one of the most reliable members at seeing bills through, he fits a focused worker.

Jake Ellzey.bottom_line: Lead with the practical step and the vote it needs, not outside pressure, since that moves him less than most members.
do: Open with the practical step, and keep the meeting brief
Name the vote he has to take and the date it falls on
dont: Lean on outside groups to move his vote
Skip the practical step for a broad pitch
Jake Ellzey.warning_sign: Open discussion will not reveal how he moves a bill through its last steps. Ask his staff which step still has to clear before the vote. Then confirm the date it falls on.
Jake Ellzey.follow_up: After the meeting, send his staff the vote date and the one open step, with a name for who clears it by when.
Jake Ellzey.personality: Ellzey shows a very outgoing side, and he explains his own work in closer, fuller detail than most. He covers somewhat fewer issues in his bills than most. Among the strongest in the chamber is his record on finishing what he starts. A focused lane is where he works, and he follows its steps closely. He sits on the Small Business committee, and he represents Texas.
Jake Ellzey.speaks: He covers a narrower range of topics than most and explains his own work in more exact terms than most. Specifics and steps are laid out, and replies stay tied to the item in front of him. He speaks in a plain, direct way, and only a small share of his talk drifts outside the bill he is working on. Listeners get exact detail more often than broad framing.
Jake Ellzey.decides: Proposals move forward when they have a clear vote and a clear next step. His record on finishing what he starts is among the strongest in the chamber. Outside pressure carries less pull with him than with most colleagues, so a case that stands on its merits counts for more than a push from groups. Since his bills cover fewer areas, an ask within them has the best chance. A decision holds only when its vote date and owner are written down.

archetype.justification: Quite reserved and slow in delivery, with long pauses and a flat pitch, he fits the Tortoise's deliberate style.

James Baird.bottom_line: Bring the written detail ahead and give him time to answer. Outside groups move him more than most, and a late push from supporters can change his view.
do: Share written technical evidence before the meeting
Let his slow delivery run and wait out long pauses before you speak
Tie each step to a date he can track
dont: Skip rushing him, since his delivery runs slowly
In a hearing, do not assume he will concede easily
James Baird.warning_sign: In a hearing he usually speaks slowly and keeps close to the record. If he gets more combative than usual, he has grown guarded, so stop the sales talk and let him set the next step.
James Baird.follow_up: Email his legislative director a written summary of the ask and each step by Monday.
James Baird.personality: Baird comes across as quite reserved and very hard to rattle, more so than most colleagues. Much more precise than most in his talk about his work, he also covers a somewhat wider set of issues than most. Bills cover a much narrower set of areas than most. Public visibility runs much lower than most colleagues, and he represents Indiana. He takes his time with each point, which matches the slow pace of his delivery.
James Baird.speaks: He speaks more slowly than nearly any colleague, with pauses that run much longer than most, and his loudness swings a lot, much more than most. Pitch stays far flatter than most, and his public language carries a little less charge than most. Each exchange moves at his own deliberate pace. He answers slowly and keeps his pace even when questions come quickly.
James Baird.decides: He judges an ask by the care in its construction and by who stands behind it. His bills cover a narrow range of areas, so an ask inside a narrow lane gets a serious look. Supporters back home sway him more than most, and written evidence he can check holds his attention. Documents that answer his questions in advance keep the process moving, so a decision follows the material he can verify.

archetype.justification: He grabs the lead in conversation and defends his stance when challenged, far more than peers do.

James Clyburn.bottom_line: Bring a short, direct case built on what the policy delivers, and let him take the lead in the room.
do: Open with the result the policy already delivered
Hold back until his long pause ends, then reply
Put the record of votes and follow through on one page
dont: Talk over the gap he leaves before answering
Compete with him for control of the room
James Clyburn.warning_sign: He usually takes a considered pause before he responds, then takes the floor. If he stops pausing and defends his position before a challenge is finished, he is on guard, so respond to his challenge with one fact.
James Clyburn.follow_up: Send his staff a dated written summary of the agreed step within two days, with the owner named.
James Clyburn.personality: Clyburn is outgoing and curious, ranking near the top of the House on both counts, and his public tone runs noticeably warm. Holding the floor and standing firm under challenge comes naturally, far more than most. His legislation spans a narrow set of issue areas, yet he is very reliable at seeing it through. Visibility runs very high in the chamber, and he represents South Carolina.
James Clyburn.speaks: He talks more slowly than most and leaves longer pauses between phrases, so his points arrive in deliberate steps. His volume shifts a little less than most, though it changes more on public radio than on Sunday talk shows. Holding the floor in longer turns is typical for him, and his words run assertive and somewhat upbeat. In a hearing he turns sharply combative, and he answers a challenge with the same force.
James Clyburn.decides: Plain results and facts that survive a challenge are the tests he applies to any request. He takes charge of the deal and does not give up a position easily, so a decision sticks once he has owned it. Pressure from outside has a lighter pull on him than on many peers, so an early yes from him carries weight.

archetype.justification: He takes charge of conversations somewhat more than most, defends his position across shows, and is a little skeptical, which fits a forceful style.

James Comer.bottom_line: Make the case once and clearly, and expect him to defend his position when challenged. Outside pushing has less pull on him, so a dated choice in the room counts.
do: Make the case once, clearly, and in the first minute
Invite him to defend his view, then answer each point
Limit each point to one sentence and pause for his reply
dont: Assume a skeptical nod means he is convinced
Count on outside voices alone to move his vote
James Comer.warning_sign: Usually his pace runs quick, with pauses that come a little sooner than most. If he slows and his pauses lengthen, treat that as guardedness, so ease off and offer him a dated choice.
James Comer.follow_up: Once you leave, send him a dated memo recording the choice and its date, copying his legislative aide within two days.
James Comer.personality: Comer ranks near the top on following through with bills, and few colleagues are more visible. He steers discussions somewhat more often than most peers, and he digs in much harder than most when pressed. His manner reads somewhat warmer than most, though his language is a shade less social than most. Testimony sessions find him ranking among the most combative members, which makes him a forceful, dependable operator.
James Comer.speaks: His tempo is brisk, quicker than most, with pauses running a little shorter than most and a tone that climbs and drops more than most. In interviews his answers run a little shorter than most, and his longest answers come in shorter than most. He defends his position much more than most when challenged, and his public language is a little less charged than most. Pressed in hearings, he turns as pointed as almost anyone present.
James Comer.decides: A clear decision date is what he looks for first, and when challenged he keeps his stance and holds it firmly. Lobbying from outside matters less to him than to most peers, so the argument has to stand on the record and timeline. His follow through ranks near the top, so a clear timeline is what gets his commitment to stick.

archetype.justification: His pace ranks at the fast end of the chamber, and his talk stays on a much narrower set of issues.

James Gallagher.bottom_line: Lead with a short, direct case on results, and keep the ask to one area. Pressure from outside pulls on him less than most, so the facts must carry it.
do: Lead with the result, since short direct cases suit him
Keep the case short, and bring one clear result per point
Give a clear next step, since pressure from outside pulls on him less than most
dont: Skip long warm-ups, since he is fairly outgoing
James Gallagher.warning_sign: An open meeting will not reveal how he handles a challenge to his facts, so ask one direct question about the figures early. Then take one concrete step: send the key figures in writing before the next hearing, and name who will respond.
James Gallagher.follow_up: Afterward, send a brief note to his office with the key result, the next step, and a date to act on.
James Gallagher.personality: Gallagher is fairly outgoing, fairly curious, and fairly careful, and quick in conversation. Rattling him takes much more than it takes for most colleagues. His wording runs far more charged than most colleagues, and his talk centers on a much smaller range of topics than most. He is a bit less visible than most, and his detail runs much less careful than most.
James Gallagher.speaks: His pace is faster than nearly anyone's in the chamber, and his pauses are among the shortest. His pitch is among the most varied in the chamber. Feeling runs far higher in his wording than most, while his case stays on a few narrow points. His detail runs much less careful than most. Under a question, he tends to answer at once rather than pause.
James Gallagher.decides: Before backing it he asks whether results and facts are laid out in a short, direct case. Pressure from outside pulls on him less than most, so the facts need to do the persuading. His public role sits a bit lower than most, so a public push alone will not carry him. Commitments from him hold once a dated next step has an owner.

archetype.justification: He is curious and careful, and his public talk covers more ground than most.

James Himes.bottom_line: Bring written evidence and let him run through it, since he talks at length. He is very dependable on finishing bills, so a dated step he accepts will hold.
do: Bring the source behind every figure you cite
Give him room for long answers before you interject
If he defends his view, hold your ground on the single ask
Bring the questions he will want answered, since he is so curious
dont: Assume a trailing sentence means he has finished
Cite his bills without checking how far each one moved
Put the ask on his public stage before the detail is settled
James Himes.warning_sign: He usually speaks at a quick clip, so brisk talk is normal for him. If he slows down and his answers drop their filler, he is choosing his words carefully, so ask him to say the key point again.
James Himes.follow_up: Send his staff a dated summary of the next step and who owns it by Friday.
James Himes.personality: Himes is outgoing and curious, and he is careful and organized in his habits. Across public talk he covers a far wider set of issues than most, yet accounts of his own work come across as far less careful and detailed. Emotion runs much higher in his words than in most, while he counts among the most visible people in the House for his role. He reaches across the aisle more than nearly anyone, and few colleagues match his record on bills. His state is Connecticut.
James Himes.speaks: His delivery is much faster than most, and gaps between his phrases are briefer than almost anyone else's in the House. Answers run long, with frequent trailing off, and filler appears more than almost anyone in the House uses. Words come out upbeat and active, carrying a heavy dose of feeling. The range of issues he covers is wide, and he is quicker than most to defend what he says.
James Himes.decides: He weighs an ask on how it fits his issue set and on whether it can win across the aisle. Reaching across the aisle comes easily to him, so a bipartisan ask gets a fair hearing. Seeing bills through is a strength for him, so a step he accepts gets done. He defends his view when challenged, so a case that holds its ground will stand up to him. A commitment from him holds when a written next step has a named owner.

archetype.justification: Much more readily worked up than most, with issue talk narrower than almost anyone's, and community impact is the frame that fits him best.

James Justice.bottom_line: Make the ask concrete and give it an owner before leaving. He is much less reliable than most at seeing bills through, so the next step needs a name.
do: Open with a short story about who the bill would help
Let him take each point in before you add the next
Add outside backers, expecting them to sway him somewhat less than most
dont: Treat a verbal yes as the end of the work
James Justice.warning_sign: By default his combativeness in hearings runs somewhat lower than the norm. If he turns combative in a hearing, he is irritated or on guard, so slow the exchange, restate the point, and ask what would make it work.
James Justice.follow_up: Within two days, send his legislative director a one page note naming the owner and the people the bill would reach.
James Justice.personality: Justice belongs with the most outgoing colleagues in the chamber, yet he sits among the least visible for his role. Quick to get set off, much more than most, he keeps an issue focus narrower than almost anyone's. Looser with details than nearly any colleague, he also has bills that cover much fewer areas than most. He is much less reliable than most at seeing bills through.
James Justice.speaks: He speaks very slowly, with somewhat shorter pauses between phrases than most, a somewhat flatter pitch, and a volume that varies somewhat less than most. His talk covers a set of issues narrower than nearly any colleague's, and when he describes his work, the detail is much less exact than most. In hearings his combativeness runs somewhat lower than most members, and his manner stays low key.
James Justice.decides: Requests win him over when the people they reach are easy to name and the case is concrete. Outside backers sway him somewhat less than most members do. His bills span much fewer areas than most, so an ask inside his usual areas suits him. Stories about who is affected reach him most, so a case built on them holds with him.

archetype.justification: He is very practical and very careful, and he sticks to a narrow set of issues in his bills and talk.

James Lankford.bottom_line: Send written, technical evidence well before the meeting and let him work through it, since he weighs documented detail and then follows through.
do: Bring the specific figures and their sources in writing
Ask him to name the next step, then expect it to happen
If he gives a long answer, let him finish before you reply
In a hearing, expect little combat and plan for long answers
dont: Count on support from the other side to carry the ask
Lean on rapport to win him over
James Lankford.warning_sign: He usually talks faster than nearly anyone and uses almost no filler. If his pace drops or filler creeps in, he is losing patience, so stop and ask which figure he wants checked.
James Lankford.follow_up: Email him a brief recap by Friday that lists the next action and its owner, since he tends to carry commitments through.
James Lankford.personality: Lankford is very reserved and very practical, with a narrow focus and a very careful, organized style. He is harder to rattle than nearly anyone in the chamber, and his public words come across as much gentler than most. Bridging is rarer for him than nearly anyone, yet he is as dependable as almost anyone at carrying bills through. Taken together he is a careful specialist who values precision and sees commitments through, and he is a little more visible than most.
James Lankford.speaks: He talks faster than nearly anyone in the chamber, with pauses between phrases shorter than nearly anyone's and a volume that stays more even than nearly anyone's. Pitch swings more than nearly anyone's, yet public wording is a little flatter and less forceful than most. Interview answers run much longer than most, and hearings find him as combative as almost nobody. Public words hold much less heat than most.
James Lankford.decides: Written technical material suits him best, so he tests a request by how well its paperwork holds up. Once he accepts a commitment it tends to hold, since he sees bills through more reliably than nearly anyone. He is a little more visible than most, which gives him a public voice for an ask he backs. Working across party lines is not his habit, so an ask that needs crossing the aisle will struggle with him.

archetype.justification: His outgoing manner sits at the top of the House, he is very visible, and he takes on a wide spread of bills in forceful language.

James McGovern.bottom_line: Offer a shared role he can announce, and keep the case direct. Pressure from outside pulls on him less than most, so the case must earn his support.
do: Lead with the shared announcement, because he ranks among the most outgoing members
Name the partner who will share the lead on the ask
Let him set the pace, since he takes charge of the room
In a hearing, expect sharp rebuttals and keep your answers short
dont: Count on dense detail from him, since his replies come in briefer form than most
Assume a quiet hearing, since hearings bring out a sharper edge in him
Hide the announcement, since he is already very visible
James McGovern.warning_sign: When pressed, he usually takes charge of the exchange and fills the gaps with filler words. Let him run out his point, then ask one short question that needs a direct answer.
James McGovern.follow_up: Afterward, set out the shared role, the named partner and one dated step in a short written message.
James McGovern.personality: McGovern is very visible and sits at the top of the chamber for outgoing manner. He is fairly curious and a little skeptical, and his detail runs much looser than most. Bill scope is among the widest in the chamber, and his wording is among the most forceful. He leans on filler well beyond most colleagues, and his replies come in briefer form than most.
James McGovern.speaks: His words are among the most forceful in the chamber, and among the least action focused. Delivery runs somewhat slower than most, with longer pauses between phrases. His voice sits somewhat flatter in pitch than most, and his answers come out far shorter than most. Filler fills his talk well beyond the usual level. In a hearing his combative edge runs a notch higher than usual.
James McGovern.decides: What matters for him is whether an ask offers a shared, visible role to lead. Because he reaches across party lines somewhat more than most, a bipartisan partner adds real weight. Pressure from outside pulls on him less than most, so a yes depends on his own read. His bills reach across more areas than nearly anyone's, so an ask inside those areas fits him.

archetype.justification: Very careful and organized, hard to rattle, and more detailed about his work than nearly any colleague, which fits the Tortoise.

James Risch.bottom_line: Come with the specifics ready and let him test each one. Outside pressure counts for less with him than most, so the merits must carry the ask.
do: Map the bill's votes and milestones on one page he can check
Give him room to lead the discussion once he is engaged
If a hearing is ahead, expect firmer questions than in private meetings
dont: Cut his long answers short before he finishes his point
Walk into a hearing expecting a casual exchange with him
Expect a warm, quick back and forth, since he is much more reserved than most
James Risch.warning_sign: He usually takes the lead and talks at a slightly quick pace, with much less pause between phrases than most. When he slows down and lets others speak, he is weighing your point, so stay quiet and give him time to answer.
James Risch.follow_up: After the meeting, send him the bill's vote and milestone timeline in writing, with the next date he must confirm by.
James Risch.personality: Risch is much more reserved than most, yet his tone runs somewhat warmer than most, and he tends to lead talks a bit more than most. He reads as very careful and organized, much harder to rattle than most, and more detailed about his work than nearly any colleague. Votes and bills show a record that tops nearly anyone's. Language is forceful, yet less excitable than nearly anyone's. In the room he is exact and deliberate, and he holds the floor when he is engaged.
James Risch.speaks: His delivery runs somewhat quicker than most, with much shorter pauses between phrases and a volume that holds somewhat more evenly than most. Pitch varies much less than most. He touches somewhat fewer topics than most and frames them around the specifics of the work. His answers run somewhat longer than most in conversation, and their length varies much more than most from one exchange to the next. Language stays much less charged than most, and he keeps to the detail rather than the atmosphere.
James Risch.decides: Asks hinge on whether their record can be verified, since his own record of getting measures done beats nearly anyone's. He leads a discussion somewhat more than most, so what he hears in the room shapes where he lands. Outside voices have much less pull on him than on most colleagues. So an ask without a checkable record tends to stall with him.

archetype.justification: He trails off unfinished more than almost anyone, often in rapid bursts of brief replies, while his bills span far fewer topics than most.

James Walkinshaw.bottom_line: Lead with who your ask helps and bring outside voices behind it. Outside voices shift him more than most, so pin a dated next step.
do: Open with the people your ask would help
Bring outside groups who back the request in writing
Put a dated next step on the record
dont: Assume a verbal yes will carry itself
Treat one sitting as enough to close the ask
James Walkinshaw.warning_sign: Usually he trails off and his volume swings up and down more than most, with long pauses between phrases. If his pauses grow longer still and he stops finishing his points, he is losing interest, so stop pressing and put the open question in writing.
James Walkinshaw.follow_up: Afterward, mail him a single page written recap of the request, naming the people it helps, and copy his legislative director within two days.
James Walkinshaw.personality: Walkinshaw keeps an organized mind, yet he is fairly visible and talks about a much narrower set of topics than almost anyone. He ranks near the bottom on following bills to passage, and his phrasing cuts sharper than nearly any colleague's. His answers stay even in length, and he often trails off in rapid bursts, so his manner reads as busy and loose. Together these traits make him a specialist who moves on outside voices and needs a named date to follow through.
James Walkinshaw.speaks: Pace runs markedly slow, slower than most, with pauses that run longer than most and a volume that swings up and down more than most. He often replies in rapid bursts of brief answers, and his answer length stays even. He trails off before finishing many thoughts, and his phrasing cuts sharper than nearly any colleague's. Hearings find him among the least combative figures.
James Walkinshaw.decides: He appraises a request by how well it serves real people, and outside voices can shift him more than most colleagues. With only a few issue areas, his commitments stay narrow. Accounts of the people it reaches land best with him. He ranks near the bottom on following bills to passage, so a commitment holds only when it carries a named date.

archetype.justification: Ranking near the top for curiosity, and broad in his bills and talk, he fits the Owl's style.

Jamie Raskin.bottom_line: Get your point in early and hold your ground when he challenges you. Pressure from outside reaches him less than most, so win on the argument, not the crowd.
do: Share written technical evidence before the meeting so he can check it
When he defends a point, answer with the source document
Let his fast opening run, then pick the one point to answer
dont: In a hearing, expect combat and keep each answer short
Skip any plan that hides his name from the announcement
Jamie Raskin.warning_sign: He usually takes the floor and keeps talking until his point is made. If he yields the floor and lets others speak, he is weighing the point, so stop pressing and ask which claim he doubts.
Jamie Raskin.follow_up: Email his legislative director the sources and the one page brief before Friday, with a short list of open points.
Jamie Raskin.personality: Raskin ranks near the top for outgoing talk and curiosity, and he leads the room in conversation much more than most. Forceful phrasing runs somewhat more than most through his words, and he digs in when pressed. His talk spans a broad set of subjects, more so than most, and his bills reach many areas. Among the most prominent members for his rank, his public profile is high.
Jamie Raskin.speaks: He speaks somewhat faster than most, and his answers stretch out, with the longest ones going much longer than most in the room. His loudness varies somewhat more than most while his pitch sits somewhat flatter than most. Speech carries a bit more filler than most, and his phrasing runs more forceful than most. Pauses come shorter than most, so the exchange leaves others less room.
Jamie Raskin.decides: An ask earns his backing by holding up well when tested. Outside pressure reaches him less than most, and his bills cover a much broader set of areas than most, so a narrow ask tends to lose his attention. Written evidence that anticipates his challenges is what moves him, so an ask earns his commitment only after it survives his pushback.

archetype.justification: Diligent and detailed in public words, fairly reliable at seeing bills through, with a low profile in the chamber.

Janelle Bynum.bottom_line: Bring a detailed case that her community can back, since outside voices move her more than most. Give her time to check the detail, because she is slow and thorough.
do: Bring the people in her community who back the ask
Give her time to check each detail before deciding
Ask for a dated follow-up she can check against the record
dont: Expect a quick yes from her in a crowded room
Count on a fast hearing exchange to change her mind
Janelle Bynum.warning_sign: Usually she is outgoing and speaks slowly, so a change in manner stands out. If she gets combative during a session, she has gone on guard over the point, so ask what concern she is protecting.
Janelle Bynum.follow_up: Then mail a brief recap naming the agreed step, its owner, and a date she can check.
Janelle Bynum.personality: Bynum is a very outgoing Oregon member whose descriptions of the work are notably careful and detailed. Her public talk stays on a small set of issues, and her bills are fairly dependable as they move through. She keeps a low profile in the chamber, yet she reacts strongly and quickly, more than most in the House. Outside voices move her more than typical, so backing from her community counts.
Janelle Bynum.speaks: Her pace is slow, but her gaps between phrases are brief. Volume swings widely from sentence to sentence, and pitch is a little flatter than typical. Her words are careful and detailed about the work, and her talk stays on a small set of issues. In a hearing she is much less combative than peers. Her recorded delivery comes from the House floor, so it may differ in a committee room.
Janelle Bynum.decides: How carefully its detail holds up, and whether her community backs it, is what she considers. A coalition of local voices shapes her view, and voices from outside tilt her more than typical. Her follow-through is fairly reliable once she commits, so a dated step gives the commitment a place to land. So an ask built on detail and local backing is what gets her yes.

archetype.justification: He is very reserved, more careful and organized than nearly any colleague, and his public profile sits a bit lower than most, which fits a patient pace.

Jared Golden.bottom_line: Offer a shared role to announce with others, and lead with the support he has. Outside voices count for less with him, so the ask must stand on its own.
do: Offer a shared role he can announce with colleagues
Give him time to finish, since his pace runs slow
Confirm the next step in writing before leaving
dont: Assume a cross aisle deal will hold without a reminder
Rush him toward a decision before he has finished
Jared Golden.warning_sign: Usually he runs a little more combative when he is in a hearing than most members. If he grows more combative and presses the detail, he is concerned, so bring the written record back.
Jared Golden.follow_up: After the meeting, send him a short written note listing the shared role, the agreed next step and its date, copied to his legislative director.
Jared Golden.personality: Golden is among the most curious colleagues, and he thinks with care and order. He is very reserved in manner, and his public profile sits a bit lower than most. He reaches across the aisle much more than most colleagues, though he trails most colleagues at seeing bills through. Together these traits make him a deliberate cross aisle builder who wants a shared role and a written record.
Jared Golden.speaks: His pace is among the slowest in the House, and his pauses run longer than almost anyone's. His volume swings up and down more than most, and his pitch shifts more than most. In hearings he runs a little more combative than most members. His delivery is deliberate, with points arriving in spaced steps rather than rapid exchanges, and his words give little sign of haste.
Jared Golden.decides: He weighs an ask by whether a shared role lets him stand with colleagues, and pressure from outside counts for less with him than with most members. Because he works across the aisle, a request with cross aisle sponsors fits his pattern. His follow through is somewhat less reliable than most, so a commitment holds when a named person tracks its date. He tends to credit colleagues who share the work.

archetype.justification: His sharper than usual wording, careful organization and facts first framing fit a bull that goes straight at the point.

Jared Huffman.bottom_line: Lead with the results in a short, direct case, since he tends to push harder than most when a point is contested.
do: Open with the outcome the bill delivers, in two sentences
Let a direct disagreement stand, then return to the facts
Ask him to name the one result the bill must deliver
dont: Stack extra asks on a bill that is already contested
Jared Huffman.warning_sign: Usually his words are sharp and he speaks somewhat slowly. If his pauses stretch further and his wording turns flat, he is deciding whether to fight or to dismiss your point. Then ask one plain question about the bill.
Jared Huffman.follow_up: Mail him a brief note covering the exact bill step, the reason it matters and the date you need a reply.
Jared Huffman.personality: Huffman is careful and organized, and his public language runs with heavier emotion than nearly any colleague's. Work across the aisle is much rarer for him than for most colleagues, and his legislation spans somewhat more topics than most. When a hearing turns adversarial, he is among the sharpest questioners in the chamber. Before public office, his career was spent as a consumer lawyer on public interest cases, and he represents California.
Jared Huffman.speaks: His pace runs a little slower than most, and his pauses stretch much longer than most, so his points land deliberately. His wording cuts harder than usual and carries heavy emotional weight. Even on routine subjects his talk stays hard-edged rather than soft. At hearings, he ranks among the sharpest voices in the chamber, and his volume swings more than most.
Jared Huffman.decides: Before he backs anything he checks whether the facts show what the policy delivers, and a case built on results moves him more than an appeal to values. Support from across the aisle is thin for him, so a request that needs it faces a hard road. Pressure from outside groups registers with him a little less than with most colleagues. So a yes comes from the case itself and holds only while it stays on evidence he can verify.

archetype.descriptor: warm and hard to pin down
archetype.justification: His public words run warmer than nearly everyone's, yet few are less reliable at voting and bill follow-through.

Jared Moskowitz.bottom_line: Build the case on what the policy delivers, in a short and direct way. He reaches across the aisle more than almost anyone, so show who already backs the ask.
do: Bring the policy results and the facts in one short document
Invite him to restate the key point whenever filler buries it
Ask for a plain yes or no, since his words are much softer than most
Check which bills he has moved before you ask him
dont: Argue over small points while the main case waits
Treat his warm tone as proof he will carry the ask
Give up your point at his first objection
Jared Moskowitz.warning_sign: In hearings he usually presses witnesses hard, so a shift in tone stands out. When he stops jabbing and turns polite, he has stopped weighing your plan closely. Stop pressing and ask which single fact would settle his question.
Jared Moskowitz.follow_up: Email his office within two days a short note that answers the point he defends hardest.
Jared Moskowitz.personality: Moskowitz is outgoing, and few House members are more so. His role keeps him much more in view than most. His public tone is among the warmest in the chamber. In hearings, few members press witnesses harder than he does. His bills touch more subject areas than most, and he builds ties across party lines further than almost every House colleague. Detail work is not where he shines, and few are less reliable at casting votes and moving bills.
Jared Moskowitz.speaks: In interviews his answers stretch out, and his longest replies outlast nearly every colleague's. His short replies often arrive in quick bursts, well more than most. His pace runs a notch quick. Filler crowds his talk more than nearly any colleague does. Return to the core point after each long answer so the thread holds, and keep the document in view.
Jared Moskowitz.decides: Results and facts are the frame that fits him best, so keep the case plain and specific. When he has settled on a view, he holds it and defends it, so bring the case before his view hardens. Pressure from outside moves him much more than most members, and persistence pays. Because his follow-through is weak, get his yes in writing and confirm the next vote.

archetype.justification: She speaks loosely about details, leads conversations more than most, and holds her ground harder than nearly any colleague.

Jasmine Crockett.bottom_line: Lead with the written case and one clear ask, and let her finish. She defends her position hard and her answers run long, so interruptions will lose the room.
do: Circulate the written technical case the week before
Give her space to finish long answers before replying
Ask her to name a date for the vote she commits to
Confirm each commitment she makes in writing the same day
dont: Interrupt her mid-answer, even when you disagree
Count on her to soften when challenged
Jasmine Crockett.warning_sign: She usually talks at length and keeps the floor through a challenge. If she starts trailing off or defending each point harder, she is on guard and the exchange is turning. Stop, restate your one point, and let her answer it.
Jasmine Crockett.follow_up: Within two days, give her staff one page that lays out the bill's dated next steps and names an owner for each.
Jasmine Crockett.personality: Crockett sits among the most outgoing members and among the most skeptical. Speech runs loosely about details and gets heated quickly, more than most. Wording reads much cooler than most, and conversations tilt toward her grip on the floor more than nearly any colleague's. Bills get seen through much less reliably than most. Answers run long, and filler appears far more often than most. Texas is the state she represents.
Jasmine Crockett.speaks: Long answers, filled with runs of filler, stretch out her points with pauses between them. Pitch runs flatter than nearly any colleague's, and wording carries more emotional charge than typical. Her descriptions of work carry less careful detail than nearly any colleague offers. When challenged, she holds her ground, and her sentences often trail off. Listeners get long passages rather than tight summaries.
Jasmine Crockett.decides: She weighs an ask on its merits, and public campaigns sway her clearly less than they sway most colleagues. Pressure will not carry the vote, so the case has to make sense to her on its own terms. She sees bills through much less reliably than most, so a decision needs a dated vote and a named owner to hold.

archetype.justification: He is much more focused on action than most, gives long answers, and holds his ground when pressed.

Jason Crow.bottom_line: Bring a concrete action plan with next steps named. He holds his line when challenged, so bring facts he can defend.
do: Lead with the action steps, then the evidence behind each
Share a visible joint announcement he can front
Ask him to name the next step in the room
dont: Treat a challenge as a sign he is closed off
Stack more points on the table when he pushes back
Jason Crow.warning_sign: He usually answers at length, with filler, and he holds his ground once challenged. If he slows down and stops pushing back, he is weighing a concession, not digging in. Name one next step in a line and let him respond.
Jason Crow.follow_up: Forward a concise note clearly listing the action items and their owners, with each due date.
Jason Crow.personality: Crow is outgoing and curious, and he works in a very careful, well organized way. He ranks among the highest for visibility, and his bills range across more topics than most. He defends his position across shows, gives long and upbeat answers, and comes across as warm. Though he reaches over to the other camp somewhat more than most, follow through is a little weaker than most. In the room he is energetic and pushes hard on the points he defends.
Jason Crow.speaks: He talks faster than nearly any member in the House, with pauses a little shorter than most. Volume is less varied than most, and pitch swings much more than most. Words come out warm and upbeat, and answers run long but stay even in length. He also relies on filler words a bit more than most. At hearings he is as pointed as almost anyone.
Jason Crow.decides: A request gets judged on the action it yields and how it dovetails with the work he is already doing. Pressure from outside reaches him more than most, so broad backing carries weight with him. He defends positions he has argued across shows, so an ask he has taken on is hard to walk back. An ask without a named owner gets argued down before it moves.

archetype.justification: His reserved manner, skeptical streak and narrow issue focus fit an independent operator who keeps a tight focus.

Jason Smith.bottom_line: Bring a short case built on technical support, since outside voices have less sway over him than over colleagues.
do: Share the written technical evidence before the meeting
Frame the ask around a concrete action he can take
Give him room to take the lead in the discussion
dont: Press him for a fast yes in the room
Rely on promises alone to move a bill forward
Jason Smith.warning_sign: He usually keeps his answers at an even length, so an even rhythm is normal. If his replies suddenly run long and uneven, he has grown wary, so pause, restate the one ask, and offer a concrete action.
Jason Smith.follow_up: Once the session ends, send him a brief technical summary with the one action he can take, and ask him to confirm by a set date.
Jason Smith.personality: Smith comes across as somewhat reserved and a little skeptical, yet he keeps a careful, organized streak, so his caution reads as method rather than doubt. His legislation touches only a handful of issue areas, one of the narrowest slates in the House. His public talk covers a narrow set of topics but goes into more careful detail than colleagues. Bills he backs usually make it through to a vote. He is fairly visible in the House, and he represents Missouri.
Jason Smith.speaks: Language from him is noticeably upbeat, action focused, and a bit more social than colleagues. He comes across as less forceful than colleagues. His answers run a little longer than colleagues on average, but they stay even in length. Interviews often come in rapid, brief exchanges, and his longest answers run a bit shorter than colleagues'. Those are patterns in his public language and delivery.
Jason Smith.decides: Each ask gets sized up by how cleanly it sits among the few issues he already works on, since his bills touch only a handful of issue areas. His skeptical streak means he wants technical support before he commits. Outside voices have less sway over him than over colleagues. He backs bills that reach a vote, so a decision needs a clear action and a date to hold.

archetype.justification: Few colleagues are quieter than he is, yet he is very careful and among the most dependable on votes and bill follow-through.

Jay Obernolte.bottom_line: Keep the request to one clear step. Few members see their bills through more reliably than he does.
do: Confirm the meeting time and room a day ahead
Lead with the single sentence that states the ask
Schedule the next contact before he decides, since pressure counts for more with him
Look up his recent votes on bills like yours before you make the ask
dont: Expect him to carry the ask in public for you
Pile extra questions onto him in hearings, since he is more combative there
Second-guess a yes once he has given it
Jay Obernolte.warning_sign: In hearings he usually presses a little more than most, so a softer tone stands out. When he softens, ask which staff member will carry the ask forward, and get that name before you go.
Jay Obernolte.follow_up: Two days after the meeting, email his office a dated recap that names the ask, each step's owner, and the next date.
Jay Obernolte.personality: Obernolte is chair of his party's House policy committee and keeps a quiet, low-key manner. He is hard to rattle, much more than most members, and he keeps a much lower public profile than most. He sees bills through more reliably than almost anyone, and he is fairly curious. Careful and organized, he is very precise with detail. For his role, few members are less visible in the House.
Jay Obernolte.speaks: On the House floor his pitch sits flatter than nearly every colleague's. His volume stays a bit more even than most. His pace runs a notch slower than most, while his pauses come a bit shorter than most. In formal settings, give him a beat before the next point, and keep your own tempo slow. Keep your questions short and in order, so each one gets its own answer.
Jay Obernolte.decides: Outside pressure counts for more with him than with most House members, so repeated, well-timed contact can shift his position. Keep each contact tied to the same request, and log the date of every contact. Before each one, ask his staff which outside voice reached him last, and plan around it. Let each contact add one new outside voice, not a repeat of the last.

archetype.justification: Very social and forceful in her words, she leads with people and community stories, and speaks quicker than nearly anyone.

Jeanne Shaheen.bottom_line: Lead with the people your ask helps, because pressure from outside moves her less than most and the case has to carry it.
do: Mirror her social style, since her words run very social and forceful
Check the bill's status before each vote, since she follows through much less
Match her quick pace, and hear out her longer answers before you reply
dont: Open with budget tables or dense charts
Assume outside pressure alone will settle the vote
Jeanne Shaheen.warning_sign: She usually finishes her sentences, so a trailing one is a clear change. Once she starts trailing off in the middle of a point, she has grown wary, so stop pushing, give her room, and ask which part concerns her.
Jeanne Shaheen.follow_up: Send a written note on the people helped, with a date for each next step, within a week.
Jeanne Shaheen.personality: Shaheen is very reserved in manner, yet she is fairly agreeable. She is also very hard to rattle. Her language is very social and forceful, and she talks about her work with much more feeling than most. Across subjects, her talk ranges somewhat wider than most, but her bills touch much fewer areas. Seeing bills through and voting are much less reliable for her than for most.
Jeanne Shaheen.speaks: Speech comes among the quickest in the chamber, with much shorter pauses between phrases. Her pitch swings somewhat more than most, while interview answers from her run longer than most. She is among the least inclined to leave a sentence trailing. Language is very forceful and carries much feeling, and she covers a somewhat wider spread of topics. Words run somewhat flatter than most, so the force comes from pace and phrasing.
Jeanne Shaheen.decides: She starts from the people an ask helps and from whether it sits inside issues she already covers. Outside pressure sways her less than it sways most, so the case itself has to decide, though pressure still counts for something. Since she sees bills through much less reliably than most, a yes from her holds only when someone keeps the work moving.

archetype.justification: He is very reserved, much less practical than most, and very reliable at seeing bills through, which fits a patient, methodical pace.

Jeff Crank.bottom_line: Bring a bill focused ask with a timeline he can hold you to. Outside voices shift him more than most colleagues, so pair the ask with voices from home.
do: Bring a bill focused ask with a clear timeline
Pair the ask with voices from home
Leave room in the pace, since he speaks slowly
dont: Assume his reserve means he is not interested
Treat a hearing as a fight, though he is less combative than most
Jeff Crank.warning_sign: Usually he is less combative in hearings, and his tone stays matter of fact. If he becomes more combative in a hearing and presses his point, he has turned guarded, so ease off and restate the timeline.
Jeff Crank.follow_up: Afterward, mail him a brief memo laying out the agreed timeline and owner, and within two days copy his legislative director.
Jeff Crank.personality: Crank is very reserved and much less practical than most, and his public focus runs narrow. Details are less his focus, far looser than most colleagues', and he describes his own work with somewhat less care than most. His legislation spans a very narrow range of policy areas, yet he is very reliable at seeing bills through. Before taking office he spent years as a congressional staffer, and his public approach reads as direct.
Jeff Crank.speaks: He speaks a little slower than most, and his pitch varies much less than most. Volume swings up and down more than most. A narrow range of topics comes through in his talk, fewer than almost anyone's, and his work gets somewhat less care than most. In hearings he tends less toward combat than most members, and his tone stays matter of fact.
Jeff Crank.decides: He judges an ask by how reliably it can be carried through, and outside voices shift him more than most colleagues. His legislation spans a very narrow set of issue areas, and a request inside those areas fits him best. Because he sees bills through reliably, a commitment from him tends to hold, so a dated next step is the thing to secure.

archetype.justification: Among the most agreeable members in the chamber, he seldom takes charge of a conversation.

Jeff Hurd.bottom_line: Come with one clear ask and let him reach his own view. A challenge makes him defend his position harder, so give him time to think.
do: Ask him an open question early so he can join in
Give him time to answer before you add a second point
If he pauses between phrases, let the pause run before you speak
dont: Treat a short reply as agreement
Assume he will concede a point when challenged
Jeff Hurd.warning_sign: He usually answers at a moderate length, so a long, drawn out reply is a change. If he starts defending his position at length, slow down and ask what he is weighing.
Jeff Hurd.follow_up: Send him a one page note with the ask, the reason and the next step by Friday.
Jeff Hurd.personality: Hurd is reserved and among the most agreeable members in the chamber, so he avoids taking charge of a conversation. His public words run much narrower than most, but his public account of his work is careful and detailed. Much more upbeat and social than most, his language still carries less force than almost anyone's. He answers in short runs, and when challenged he defends his point at length.
Jeff Hurd.speaks: He speaks at a somewhat quicker clip than most colleagues, and his pauses between phrases run longer than almost anyone's. His answers run short, and his longest replies are much shorter than most. Force in his words runs much lower than almost anyone's, and his tone rises and falls much more than most. When challenged, he defends his point somewhat more than most colleagues.
Jeff Hurd.decides: He weighs an ask against his own reading of the issue, and once challenged he defends that reading. Pressure from outside reaches him more than it reaches most members, so allies who back the ask can shift him. He is somewhat reliable at seeing bills through, so an ask with a clear next step can stick. A decision from him therefore comes only after he has tested the facts for himself.

archetype.justification: His curiosity ranks very high, with fairly careful habits and bills that touch somewhat more issue areas than most.

Jeff Merkley.bottom_line: Let him test the evidence before he agrees, since his curiosity runs high and outside groups move him more than most members.
do: Send the evidence file ahead, since he wants to test it
Expect him to defend his view, and answer each point in turn
Point to a bill he already joined with the other party
dont: Read his defense of a point as a closed door
Press him for a yes before he has tested the evidence
Count his public visibility as support for the ask
Jeff Merkley.warning_sign: He usually talks fast with very short pauses and defends his position hard. So when he slows and leaves long gaps, he is weighing your point rather than digging in. Let him finish, then ask about the part he has not answered.
Jeff Merkley.follow_up: When the meeting concludes, hand his staff a single sheet listing the points he agreed to test, with a date to report back.
Jeff Merkley.personality: Merkley numbers among the most curious people in his chamber, and he is somewhat more outgoing than most. Reaching across the aisle comes somewhat more easily to him than most, and he is somewhat careful in how he organizes detail. The bills he backs touch somewhat more issue areas than most, and his words carry very little emotional charge. When challenged he holds his ground much more than most, and in hearings he argues with much less edge than most.
Jeff Merkley.speaks: He talks at a fast clip, with very short pauses between phrases, and his pitch rises and drops more than nearly anyone's. His volume swings a great deal, and his wording runs a little more upbeat than most. When pushed, he digs in harder than most and keeps a firm line.
