His word choice is a little less forceful than most, so the firmness comes through in repetition rather than force.
Jeff Merkley.decides: How well a request holds up under testing is what he considers, since his curiosity runs high. Outside groups push him harder than most members do, so pressure from them is what moves a decision. His bills reach somewhat more areas than most, so a request within his lanes sits well. Because he sees his bills through somewhat more than most, a dated written commitment is what keeps him to it.

archetype.justification: Very outgoing and much more careful in detail than most, with a narrow issue range, which fits a practical, focused style.

Jefferson Shreve.bottom_line: Bring one practical ask and set a concrete next step, since his bills tend to reach the finish.
do: Offer a visible shared role he can announce with you
Let him finish each point before you respond, since his pauses run long
Agree a dated next step and confirm it by email
dont: Lean on outside pressure to force a quick vote
Open with a sweeping vision that outruns the specifics
Jefferson Shreve.warning_sign: A mild exchange is normal for him, since he is usually a bit less combative than most colleagues in a hearing. Should he turn terse and stop engaging, he has put his guard up, so ease off and ask which detail he still needs.
Jefferson Shreve.follow_up: Email his staff two days after you meet, naming the agreed step, who owns it, and a due date.
Jefferson Shreve.personality: Shreve comes across as very outgoing and fairly careful and organized, going into real detail whenever he describes his work. His public talk stays on a narrow set of issues, and his legislation touches somewhat fewer topics than most. Hearings find him a bit less combative than most colleagues, and his votes and his follow through on bills are fairly dependable.
Jefferson Shreve.speaks: His public talk stays on a narrow set of issues and goes into careful, detailed terms about each one. Pace runs a touch slower than most colleagues, he pauses a little longer, and his volume swings much more than most. His pitch moves a little more than most colleagues', which gives his delivery an emphatic swing. In hearings he is a bit less combative than most colleagues, so his tone there is less pointed.
Jefferson Shreve.decides: An ask fits him best when it sits inside the areas he already works in and the next step is clear. Pressure from outside reaches him a little less than most colleagues, so a shared role he can announce with you counts for more. His follow through is dependable enough that a written, dated step tends to hold. So he decides on the record in front of him rather than on who is pushing.

archetype.justification: Fairly outgoing, a little skeptical, and quick to press a point in formal hearings.

Jefferson Van Drew.bottom_line: Send technical evidence early, since outside pressure moves him more than almost any member, so the case needs checkable detail.
do: Share the technical detail before the meeting so it can be checked
Bring outside voices who back the ask, since they carry real weight with him
In a hearing, expect pointed questions, since he is more combative there
dont: Assume a yes vote will carry through, since his follow through on bills lags
Treat a firm position as final, since outside voices can shift him
Jefferson Van Drew.warning_sign: Usually he is outgoing and a little skeptical. If his words suddenly sharpen, read it as guardedness, so ease up and answer each doubt with the technical detail he asked for.
Jefferson Van Drew.follow_up: Send the technical detail in writing by Friday, naming who will answer each open question.
Jefferson Van Drew.personality: Van Drew is outgoing and a little skeptical, and he covers a broad set of topics. His talk about details is looser than most, and he is easily stirred. His role keeps him fairly visible. At hearings he turns more combative, and finishing bills is less reliable for him than for most, and his backing needs watching. Outside pressure carries real pull with him, which shapes how his support should be secured.
Jefferson Van Drew.speaks: He speaks in an outgoing way, and his words carry strong feeling. His talk about details is looser than most, and his questions in exchanges come with some edge. In a hearing he turns more combative, and his manner becomes more pointed, which means the room should expect a sharper tone there. Expect candor from him rather than softness in formal settings, and plan for direct questions on each figure.
Jefferson Van Drew.decides: Technical facts laid out in advance are what he weighs most heavily. Outside pressure moves him more than almost any member, so a push from outside groups can shift his position. His legislation covers a broader spread of topics than most, so a request within his own fields lands best. Because his follow through on bills tends to lag, his yes holds only when someone owns the next step.

archetype.justification: Few colleagues match her bill follow-through, and she is quite reserved in public.

Jennifer Kiggans.bottom_line: Lead with the people the policy helps, and ask for a next step with a date attached. Few members match how dependable she is on bills.
do: Bring short stories about who the policy helps, with names left out
Open with a brief greeting before you turn to the ask
Name a bill she has seen through, as a sign the next step is realistic
Close by confirming the one next step she has agreed to
dont: Fill the room with extra speakers
Count on press coverage to carry the ask, since her profile is lower than most
Read her reserve as disinterest, since she is among the most reliable on bills
Jennifer Kiggans.warning_sign: Usually, in hearings, she runs somewhat more combative than most members. If she goes quiet on a point she usually presses, she is weighing it, not agreeing. Ask which part of the case she would check first before you leave.
Jennifer Kiggans.follow_up: Within a day, write her staff a summary that names each step, its owner, and the due date.
Jennifer Kiggans.personality: Kiggans ranks among the most reliable members on bills in the House. She keeps a careful, organized approach, and her public talk about her work is much more detailed than nearly any colleague's. The public manner is quite reserved, and the outlook is a little practical. Her language is much more emotionally charged than most, and her bills touch on a smaller range of issues than most. She sits lower than most in public visibility.
Jennifer Kiggans.speaks: On the House floor she runs somewhat slower than most, with somewhat shorter gaps between phrases. Her pitch is much flatter than most, and her volume swings less than most. Put the detail on your projects in writing, since her public words are more exact and detailed than almost anyone's. All of her recorded audio comes from the floor, so these points describe floor delivery only.
Jennifer Kiggans.decides: She responds to a case about the people the policy helps, which fits her best. Pressure from outside sways her more than most colleagues do, and a clear, repeated ask keeps the issue alive. Her follow-through ranks among the strongest, so a written yes from her carries real weight. Give her one short written page she can check line by line, so the yes is easy to confirm.

archetype.justification: Bridges the aisle far more than most, and is less easily rattled than most, which fits a cooperative, easygoing approach.

Jennifer McClellan.bottom_line: Ask for one shared commitment and frame it around who is helped, since she works across the aisle far more than most.
do: Open with the people your bill would help before the numbers
Name the bipartisan colleagues who already share the goal
Let her finish a pause before you jump in
dont: Rely on her record across the aisle alone to close the deal
Read her gentle tone in hearings as agreement with your position
Jennifer McClellan.warning_sign: At a hearing she tends to be gentle, so a firm answer will not read as hostility by default. If her questions turn pointed, she is losing patience, so stop and ask what she needs.
Jennifer McClellan.follow_up: Afterward mail her office a concise summary of the shared commitment naming who owns each step and when it falls due.
Jennifer McClellan.personality: McClellan is a cooperative and easygoing legislator who works across the aisle far more than most colleagues. She is organized and fairly careful, and less easily rattled than most colleagues. Public talk centers on a limited range of topics and seldom dwells on detail or strong feeling. Her votes and bill follow through are a little less reliable than most colleagues, so cooperation shows up more in her coalitions than in her paperwork.
Jennifer McClellan.speaks: Her public words feel low in emotional heat compared with nearly any colleague, and they stay on a narrow range of issues. Her delivery is slow, with long gaps between phrases and a pitch that stays flatter than most. During hearings she stays among the least combative members, so her questioning tends to be courteous rather than pointed. Her manner is even and plain throughout.
Jennifer McClellan.decides: Before backing it she judges how well it serves the people it would help and whether it wins support across the aisle. Her follow through is a little less reliable than most, so a commitment needs an owner and a date to hold. Formal settings bring out her gentler side, since in hearings she counts among the least combative members. So a shared commitment holds only once someone owns the next step.

archetype.justification: His public words read much sharper than most, and he is much more combative when hearings start, so he tends to lead the exchange.

Jerrold Nadler.bottom_line: Keep the ask short, with one next step he can own. He gives among the shortest answers, so a clear ask with a date will get a usable reply.
do: Ask one short question and let him finish his reply
Offer a shared announcement he can front with local partners
Expect him to skip filler and go straight to the point
dont: Treat his short answers as disinterest
Count on outside pressure to carry the decision
Jerrold Nadler.warning_sign: He usually uses almost no filler, so a run of filler words in his answers is a change. If he takes over the discussion, slow down and ask what matters most to him.
Jerrold Nadler.follow_up: By Friday, send a one page memo covering the ask, its pending step, and whoever owns it.
Jerrold Nadler.personality: Nadler is very reserved and very skeptical, but hearings bring out a much more combative side in him than in most members. He is somewhat careful with detail and somewhat quicker to get worked up than most. Conversations come under his control a little more than most, and phrasing cuts much sharper than most. Public profile sits among the most prominent of any member, and he speaks with somewhat more force than most.
Jerrold Nadler.speaks: His answers run among the shortest in the House, and his longest replies are much shorter than most. In interviews, answer length runs much shorter than most, and it varies somewhat more than most. He trails off somewhat less than most, and filler barely shows up, lower than nearly anyone's. His volume shifts less than almost anyone's, and his pauses between phrases run much longer than most.
Jerrold Nadler.decides: Requests get checked against his own read of the issue, and he takes charge of the room while doing so. Outside pressure moves him less than nearly any member, so the case has to stand on its own merits. A visible shared announcement fits him, but only once the substance is clear. Being very skeptical, he commits only when the facts are settled, so a decision from him comes with an owner already named.

archetype.justification: He is quite reserved, very careful and organized, and hard to rattle.

Jerry Moran.bottom_line: Come with a short, reasoned case and a bipartisan partner in view, and leave with a named next step.
do: Bring a short, reasoned memo with the exact bill language
Work with a bipartisan cosponsor before you make the ask
Let him finish his long answers before you respond
Keep the request low key, since his public exposure runs short of his role
dont: Mistake his long replies for evasion, since they run longer than most
Interrupt him mid sentence, since he tends to finish his replies
Assume a hearing will feel confrontational, since he is much less combative there
Jerry Moran.warning_sign: He usually talks at length, so a sudden break in his flow stands out. If he suddenly halts mid thought or his tone turns sharp, he has become guarded, so ask one question and wait.
Jerry Moran.follow_up: Mail his office a single page digest of the agreed action and its owner by Friday.
Jerry Moran.personality: Moran is quite reserved, very careful, and hard to rattle. His wording is much gentler than most colleagues. When he describes his own work, he gives more detail than nearly any colleague. His work across party lines trails most colleagues. On bills and votes he trails most colleagues a bit. His public exposure runs short of what his role suggests. He represents Kansas in the Senate.
Jerry Moran.speaks: His answers are lengthier than typical, and his longest replies stretch much longer still. His public wording reads as cooler than nearly any colleague's, yet it reads upbeat. In hearings his tone runs milder than most members. He keeps his sentences complete and rarely trails off, so his delivery sounds finished. Overall, his wording sounds sociable and far less focused on action than most.
Jerry Moran.decides: Requests are checked closely for fit with his own camp's priorities, since his crossover ties trail most colleagues. Bill and vote follow up trails most colleagues somewhat, so commitments need someone tracking them. In hearings his tone runs milder, so formal questioning rarely unsettles him. His public exposure stays short of his role, so an ask lands on its substance.

archetype.justification: His public wording cuts sharper than nearly anyone's, his bills span more policy areas than nearly anyone's, and his words carry a good deal of feeling.

Jesús García.bottom_line: Carry the follow-up yourself, since he is much less reliable on bills than most members.
do: Answer his sharpest points in plain words, without matching his edge
When his voice rises, return to the one point, since follow-through is weak
Open by naming the vote or step you need from him
dont: Rely on a public event as the main lever for the ask
Count on cross-party backing to carry the ask
Jesús García.warning_sign: Usually his public wording cuts harder than nearly anyone's in the House. If it turns even sharper than that, the back-and-forth has become a contest. Lower your own tone and slow your next reply.
Jesús García.follow_up: Within a day, send his staff a short written recap of each agreed step, with the person who owns it.
Jesús García.personality: García is one of the widest-ranging members in the House, and his bills span more policy areas than nearly anyone's. He describes his work in much looser terms than most, while his public wording is more pointed than nearly anyone's. His words carry a good deal more feeling than most. Few members build less across party lines than he does, and he trails most colleagues on seeing bills through. His public profile runs somewhat lower than most colleagues'.
Jesús García.speaks: In short clips, his pace runs quicker than nearly anyone's in the House. Pauses between phrases come shorter than almost anyone's. Pitch moves up and down more than nearly anyone's, and his volume shifts somewhat more than most. His talk ranges across more subjects than nearly anyone's, and his descriptions of his work come out looser than most. Taken together, his delivery is fast and varied, with few long gaps.
Jesús García.decides: His follow-through on bills runs much weaker than most, so check where his earlier bills stand before you meet. Bring their current status into the room, so the talk starts from what has actually happened. Ask whether any of them has reached a committee vote since, and what it would take to move it next. Name the bills that matter most for your ask, so the status check stays short.

archetype.justification: Gentler than most and people focused, quick in delivery, and among the most agreeable members.

Jill Tokuda.bottom_line: Lead with the people your ask helps and work across the aisle, since she is a notably agreeable member.
do: Bring stories of who is helped, since people and community impact fits her best
Share the wider context of your ask, since she is among the most curious members
In a hearing, expect her to push harder than in conversation
dont: Stay silent for long stretches, since she fills silences quickly
Treat her yes as final, since outside groups sway her a bit more
Jill Tokuda.warning_sign: Usually she is gentle, agreeable and quick in speech, so a change stands out. If her words sharpen, she is on guard, so slow down and name the people your ask would help.
Jill Tokuda.follow_up: Send her staff a short summary of who the ask helps and by when, and name one owner for each step.
Jill Tokuda.personality: Tokuda is outgoing and among the most curious members. She is among the most agreeable members. Across the aisle she works somewhat more than most, and her tone is gentle. She covers a broader spread of topics than most, and her words carry strong feeling. In hearings she pushes harder than in conversation, which shows in her probing. Her manner is open, and she responds well to people who share her goals.
Jill Tokuda.speaks: Her pace is much faster than most, and her pauses between phrases are much shorter, so she moves quickly from point to point. Volume varies more than most, while pitch stays much flatter than most. Her words are gentle, and she talks about a broader spread of topics with less detail than most. In hearings she pushes harder and presses her points.
Jill Tokuda.decides: She weighs an ask by who it helps and whether it draws support from both sides. She is among the most agreeable members, so a bipartisan path draws her in. Bills she sponsors cover a broader spread of issues, so an ask inside her areas fits best. Outside groups can sway her a bit more than most, so her commitment holds only while backers stay engaged.

archetype.justification: Few senators are as skeptical as he is, and his details run looser than typical.

Jim Banks.bottom_line: Give him the written case early and a bipartisan partner he can see, since public pressure carries extra weight with him.
do: Put the technical case in writing first, since that suits how he decides
Name a bipartisan partner, since he is skeptical and works across party lines
Keep pace with his quick delivery, since his answers run long and fast
In hearings, expect fewer sharp exchanges and prepare for long answers
dont: Count on fast follow through, since he is skeptical and ranks low on bills
Cut in during his long answers, since his replies run far past typical
Rely on private assurances alone, since public pressure carries extra weight with him
Jim Banks.warning_sign: He usually speaks in an even run of words, so a break in that rhythm stands out. If he suddenly turns quiet in a hearing, he has become wary, so ask one specific question.
Jim Banks.follow_up: Write his office a brief message with the agreed next step, its owner, and a date by Friday.
Jim Banks.personality: Banks is fairly outgoing, quite practical, and among the most skeptical senators. Getting worked up comes easily to him, well beyond the typical colleague. When he describes his work, he offers few detailed specifics, well below nearly any senator. His work across party lines runs a notch ahead of most colleagues. Indiana is the state he represents. His issue range stays narrow, and he is less curious than most.
Jim Banks.speaks: His delivery runs well above typical pace, with much shorter pauses between phrases. Pitch rises and falls well above typical, and volume stays among the most even in the chamber. He answers in long, even runs of words, and his longest replies run past typical. Unfinished sentences show up in his replies well beyond typical levels. In hearings his tone runs milder than most, and he rarely presses witnesses.
Jim Banks.decides: He checks whether a request survives scrutiny, since he ranks with the most skeptical senators. His issue range stays narrow, so an ask tied to one area stands on firmer ground. Public pressure carries extra weight with him, so a bipartisan coalition can help. His follow through trails most colleagues somewhat, so a commitment needs someone tracking it after the vote.

archetype.justification: Holds the floor firmly, runs quick bursts of short replies and is very curious about the issues.

Jim Costa.bottom_line: Let him hold the floor for his first point, then leave with one dated next step he owns.
do: Give his first point the floor before you answer
Name a dated next step before he leaves the room
dont: Count on a verbal yes lasting through the next vote
Jim Costa.warning_sign: By default he trails off and his volume swings widely, while his pitch stays flat. If his sentences finish whole and his voice climbs, he is on guard or irritated. Ease off, restate the one ask, and let him answer.
Jim Costa.follow_up: After the meeting, send him a short written note restating the ask and the dated next step, copying the staff contact who owns it.
Jim Costa.personality: Costa is very curious and holds the floor firmly, yet his public words run cool and flat in tone. His bills get less follow through than nearly any colleague's, and he works across party lines less than most. Much of his wording is action focused, and his bills cover a fairly wide range of issues. In hearings he is far more combative than most, so pressing him directly raises the heat.
Jim Costa.speaks: His pace runs far slower than the typical colleague's, with long pauses between phrases and a volume that swings widely. Pitch stays flatter than nearly any colleague's, and his wording reads as far less forceful than most colleagues'. Replies arrive in bursts of brief turns, and he often trails off before a sentence ends. Public wording carries strong feeling, and it sits close to the surface.
Jim Costa.decides: He holds the floor when he takes it, but his follow through trails nearly every colleague's, so a commitment fades without a tracker. Pressure from outside shifts him far more than it shifts most colleagues, so the voices pressing him can change his answer. Bills he carries need someone else tracking them to keep moving. A decision sticks only with a named next step and a set date.

archetype.justification: Very loose with details, he takes charge of conversations and defends his position far more than most.

Jim Jordan.bottom_line: Put the written technical case in front of him first, since he defends positions hard once challenged.
do: Send the technical evidence ahead of time, not in the room
Let him take the floor, then answer in one tight point
Keep your own answers short, since his replies run tight
dont: Compete with him for the floor in a long exchange
Count on his bill follow through without a written date
Assume his skepticism means he will reject every ask
Jim Jordan.warning_sign: By default his words come out a little gentler than most, so a sharper edge from him usually means he has taken a point personally. Let him finish, then restate your one fact and stop arguing the point.
Jim Jordan.follow_up: Send a short written memo with the figures and the date for his decision, naming the staff contact who will track it.
Jim Jordan.personality: Jordan counts among the most outgoing and most skeptical members. Details come out loose, and his public talk narrows to a few areas. Follow through on bills is among the weakest in the House. He takes the lead in conversations and defends his position far more than most colleagues. Hearings find him among the most combative voices in the chamber, and few members are more visible for their role.
Jim Jordan.speaks: He talks among the fastest in the chamber, with very short pauses between phrases. Volume holds much more even than most, and pitch runs flatter than most too. Language runs much hotter than most in emotional terms, and he covers a narrow set of areas. Replies run much tighter than most, and bursts of them come far more often than usual.
Jim Jordan.decides: An ask has to survive a hard exchange to win him over, since he defends his position far more than most. He holds the floor, so an ask has to be stated before he takes over. Outside pressure sways him a bit less than most, so pressure alone will not carry an ask. His commitments hold only when a written date backs them.

archetype.justification: His forceful, somewhat sharp public words and firm hearing manner fit a direct legislator who holds his ground.

Jimmy Gomez.bottom_line: Open with who gains from the ask, and pin the vote to a date. Outside force moves him less, so the case itself has to carry it.
do: Anchor each point in a family the policy changes
Ask him to name the one vote he will commit to
Let him finish each answer before you add a point
dont: Treat a verbal yes as a committed vote
Read his somewhat sharp wording as a reason to escalate
Jimmy Gomez.warning_sign: Usually his words run somewhat sharp and his pitch stays flat, so a lift in tone is the signal. When his voice climbs sharply, he is reacting, so ease off, return to who your ask helps, and allow him to finish.
Jimmy Gomez.follow_up: Send him a single page note with the vote date and the name of the staffer who tracks it within two days.
Jimmy Gomez.personality: Gomez spans a broader spread of issues than most, yet his talk about his own work is much less careful and detailed than most colleagues. He leans a bit skeptical and gets heated more quickly than most, and his public words come across as forceful. Carrying bills to a vote is a clear weakness for him, and he stands out somewhat in the House.
Jimmy Gomez.speaks: He talks slowly and keeps a flat pitch, with shorter pauses between phrases than most. His replies come in shorter lengths than most, and they stay consistent, so he rarely gives long replies. Forceful and somewhat sharp words mark his public manner, and his volume swings a great deal. In hearings he is a bit more pointed than most, and in conversation he runs quick short replies less often.
Jimmy Gomez.decides: How a request fits the issues he already covers is his gauge, and he backs bills that stay within his broad agenda. Crowds and campaigns move him less than the case does, so the plan must carry the decision. Keeping bills on track is far harder for him, so any call must rest on a named vote date, and a vague date stalls him.

archetype.justification: He is very careful and among the most curious members in the House, and his bills reach much more issues than most.

Jimmy Panetta.bottom_line: Open the case with what the policy achieves, kept short and direct. Outside voices carry extra weight with him, more than most, so bring ones who back the outcome.
do: Name an outside backer of the outcome before the meeting starts
Open with the question the policy answers, not the process
Welcome his follow-up questions and answer each with the result it delivers
Close by naming the one result you will report back on
dont: Press him to front the bill, since he is much less in view than most
Lead with his cross-party record as proof of support
Stack several asks into one meeting, since he is less certain to see bills through
Jimmy Panetta.warning_sign: A warm, quiet meeting does not show whether he will act on your request. Before you leave, ask which single step he would take next, and offer written answers before the next meeting.
Jimmy Panetta.follow_up: Within a day, send his office a one-paragraph note on the outcome and the next step.
Jimmy Panetta.personality: Panetta is among the most curious members in the House and is very careful. His public language covers one of the widest ranges of issues in the House, and his bills reach much more issues than most. Cross-party work is much heavier for him than for most. Finishing bills is a bit less certain for him than for most. He is much less visible than most, and a bit less visible in his role. He is hard to fluster, much harder than most.
Jimmy Panetta.speaks: When he speaks on the House floor, he moves somewhat faster than most, with somewhat longer pauses between phrases. Pitch swings more than most in his delivery. His words carry one of the lowest levels of emotional charge in the House. He describes his work with a bit less care and detailed terms than most, so put the specifics in writing. These are floor patterns, so do not read his longer pauses as meeting pace. Keep your own points short so they are not lost.
Jimmy Panetta.decides: A case that delivers clear results fits how he decides. The results of the bill, stated in plain terms, are what the case rests on. He works across the aisle much more than most, so a bill with broad backing fits his record. He sees bills through less reliably than most, so name the vote he should commit to and the date you will check that vote.

archetype.justification: Very outgoing, a visible shared role frame and a warm, upbeat tone fit an Orca.

Jimmy Patronis.bottom_line: Build the ask around a shared announcement, then close with a named next step and its date.
do: Name him as co-lead on the announcement
Ask one short question and expect a short answer
Match his upbeat energy in your opening line
dont: Treat a verbal yes as the end of the work
Jimmy Patronis.warning_sign: By default his volume and pitch vary a fair amount, and he answers with upbeat energy. If he starts defending his position hard, he is on guard. Stay with the one ask and give him room to state his case.
Jimmy Patronis.follow_up: Following the session, mail him a brief memo that names the joint action, its deadline and the aide responsible for carrying it.
Jimmy Patronis.personality: Patronis comes across as very sociable and exceptionally agreeable, though his public words read as less social than most. Details sit loosely with him, and he rarely leads a discussion. His bills span very few issue areas, and his follow through is among the weakest in the chamber. His words are upbeat and brief. Few things rattle him. His public tone is warm, which makes him easy to approach.
Jimmy Patronis.speaks: Answers come shorter than nearly any colleague's, and the longest turns are the briefest in the chamber. Replies arrive in quick runs of brief turns, and the wording runs upbeat with plenty of energy. Delivery runs somewhat slower than most, and his volume and pitch vary a fair amount. His answer length stays even from turn to turn, so the exchange keeps a quick tempo.
Jimmy Patronis.decides: The shared role an ask offers him is what he values most, and his follow through is the weak point. So a yes can fade quietly. Visibility for his role sits above the typical level, which gives a shared announcement real pull. His bills span few issue areas, so an ask outside those areas will struggle. A decision sticks only with a named next step and a set date.

archetype.justification: He rarely takes charge of a conversation, yet his words are among the most forceful, and his answers run long.

Jodey Arrington.bottom_line: Bring one specific ask with the people it helps, and allow long answers. Outside pressure has a clearly lower hold on him, so the facts must settle it.
do: Name a family the change would reach, not the statute
Let him give a long answer before you respond
Offer a second source when he digs in on a point
dont: Count on a bill's momentum to hold without a named owner
Rely on outside pressure to settle a weak case
Jodey Arrington.warning_sign: Usually his answers are full and drawn out, and he rarely takes charge. When he starts defending his position whenever challenged, he is digging in, so stop, let him finish, and return to who your ask helps.
Jodey Arrington.follow_up: Send him a one page note listing the vote date, the bill's next step, and who tracks it within two days.
Jodey Arrington.personality: Arrington, from Texas, gives details a loose hand, and he is quite skeptical. He is much more worked up than most, and his public words carry a heavy emotional load, more than nearly any colleague's. Bills he sponsors reach fewer areas than almost any colleague's do, while his votes are somewhat less dependable than most. Taking the lead in conversation is not his habit, but he ranks among the most combative members in hearings.
Jodey Arrington.speaks: Pitch varies little in his talk, and his volume holds a fairly even line. His answers run long in interviews, and his longest ones are very lengthy. His answer length stays even, and quick brief exchanges come much more often in his talk than they do for most. Forceful and warm words rather than social ones mark his talk, and filler and defense show up often. Action words are somewhat more common in his public language than most.
Jodey Arrington.decides: He judges an ask by its fit with the narrow areas he already works on. Outside force weighs lightly on him, so the substance has to settle the matter. His follow through on bills runs uneven, so any decision holds only with a named owner and a set date. Examples of families affected fit his framing best, so a case about who gains will land.

archetype.justification: Very careful and organized, yet his language is much more charged than most, and he speaks at a much quicker clip than most.

Joe Courtney.bottom_line: Keep the ask to one step with a fixed date, since his follow through runs much weaker than most. Bring community stories that show who benefits, since they move him.
do: Bring community stories that show who benefits
Match his fast pace and put the date first
Fix a date before the meeting ends so follow through holds
dont: Treat his fast delivery as a firm commitment
Joe Courtney.warning_sign: When hearings get going he is usually much less confrontational than most, so a pointed, forceful reply from him is a change. If he turns combative, slow down, ask what worries him, and make the next step explicit.
Joe Courtney.follow_up: Send him a one page note with the ask, the community story and a fixed date by Friday.
Joe Courtney.personality: Courtney is somewhat curious, and he is much less easily rattled than most. His account of his work is much less exact than most, but his language carries much more charge. He sees bills through much less reliably than most, though his legislation spans somewhat more issue areas than most. Public notice falls somewhat less on him than most colleagues. In hearings he shows much less combat than most members. He represents Connecticut's second district and once worked in criminal law practice.
Joe Courtney.speaks: His delivery runs at a much quicker clip than most, and his pauses are much shorter than most. Volume and pitch both stay much more level than most. His language runs with much more feeling than most colleagues. Under hearing questions he is much less confrontational than most colleagues. When he discusses his work, the terms are much less exact than most.
Joe Courtney.decides: Before backing anything he tests whether its human stories ring true, and he responds to people who are helped. Across his legislation the mix of areas runs wider than most, so an ask in one of them fits. He follows bills to the finish much less often, so any decision from him needs a dated owner. Having worked in criminal law practice, he weighs the people behind a case first.

archetype.justification: His very outgoing, very warm style and bipartisan bill work show a connector who brings many people in.

Joe Neguse.bottom_line: Make a specific case with allies who back it. Once he has heard it out, he holds his position, so settle the next step before leaving.
do: Bring voices from both parties who share the ask
Agree a next step, its owner, and a date before the meeting ends
Let him finish defending his position before you reply
dont: Cut in before he finishes, since he often trails off mid sentence
Talk over his long answers, since he holds the floor firmly
Joe Neguse.warning_sign: He normally holds the floor and talks in uneven runs. If he drops the point and his pitch flattens, he is backing off, so stop and ask what changed for him.
Joe Neguse.follow_up: Within two days, forward a brief writeup of the request, listing the upcoming step, its owner, and due date.
Joe Neguse.personality: Neguse has a very outgoing manner and very careful habits, and his words are warm yet forceful. He works across the aisle and joins bills in many areas, so his reach is wide. He leads conversations as firmly as almost anyone, and he pushes back hard when someone challenges him. Put together, he is a connector who holds his ground on the points that matter to him.
Joe Neguse.speaks: Long, uneven runs mark his talk, and his answers run longer than nearly any colleague's. His words are warm, upbeat and forceful, and he pushes back firmly when challenged. Speed is high, with short pauses and a pitch that swings widely. Each exchange tends to run well past the question that was asked, and he keeps going. His manner is direct, and he keeps the exchange moving.
Joe Neguse.decides: Backers of a request count for most with him, since his reach across issues and parties gives him many people to check with. Pressing him in the moment tends to harden his stance. A decision sticks with him when it has backers from both sides and a named next step, so an ask needs proof of who will stand with it. His long, detailed answers give him room to test each backer before he commits.

archetype.justification: His words are warm, upbeat, and forceful, while his details run looser than most and his bills reach fewer issues than most.

Joe Wilson.bottom_line: Lead with the outcome in a short, direct case, and follow up through his staff.
do: Bring the policy's results in a short, direct case
Name who outside the room backs the ask, before you make it
Put a yes or no question first, since even his longest answers stay brief
Ask him to finish a point he has left unfinished
dont: Answer his upbeat words with a flat, drawn-out delivery
Pad your replies with filler phrases, since he speaks with almost none
Take a warm yes as settled, since he sees bills through less reliably
Joe Wilson.warning_sign: His replies usually come singly rather than in runs. If he starts firing back a rapid run of replies, he is going back and forth on one point. Name that point back to him in a sentence, then let him answer it.
Joe Wilson.follow_up: Send written answers to his staff within two days, with each question matched to a short reply.
Joe Wilson.personality: Wilson reads as fairly outgoing and very agreeable, and his public words are warm and forceful. Specifics are a weak spot for him, yet he is among the most practical members in the House. His bills reach a few fewer issues than most, and his public words reach a much narrower set of issues. He has spoken about his son's work as a state attorney general. Following bills through is a somewhat weaker area for him than for most.
Joe Wilson.speaks: His public tone is one of the warmest and most upbeat in the House. He speaks a touch slower than most. Between phrases, his pauses are much briefer than most. Volume stays even, more so than most. His longest answers rank among the shortest in the House, and his replies are brief. Keep your own replies about as brief as his.
Joe Wilson.decides: Outside voices carry extra weight with him, so attach a backer's letter to the ask. A letter from someone outside the room gives him something to point to. Keep the ask to one vote, and name the day you need his answer. Attach the one plain figure that backs the result, so he can repeat it in his own words.

archetype.justification: Quite reserved and skeptical, he talks in a narrow lane and is among the most reliable at seeing bills through.

John Barrasso.bottom_line: Bring one specific request and the facts behind it, since outside sway moves him far less than most lawmakers.
do: Expect him to be far less combative than most colleagues in hearings
Put a named owner on each step you agree
Expect skepticism and test the facts before he agrees
Offer him a visible role since he keeps a low public profile
dont: Push him with pressure from outside groups
John Barrasso.warning_sign: He usually answers in one unbroken thread, without quick short replies. When you challenge him and he starts defending his position a little more than most, he is on guard, so restate your one point rather than press harder.
John Barrasso.follow_up: Forward his office a short page of facts with each agreed action and its owner within two days.
John Barrasso.personality: Barrasso is guarded and skeptical, and his talk stays on a tight range of issues. Public words run cooler than almost anyone's, yet they are among the most upbeat in the chamber. Among the most reliable members at seeing bills through, he also describes his work with somewhat careful and detailed language. In public he is far less visible than his post would suggest. He crosses party lines a little less than most.
John Barrasso.speaks: Descriptions of his work are fuller and more precise than most, and his wording sticks to a handful of issues. His phrasing runs cooler than almost anyone's but still upbeat, and it is a little less social than most. Under pressure he holds ground a little more than most, and rapid clipped answers are not his habit. In hearings he keeps a much less combative tone than most.
John Barrasso.decides: Requests get weighed by the facts behind them, since results and evidence fit his framing. Backing from across the divide counts for less with him, since he reaches over a little less than most. A push from outside will not settle a question with him. He is about as dependable as almost anyone when finishing bills, so once he agrees to a step, he tends to carry it out.

archetype.justification: His reserved manner, careful organization and low public visibility fit the Tortoise well.

John Boozman.bottom_line: Come with a careful, organized case on a single bill, and give him time, since outside voices carry less weight with him than most.
do: Lead with the bill and its record of follow through
Ask him to name the next step and when it happens
Expect him to stay among the least combative members at a hearing
dont: Assume a quiet ask will move him through outside noise
Read his low profile as a lack of interest in your ask
John Boozman.warning_sign: He usually keeps his views to himself in open rooms. Any firmer tone from him at a hearing signals that he is weighing the ask hard, so take it seriously. Slow down, ask what would work, and confirm each step in writing.
John Boozman.follow_up: Email his office in writing the next action and its timing, naming the staffer who will follow up.
John Boozman.personality: Boozman stays quite reserved while being very careful and organized. His talk covers a far wider span of subjects than most, and he describes his own work with exact, granular detail. He works with the other side less than almost anyone in the Senate, and he keeps a low public profile. Outside voices carry less weight with him than most, which makes him a methodical, low key senator.
John Boozman.speaks: Reserved in delivery, he keeps answers close to the record. Exact, granular detail marks how he describes his work. His talk spans a far wider set of issues than most. Yet at hearings he sits among the least combative speakers. Pushing an argument past what the record supports is rare for him. He prefers to make the case through specifics and documented detail.
John Boozman.decides: His bills stretch across a far broader range of issue areas than most, so asks within his lane fit well. He works with the other side less than almost anyone, so a cross aisle deal is a hard sell. Outside voices carry less weight with him than most members, so the ask must carry its own record. So a decision from him needs proof that the ask will hold up over time.

archetype.justification: Careful, detailed talk about his work, reliable at seeing bills through, and very little emotional charge.

John Carter.bottom_line: Bring the ask in writing with the detail that matters, then give him time to check it. Outside voices sway him less than most, so the case must stand alone.
do: Walk through the bill's sections in order, with the detail for each
Let him check the figures on his own before you meet
dont: Rely on a crowd of supporters to carry the ask
Mistake his low visibility for low interest
John Carter.warning_sign: A public event cannot show whether he has checked the ask, since his public words do not show it. Ask him at the end which detail he would check first, then send that detail the same day.
John Carter.follow_up: Send a written summary of the detail the same day, naming the one step he needs to approve.
John Carter.personality: Carter is careful and thorough when he discusses his work, and his public language is low on feeling. He covers a far narrower set of topics than most colleagues. His bills reach fewer issues than most. Following bills through is stronger for him than for most. He is less visible than most, including for his role. He has a background in general counsel work for a state House agriculture panel.
John Carter.speaks: He discusses a narrow slice of topics and stays close to the detail of his work. His language is precise and carries little emotional color. That makes his public talk read as exact rather than expressive. Specifics matter more to him than sweeping claims, so each point is tied to the particulars of a bill. Methodical is the word for his manner, and he is more of a specialist than a generalist.
John Carter.decides: He tests a request on whether it fits the narrow set of issues he works on. Whether the detail holds up when he checks it also matters. He keeps up with his bills better than most, so a clearly specified ask earns his attention. Outside voices sway him less than most, and his public visibility stays low, so a decision needs a written record and a named next step to stick.

archetype.justification: Very careful and organized, he keeps answers short and holds firm when someone challenges him.

John Cornyn.bottom_line: Build the ask on results rather than rhetoric, then accept a brief reply. He digs in once he has taken a view, so secure the decision early.
do: Share the results in writing ahead of the meeting
Point to the bills he has already carried through
Let his short answers stand and move to the next point
Prepare for him to be more combative than most members in hearings
dont: Keep pressing once he has stated a position
Take his upbeat public tone as a sign of agreement
Raise your tone when he answers briefly, since his words run much less sharp
John Cornyn.warning_sign: He usually answers briefly and defends his position when pushed. If replies shrink to one line and he restates the same view, he has settled, and more argument will only harden him. Ease off and end on a question he can answer briefly.
John Cornyn.follow_up: After the meeting, send his office a written list of the bills that carry the ask, each with an owner and a date, within two days.
John Cornyn.personality: Cornyn is a reserved, careful and organized member who is hard to fluster. His public words run upbeat and social, yet he keeps replies brief and sticks to a short list of topics. He is among the most dependable in the chamber at casting votes and carrying bills forward, and his public profile runs high for the role he holds. These traits fit: he works a small, deliberate lane, and once he has taken a position he defends it, so he runs the meeting on his terms.
John Cornyn.speaks: He talks in short, direct sentences and keeps to a few issues. When he describes his work, he tends to be a little more thorough than most, and his words carry little emotional charge. His words are much less sharp than most, and his pauses between phrases run short while his volume stays even. Under challenge he holds his ground without raising his voice, and in a hearing he is more combative than most members, though his answers stay compact.
John Cornyn.decides: Clear results and a short, direct case are what he looks for in any request. Once he has taken a position, he defends it when challenged. His work stays inside the handful of bill types he already carries, and in carrying those bills forward he is among the most dependable. So a decision from him sticks when the case rests on results and a clear next vote.

archetype.justification: His very outgoing manner, upbeat wording and action focus earn the Hummingbird label.

John Curtis.bottom_line: Bring a clear ask and a written next step, since he follows bills through closely. Outside pressure counts a little less with him, so the case must carry it.
do: Open with the results in a short, direct case
Keep the talk moving with brief, action focused exchanges
Anticipate that he will be somewhat less combative at hearings
dont: Treat his friendly demeanor as a firm commitment
Let a warm, social exchange stand in for a clear next step
John Curtis.warning_sign: He usually speaks in upbeat turns and takes charge much less than most. If he starts holding the floor longer than usual, he is weighing the ask, so slow down, ask his view directly, and confirm the next step.
John Curtis.follow_up: Afterward, mail his staff one page that lays out the coming action, who follows up and the due date.
John Curtis.personality: Curtis stays very sociable and fairly inquisitive, with a notably agreeable streak. Carefulness and organization mark his approach, and his talk about his work runs deeper than most. His wording is gentle and social, yet it is less forceful than most. Follow through on bills is very reliable for him, and he leads conversations far less often than others. His bills touch a bit fewer topics than most, and he draws a little less public notice than most.
John Curtis.speaks: His answers come in short, quick runs, and his replies stay brief. He describes things in upbeat, action focused terms, and his wording is among the most sociable in the chamber. Others often take the lead in conversation. Light touch marks how he talks, so the room rarely feels pressed. His talk stays brief and bright, with a focus on what gets done.
John Curtis.decides: Requests are judged on whether they can be carried out and on the outcomes they claim. He leads conversations far less often than others, so an ask has to come from someone else's lead or a written plan. Outside voices move him a little less, so the case itself must carry the ask. So he commits when the next step is written down and the results are plain.

archetype.justification: He is outgoing, and he works across party lines much less than most, with filler-heavy talk and a sharp hearing tone.

John Fetterman.bottom_line: Send written technical evidence ahead, since he will defend his position hard in the room. Keep your asks short so he can answer them on paper first.
do: Send a written technical brief ahead, with the method laid out
Open by naming the one technical point you want him to test
Leave a short pause after each point, since his filler runs heavy
Let his upbeat energy open the talk before you raise the ask
dont: Trade rebuttals with him, since he defends his ground hard
Treat a sharp hearing exchange as the whole of his view
Accept a verbal commitment as settled, since he is among the least reliable on bills
John Fetterman.warning_sign: He usually talks with a heavy run of filler. If that filler thins out and his replies come back clean and direct, he has stopped working the point with you. Sum up his stated position in a line and let it stand.
John Fetterman.follow_up: Within a week, send his staff a written technical note with the next step marked and its owner named.
John Fetterman.personality: Fetterman stands out as among the most outgoing senators, and he gets worked up far more readily than most. His words carry very little emotional charge, and his public words cut harder than most. Specifics do not come easily to him, and his account of the work is among the least careful in the Senate. He is much more visible than most senators in his role. Cross-party work is much lighter for him than for most.
John Fetterman.speaks: He speaks a touch slower than most, with pauses that run longer. Filler runs through his speech, among the heaviest in the Senate. His pitch swings more than most. Upbeat language marks his interviews, well beyond most. Pressed on a point, he digs in across interviews. Keep your replies to one point at a time, as his own answers run shorter than most.
John Fetterman.decides: After he settles on a view, he digs in, so make the written case, kept to a single page, before he has decided. Outside voices carry a little extra weight with him, so line up the first backer before the meeting. Bills are where he is among the least reliable in the Senate, so keep your ask to one step he can take.

archetype.justification: His much wider issue range, fairly curious nature and preference for technical written evidence earn the Owl label.

John Garamendi.bottom_line: Bring written technical evidence and a clear next step, not pressure. Pressure from outside works on him less than on most, so the proof has to carry the case.
do: Send the technical summary ahead of the meeting in writing
Let long answers finish, since he trails off without a clear end
Offer a public moment where his visibility helps the ask
dont: Count on outside pressure to close the gap
Take a quick yes as the final word on the vote
John Garamendi.warning_sign: Usually he gives lengthy answers that trail off, so trailing is not a refusal. When he suddenly gives brief replies and stops engaging with follow ups, he is disengaging. Stop, ask one closed question, and offer a written summary to pick it up later.
John Garamendi.follow_up: Right after the meeting, give him a compact written note naming the bill's next step, with the evidence attached and a reply date.
John Garamendi.personality: Garamendi is a curious member who covers wide ground and is fairly outgoing. He is somewhat less exacting about details than most, and he carries a touch of skepticism. His words feel cool compared with almost anyone's, though he is socially lively. Among the least reliable at seeing bills through, he is nonetheless very visible. Interview answers run long, and they often trail off unfinished.
John Garamendi.speaks: He speaks in a cool, social way and ranges across many issues in each answer. In interviews his replies run past most others, and the longest ones go further still. He sometimes stops short and leaves a sentence hanging, and the charge in his words is lower than almost anyone's. He is less forceful than most in how he states a point. During hearings he comes across as somewhat less combative than most members.
John Garamendi.decides: He judges an ask by how firmly written technical evidence supports it. Outside force gets less traction with him than with most colleagues. He carries a touch of skepticism, and his follow through is weak, so a verbal promise rarely becomes a vote. A decision needs a documented next step with someone responsible for it, so his support holds only when it is written down.

archetype.justification: He is social, and his public talk ranges across far more issues than most.

John Hickenlooper.bottom_line: Lead with results and a bipartisan list of backers, since outside voices move him much more than most. He also pushes back when challenged, so give him room.
do: Open with the results, then make time for the personal side
Build rapport early, since he ranks among the most social voices in the Senate
Bring upbeat energy to the discussion
Let him take the floor, then test the detail with a short question
dont: Skip long speeches, since his answers run short in interviews
Assume a quick yes, since crowds outside sway him far more than most
John Hickenlooper.warning_sign: He usually fills his answers with filler at a level few colleagues match. If the filler drops away, he is on guard. Slow down, ask one open question, and let him finish.
John Hickenlooper.follow_up: Send him a one page memo with the results, the bipartisan backers, and the next step, within three days.
John Hickenlooper.personality: Hickenlooper is somewhat outgoing, and he is very agreeable. His public talk covers far more issues than most, and he comes across as very careful and organized. His wording is much gentler than most, and it carries far more heat than most. Cooperation with the other side comes somewhat more easily to him than to most. He holds his position when challenged, and he keeps his answers to the point. He is social and quick with words, and his filler runs high. Votes and bill follow through rank as reliable on his record.
John Hickenlooper.speaks: He talks in a quick, expressive way with somewhat more upbeat energy than most. In interviews his answers run much briefer than most. Even his longest replies stay somewhat brief. Across replies, his answer length varies somewhat less than most. He trails off somewhat more than most, leaving sentences unfinished. Filler runs heavy in his speech, at a level few colleagues match. When challenged, he holds his position firmly, and his words grow forceful under strain. Pitch climbs and drops somewhat more than most, while his tempo runs somewhat faster than most.
John Hickenlooper.decides: Prior to backing anything he checks whether results are concrete and whether it can win across the aisle. Pressure from outside moves him far more than most colleagues. In a room he leads at a level among the highest of his colleagues. His voting and bill record ranks among the most reliable, so commitments he makes tend to hold. So a bipartisan ask with a named next step is the one he takes up.

archetype.justification: His careful organization, very high reliability and low visibility fit the Tortoise well.

John Hoeven.bottom_line: Bring a clear written case, since he weighs follow through heavily. Outside voices count for less with him, so the record carries the ask.
do: Put the written case in front of him before the meeting
Ask him to name the next step and its timing
In a hearing, expect a less confrontational tone from him
dont: Read his reserve as a sign he is unconvinced
Assume a quiet profile means he has little influence on the bill
John Hoeven.warning_sign: He usually keeps his answers short and takes little charge of a conversation. If he holds the floor at length, he is weighing the ask, so slow down, restate it plainly, and put the next step on paper.
John Hoeven.follow_up: Send his office a brief writeup covering the next step, its timing, and the staffer who will follow up.
John Hoeven.personality: Hoeven sits with the most reserved members in the Senate, yet he is fairly agreeable. Careful structure defines how he approaches things, and his talk covers a far wider range of topics than most. His wording is gentle, upbeat and very social. His follow through on bills ranks near the top in the Senate, and he works with the other side somewhat less than most.
John Hoeven.speaks: Answers run short, and his longest replies sit much shorter than most. Filler turns up a little more in his talk than most, yet sentences tend to reach their end. Wording comes across cool and gentle, and it is less forceful than nearly any colleague's. Points stay close to the record, and others often carry the exchange. He does not push for the floor, so exchanges tend to move at an unforced rhythm.
John Hoeven.decides: His test is how well an ask follows through on bills he already handles. Fewer issue areas than most show up in his bills, so asks within that lane tend to land. He works with the other side somewhat less than most, so a cross aisle deal needs strong backing. Outside voices count for less with him, so the record has to carry the ask.

archetype.justification: His outgoing, curious style and fairly high visibility mark a sociable member who works the room.

John James.bottom_line: Bring one narrow, clear ask with a named owner. He gives brief answers, so leave room for quick replies.
do: Start with the one issue area he already works in
Keep your replies short, since he rarely fills gaps with extra talk
Match his warm, social tone and keep it light
dont: Lean on outside pressure to carry the ask
Read his forceful wording as hostility toward the bill
Expect a long reply after each question
John James.warning_sign: He usually talks fast with short pauses and a very even volume. If his pauses lengthen and his volume starts to move, he is pulling back, so stop pressing and ask one simple question about his concern.
John James.follow_up: Email a single page recap of the request with a named owner and deadline within two days.
John James.personality: James is highly outgoing and fairly curious, and he is very sociable, with warm, upbeat talk that makes him easy to approach. His bills stay in only a few issue areas, and he fills few gaps with extra talk. He is fairly visible in the chamber, and seeing bills through is one of his habits. Put together, he is a friendly specialist who keeps things short.
John James.speaks: Fast speech, short pauses and an even volume keep the rhythm brisk. Words are upbeat and social, with little focus on action. Filler is rare, and short replies come one at a time rather than in quick runs. In conversation the manner is open and quick. The brisk tempo means each point lands in a few seconds. He keeps replies crisp.
John James.decides: He tests a plan by whether it matches one narrow topic he already handles. Seeing bills through is one of his habits, so a short, dated next step matters to him. Pressure from outside counts for much less with him, so a decision sticks only after he sees the case and agrees to a named next step. He moves quickly once the next step is clear.

archetype.justification: His careful, detailed talk about his work and his very reliable voting record fit a diligent, thorough member.

John Joyce.bottom_line: Bring one detailed ask with the paperwork ready. Outside pressure moves him only a little, so the case must hold on its own.
do: Bring the bill's full path and its vote record
Match his quick pace and skip long preambles
Give him a private heads-up before a vote, not a public push
dont: Read his fast talk as a sign he has already decided
Lean on pressure from outside voices to close the gap
John Joyce.warning_sign: A casual talk will not expose how he advances bills step by step, so the procedure is the gap. Before the meeting, ask staff where the bill stands and name the next step.
John Joyce.follow_up: Within a day, send his staff the bill's status and vote record on one page so he can check each figure.
John Joyce.personality: Joyce is a diligent member whose public talk stays within a limited set of issues and explains his work with exacting care. His bills reach fewer issues than most colleagues, but he gets the bills he files through votes and follow through. Visibility on the floor runs low, and he does not push for attention, so he rewards precision over show.
John Joyce.speaks: His remarks hold to a tight set of topics and dig into careful, detailed terms rather than broad framing. Few remarks wander into side topics, so each point tends to be a full one. Public words describe his work with exacting care rather than sweeping claims. Across the issues he names, his language stays exact and fully developed from the first point to the last.
John Joyce.decides: Asks are tested on how well their details hold up under his own review, and he trusts a bill with a clear record of votes and progress. Outside pressure moves him only a little, and his low profile means few voices push him in public. His bills cover a small range of issues, so a request that fits his existing work carries more weight with him. A decision sticks with him only when it comes with a documented record.

archetype.justification: He is one of the most outgoing senators, and few colleagues speak with as much force.

John Kennedy.bottom_line: Keep your ask short and direct, and give him one clear next step. He defends his position often, so do not argue every point.
do: Plan extra minutes into the meeting, since he holds the floor and talks slowly
Greet him warmly, since he is one of the most outgoing senators
Match his forceful tone with a short, plain reply, not a speech
Keep the talk on one topic, because he tends to take it over
dont: Push back on every answer, since he defends ground when challenged
Mistake his very warm tone for a yes on the ask
Read a long pause in his slow delivery as the end of his answer
John Kennedy.warning_sign: In hearings he is usually much more combative than most senators. If he turns polite and asks about timing, not substance, he is ready to wrap up. Ask one open question to bring him back to the ask.
John Kennedy.follow_up: Within a day, send his office a written reply with the one next step and its owner, and ask him to confirm it.
John Kennedy.personality: Kennedy ranks among the most outgoing senators, and among its most curious. Details run much looser for him than most, and he is quite skeptical. His public tone runs very warm, and he keeps the floor far more than most. Across the aisle he builds much less than most, and he digs in on his own ground. He serves on the Senate Banking Committee. He is much more visible than most senators in a similar role.
John Kennedy.speaks: Interview answers from him run shorter than most, and his longest replies stay short. He trails off somewhat more than most; his pace is one of the slowest in the Senate. His pauses are much longer than most. Pitch sits a bit flatter, and his volume moves more than most. Keep your replies short and let the pauses sit. Expect short answers, and give him room to hold a point.
John Kennedy.decides: He holds his ground when challenged, and he digs in once he has taken a position. He builds across the aisle much less than most. Outside pressure shifts him a little more than most colleagues. Build your reply on the points he raises, since he takes charge of the conversation much more than most. End by reopening a point he has held firm on only with something new he has not yet heard, once he has stopped talking.

archetype.justification: Very curious and outgoing, holds the floor more than almost anyone, and gives very long answers.

John Larson.bottom_line: Let him finish, then bring the one ask with a written next step, since he holds the floor and follows through less reliably.
do: Let his longer answers finish before you reply
Write down the step and its owner before you leave
In a hearing, let him finish and answer each point in turn
dont: Compete for the floor, since he holds it more than almost anyone
Treat his gentler wording as agreement
John Larson.warning_sign: He usually takes charge of the room and holds the floor, and extended replies are normal for him. When his volume swings more and he talks through every reply, he is losing patience, so stop and ask which point he needs settled.
John Larson.follow_up: Send a short written next step with a date, and offer a shared public announcement once it is agreed.
John Larson.personality: Larson counts among the most outgoing colleagues and is very curious, with a friendly, agreeable streak. He flares up somewhat more readily than most and describes his efforts in much less detail than most. His bills span somewhat broader ground than most, yet he is much less dependable at carrying them through. Conversations bend toward him, since he leads them and holds the floor, and his answers stretch longer than nearly anyone's. From Connecticut, he sets the pace in the room.
John Larson.speaks: He speaks at length and with force, and his answers are among the longest in the House. Long runs of talk often end mid sentence, since he trails off more than most. Pitch and volume swing more than most, and his words are flatter and cooler than most. Broad in range, he describes his work in general terms rather than detail, and conversations stay in his hands.
John Larson.decides: He asks how well a request fits his wider set of issues, and he is agreeable to a point. Outside voices carry less weight with him, so a push from home will not settle the matter. He presses his own view in the room and tends to hold the floor until he has said his piece. Because he follows through less reliably than most, a yes holds only when it has a written next step and an owner.

archetype.justification: Careful and organized, he keeps a tight focus on few issues and sees his bills through more reliably than most.

John Mannion.bottom_line: Offer a shared role he can announce with you and ask for a commitment he can keep. Outside backing sways him more than typical, so bring those voices in.
do: Propose a joint announcement he can make with you
Ask for a specific commitment, since he follows bills through
Bring outside voices who share the ask
dont: Read his restrained manner in hearings as full endorsement
Fill his long pauses with more facts before he answers
Lead with a long list of practical steps
John Mannion.warning_sign: During hearings he usually runs less combative than most, so a firmer line from him is the shift to watch. That usually means he is wary, so ask what would help him decide.
John Mannion.follow_up: Afterward, send his office a short memo that restates the commitment and names the staffer who will track it.
John Mannion.personality: Mannion is careful and organized, with a practical bent that runs slightly lower than colleagues. His talk stays on a tight set of issues, and his bills cover fewer areas than most. Very reliable at seeing bills through, he is a bit less combative in hearings. The room stays focused on the policy work in front of him. He represents New York.
John Mannion.speaks: He keeps to a narrow set of issues and describes his work in fairly careful, detailed terms. Talking slowly, with long pauses, he lets his volume swing a good deal. His pitch varies somewhat as he speaks. In hearings he is less combative than most, so he tends to make his points without edge. His pace is unhurried, slower than colleagues tend to be.
John Mannion.decides: Whether a request can be carried out is the test he applies, and he is very dependable about carrying bills forward. Shared announcements with a partner he can name give him a reason to commit, and outside voices behind the ask move him more than most. A decision needs a named next step to stick, with an owner for each step.

archetype.justification: Practical in outlook, he stays much looser with details and works on a much narrower set of issues.

John McGuire.bottom_line: Put written, technical evidence in front of him ahead of time. Local voices carry sway with him, moving him much more than most members, so back the ask with them.
do: Send written, technical material before the meeting
Offer a shared role he can announce, since public visibility runs somewhat lower for him
Confirm the next step in writing, since he follows bills through reliably
In a hearing, expect a somewhat less pointed exchange with him
dont: Count on outside pressure alone to settle the question
Debate the theory behind the ask, since he counts among the most practical
John McGuire.warning_sign: When hearings get tense he is usually somewhat less pointed than most, so a blunt question from him is a change. If he turns pointed, slow down, ask what concerns him, and let him finish.
John McGuire.follow_up: Send him a one page note with the ask, the written evidence and the next step by Friday.
John McGuire.personality: McGuire is somewhat reserved and among the most practical members. His grip on details is loose, and he stays much less easily rattled than most. The range of his bills is much narrower than most colleagues. His account of work is somewhat less exact than most, and his language carries somewhat less charge. He follows bills through somewhat more reliably than most. Virginia's fifth district is his seat.
John McGuire.speaks: Loudness moves up and down somewhat more than most, while his tone stays much flatter than most. Language is somewhat less emotionally loaded than most colleagues. His public talk spans a somewhat narrower range than most. In a hearing he turns somewhat less combative than most, and his questions are less pointed. His remarks stay close to the core of his bills, which are narrower than most.
John McGuire.decides: He wants a written, technical case that holds up, so evidence comes before anything else. His bills span a narrow set of issues, so an ask inside those areas fits him. Pressure from outside reaches him much more than most members, so local voices can carry weight. Public visibility runs somewhat lower than most, so a shared role with him can raise his profile.

archetype.justification: Reserved and difficult to fluster, he keeps a narrow focus, speaks in precise terms, and keeps a low public presence.

John Moolenaar.bottom_line: Bring the facts on what the policy delivers, briefly and plainly. Outside pressure counts a bit more with him than with most, so a written step holds him.
do: Lead with the result in one sentence before any detail
Bring outside voices if the first meeting stalls
Keep the ask quiet in public, since his own exposure stays low
dont: Read his quiet manner as agreement
Expect a quick yes from him
John Moolenaar.warning_sign: A public forum will not show where he stands, since he is quite reserved in open discussion. Ask him directly which part of the plan he will take back to his office, and note it before you leave.
John Moolenaar.follow_up: When the meeting closes, mail his office a single page recapping the agreed step and who owns it.
John Moolenaar.personality: Moolenaar is quite reserved, fairly careful and organized, and difficult to fluster. He keeps his public talk on a narrow range of issues and describes his work in fairly precise terms. Bills cover a bit fewer issues than most. A low public presence, even for his role, keeps him in the background. He represents Michigan. He is methodical with the detail he does offer.
John Moolenaar.speaks: He keeps to a narrow range of issues and describes his work in precise terms. His words carry a little less feeling than colleagues. Talking slowly, he keeps his volume fairly even, though his pitch moves a good deal. He does not reach for drama, so his manner reads as plain and direct. He does not wander, and each point comes in plain terms.
John Moolenaar.decides: He weighs an ask on the facts behind the result it delivers. Pressure from beyond sways him more than most, so any backed ask gets his attention. He takes on fewer issues than most, so an ask that stays inside his areas fits better. With a low public presence, a decision needs a named next step to stick, and an owner for each step.

archetype.justification: Curiosity runs high, and his bills span issues more broadly than nearly anyone's.

John Rose.bottom_line: Bring a shared role he can announce with you, since his bills span issues widely and he follows through somewhat less than most.
do: Offer a joint announcement or event so he has a role to share
Name the next step aloud and write it down before you leave
Plan for a somewhat more combative streak from him in hearings
dont: Expect his wide interests to keep this ask at the top of his list
Lean on outside groups alone, since outside pressure moves him less
John Rose.warning_sign: By default he is curious and fairly outgoing, and he moves across many topics. If he stops ranging and presses a single point hard in a hearing, he is on guard, so answer that point directly and then return to the ask.
John Rose.follow_up: Email his staff a short note with the step ahead, its owner, and its due date within two days.
John Rose.personality: Rose stays fairly outgoing and curious, and his public talk reaches far more issues than most colleagues. His public account of his work is broad rather than detailed. His public words run less charged than most colleagues, and bill follow through trails a little behind most colleagues. In hearings he runs a bit more combative than most, and his public profile sits lower than most for his post.
John Rose.speaks: He speaks broadly, touching many issues, and describes his work in general terms rather than detail. His words carry less charge than most, and his manner is low key. In hearings he is a bit more combative than most, so the tone sharpens there. He works across many topics at once, and his phrases tend to stay on the surface. Answers come out fluent, but they do not reach the finer points.
John Rose.decides: Fit with the wide set of issues his bills already cover is how he judges a request. Outside voices move him clearly less than most members, so a local push counts for less. A joint announcement or shared event gives him a reason to stay with the ask. Follow through trails most colleagues a little, so commitments stick only with a named owner and a firm date in place.

archetype.justification: Fairly outgoing and readily worked up, with upbeat, action focused words and people first framing.

John Rutherford.bottom_line: Bring him a short case with people in it and lock in the next step. He works across the aisle more than almost anyone, so a shared ask fits him.
do: Bring people who benefit, since stories fit his framing
Name a bipartisan cosponsor, since he often works across the aisle
Keep your turns brief, since he answers in quick bursts
dont: Mistake his upbeat tone for an agreement to act
Answer his quick bursts with a long speech
John Rutherford.warning_sign: His usual pattern is quick bursts of upbeat replies, by default. If the bursts stop and he goes quiet, he is on guard or weighing the ask. Stop, name what you need from him, and let him answer in his own time.
John Rutherford.follow_up: Give him a one sheet recap naming the next step, who owns it, and the due date.
John Rutherford.personality: Rutherford comes across as fairly outgoing and readily worked up, with words that carry a touch more emotion than most. He is a bit less trusting than most, and almost nobody in the House reaches across the aisle more often. Across his bills he covers a somewhat wider set of topics than most, and his talk is upbeat and action focused. Replies come much shorter than most, while he turns far more combative than most members once hearings begin. His public profile is somewhat lower than most.
John Rutherford.speaks: He answers in bursts of quick, upbeat replies, and his talk stays focused on action. Upbeat wording marks much of what he says, well beyond the usual level. His interview replies run tighter than almost anyone's, and their length swings more than almost anyone's. The same quick rhythm shows in his interview turns, which are brief and fast. In hearings the edge in his manner runs hotter than most members.
John Rutherford.decides: Whether an ask helps people, and whether it works across the aisle, shapes his view. Pressure from outside gets through to him clearly more than to most members, so a visible push can change his view. He works across the aisle more than almost anyone, so a shared ask carries weight with him. Bills he takes up get finished a bit less reliably than most, so a decision holds once an owner and a due date are named.
