archetype.justification: He is among the most reserved senators and skeptical by default, and his bill follow-through is strong.

John Thune.bottom_line: Lead with a short case about the results, and keep each step of the ask concrete and plain.
do: Bring the results on a single page, with the timing stated
Track each figure in his long answers, since his volume stays even
Let his longer answers play out before you reply
Answer his doubt by pointing to bills he has already seen through
dont: Fill silence hoping he will take charge of the talk
Press the ask in forceful terms, against his mild word choice
Lean on outside pressure to move him, since it counts for less with him
John Thune.warning_sign: In hearings he usually keeps a very mild tone, much less combative than most. If he grows even more polite and starts thanking you for coming, he has set the ask aside. Pause and restate the ask in one plain sentence.
John Thune.follow_up: Send his legislative director a short note on the results and the next step by Thursday.
John Thune.personality: Thune serves as Senate Majority Leader, and he is among the most reserved senators and among the most practical. Few members in the Senate match his record of getting bills seen through. By default, he is a bit skeptical. Cool wording marks his talk, and it is one of the least forceful in the Senate. In hearings he is much less combative than most members, and he is very visible. The bills he carries span somewhat fewer areas than most.
John Thune.speaks: In interviews his answers come out somewhat longer than most, and filler fills his speech. Few senators talk faster than he does. His pitch swings more than nearly any colleague's. His pauses are short, and his volume stays even across the whole talk. Plan on a fast pace, with few gaps between his points. Let the filler pass and listen for the point.
John Thune.decides: Facts laid out in order fit him best, with the outcome spelled out. Because his default is doubt, the case has to hold up under close checking from the first claim to the last. Pointed questions at that stage are fine, so long as each answer stays plain and tied to the facts. Close by asking which claim he would check first.

archetype.justification: Very careful and organized, with a narrow issue range and low emotional heat in his public words.

Johnny Olszewski.bottom_line: Bring one short, specific ask he can check, since he follows through fairly reliably on bills, and agree a dated next step.
do: Offer him a shared announcement he can front with you
Give him room for long answers and wait for the full point
In a hearing, expect questions a little less combative than usual
dont: Read his warm tone as a commitment he has not yet made
Rush him when an answer runs long, since he often trails off unfinished
Let his quiet manner stand in for a commitment to act
Johnny Olszewski.warning_sign: By default he is less combative in hearings, and his public tone stays low key. If he turns combative during a hearing, something in the ask has struck a nerve, so answer that concern in one plain sentence and then stop.
Johnny Olszewski.follow_up: Email his staff a note stating the ask, its next step, and its owner, within two days.
Johnny Olszewski.personality: Olszewski keeps his work tidy and methodical, and his public words run warmer than the chamber's typical tone. Seldom does he take the lead in conversation, and his manner is quite reserved. His issue range stays narrow, while his public talk goes into careful, detailed terms about his work. He is fairly agreeable, and bills tend to get carried through. Little emotional heat shows up in what he says in public.
Johnny Olszewski.speaks: He gives long answers in interviews, and they stay even in length from one to the next. His public words are warm and focused on action, and his tone reads as low key. In hearings he keeps a gentler edge than most members, but his longest answers still trail off before the point ends. He does not push for the floor and lets others lead.
Johnny Olszewski.decides: A request is tested by whether he can unveil it alongside someone and whether local voices back it. Follow through on bills is fairly good, so an agreed step usually holds once he commits. Pressure from outside groups counts for him more than for most colleagues. A decision holds only when people he listens to back it and a dated next step is set.

archetype.justification: He is quite reserved, among the most dependable on follow through, and rarely visible for his role.

Jon Husted.bottom_line: Lead with the people a plan helps and set clear steps. Outside voices weigh more with him than with most, so a careful documented case works best.
do: Send the plan in writing with dates and owners
Tell the story of who is helped, not the vote count
Let trusted outside voices speak before you make the ask
dont: Push him to commit on the spot to a new position
Rely on charm or public pressure to win him over
Jon Husted.warning_sign: He usually keeps reserved and sticks close to the facts. If he stops volunteering views and asks for more written detail in a hearing, he is weighing the risk, so send the detail, not pressure.
Jon Husted.follow_up: Afterward, send a brief written summary naming the next step, who owns it and a date.
Jon Husted.personality: Husted stays quite reserved, and little rattles him. He speaks about bills in tight, careful terms and keeps a narrow set of issues. Visibility ranks very low for his role. He tends to finish what he starts, and he ranks among the most dependable members on follow through. His words carry little emotional charge, and in hearings he is milder than most.
Jon Husted.speaks: He keeps his language plain, and his words carry little emotional charge. His manner is low key rather than charged, and it stays that way throughout. Plans are explained in tight, precise terms. In hearings he is milder than most, and he keeps his points narrow, which matches his limited range of issues. He stays close to the facts and keeps to his own area.
Jon Husted.decides: Clear impact and a documented record are what he looks for in an ask. Outside voices move him more than most colleagues, and in formal settings he is milder than most, so a request gains from clear written detail. He also tends to finish what he starts, which makes a clear plan easier for him to carry. So a commitment holds with him when the plan is written and someone checks back on it.

archetype.justification: Very curious and very upbeat, somewhat outgoing and visible, yet near the bottom of the chamber at seeing bills through.

Jon Ossoff.bottom_line: Bring a specific ask that sparks his curiosity and pin down who moves it next. His yes does not carry the bill without a named owner.
do: Offer him a joint announcement he can front publicly
Bring outside supporters who can back the ask alongside you
Keep your points brief and let him answer in short turns
In a hearing, expect combative exchanges and answer with facts
dont: Take his upbeat tone as agreement on the details
Assume he will drive the conversation toward your ask
Jon Ossoff.warning_sign: Usually he is curious and somewhat outgoing, answering briefly without clipped runs. If he replies in quick bursts and stops asking questions, he is losing interest or on guard. Stop, name the point he is weighing, and offer one concrete way to meet it.
Jon Ossoff.follow_up: Within two days, send his staff a short note naming the agreed next step and its date.
Jon Ossoff.personality: Ossoff has a very curious mind and a very upbeat, somewhat outgoing style, so he takes conversations with energy. He shows a little skepticism toward easy answers, and he is somewhat less easily rattled than most. His bills touch a somewhat narrower set of issues than most. Seeing bills through sits near the bottom of the chamber for him, so his energy shows more in the room than on paper. He is warmer than nearly any colleague and somewhat more visible than most, so people notice him when he speaks up.
Jon Ossoff.speaks: He speaks somewhat quicker than most, with pauses that run somewhat longer between phrases and a volume more even than nearly any colleague's. Answers come in somewhat shorter turns than most, and he trails off much less than most. His speech carries almost no filler, which puts him near the bottom of the chamber. Language is very social and a little more forceful than most members. He touches a somewhat broader field of topics than most.
Jon Ossoff.decides: Requests get sized up by how well they match his curiosity, and he tests them against other views before he commits. Outside pressure moves him more than most members do. His bills run across a somewhat narrower set of issues than most, so he tends to stay within the areas he already works in. Carrying bills through sits among the least reliable for him, so commitments hold only while someone tracks the bill.

archetype.justification: Fairly outgoing, unusually loose with details, and narrower in the issues his bills cover.

Jonathan Jackson.bottom_line: Bring one written technical brief ahead of the meeting, since that fits how he works. Outside force gets less of a grip on him, so the document carries the case.
do: Open with a quick, friendly exchange before the document
Keep the ask to one point he can check against the document
Give him time to react before you press for a view
dont: Assume a spoken briefing alone will carry the case
Jonathan Jackson.warning_sign: An ordinary briefing cannot show when he has lost the thread, so watch for quiet on a specific point. When that happens, send the detail in writing the same evening.
Jonathan Jackson.follow_up: Send the written brief to his office the day after and ask for a reply on the single point you care about.
Jonathan Jackson.personality: Jackson tends to be fairly outgoing and readily gets worked up, and his words carry a touch more emotion than most. Details come looser from him than from most colleagues, so his public case leans on feeling more than specifics. Across his bills he takes up far fewer topics than most, and his account of his work is much less careful than most. Visibility runs somewhat low, and written, technical material suits how he works best.
Jonathan Jackson.speaks: He speaks in loose, animated terms, and his details come out less precise than most. Feeling tends to arrive before facts when he makes a case. His account of his work is much less careful and detailed than most. Across the topics he takes up, his range is somewhat narrower.
Jonathan Jackson.decides: He gauges an ask through the written technical case behind it, more than spoken pressure. Outside pressure has less grip on him than it has on most members, and a push from the room carries less force with him. Across his bills he takes up far fewer topics than most, so an ask fits best inside his own areas. Spoken requests carry less weight than documents he can check at his own pace. A decision holds for him once it is written down.

archetype.justification: Skeptical by nature, she still speaks warmer than nearly any senator, and her work is framed around the people it helps.

Joni Ernst.bottom_line: Lead with the families the plan helps, and keep your tone gentle and even. A push from outside carries less weight with her, so one clear case does more.
do: Prepare a one-page story about the families the plan reaches
Wait a beat after each short answer before you add a point
Be ready to set the agenda, since she seldom takes charge of the talk
Name the counties the plan reaches, since her yearly tour covers every one
dont: Plan on quick runs of replies to speed things up, since she rarely gives them
Use hard-hitting language, since her words are a little less forceful
Take her warm words as a sign she is sold
Joni Ernst.warning_sign: In hearings she is usually much less combative than most senators. If she starts turning your questions back on you, she is sharper than usual. Ask what would settle it.
Joni Ernst.follow_up: By Tuesday, send her office written replies to every question she put to you, in sequence.
Joni Ernst.personality: Ernst is warmer in public than nearly any senator, and hearings rarely bring out an edge in her. Across issues, she talks about a wider range than most, and her public account of her work is more detailed than most. A little skeptical, she is also a bit looser with specifics than most. She builds across party lines a bit more than most. She has described her yearly tour of Iowa counties, which she enjoys.
Joni Ernst.speaks: Her public words run much gentler than most, and they carry much more feeling than most. Interviews show brief answers, and even her longest replies stay short. Her pitch moves less than nearly any senator's, and she leaves only short pauses between phrases. She seldom takes charge of the talk and rarely trades quick runs of replies, so plan to steer the meeting yourself. Keep your pace unhurried and let her finish before you add anything.
Joni Ernst.decides: She builds with the other party a bit more than most, so a plan with backers in both parties fits her record. Where it fits, mention the family-farm health struggle she has spoken about in public, and keep it brief. Before the next talk, line up backers from both parties, and bring their names along with the plan so she sees who already stands behind it.

archetype.justification: His very curious, very careful, slow spoken manner and wide issue range fit a deliberate, curious member.

Joseph Morelle.bottom_line: Bring a case about the people it helps, since stories of who gains move him. Outside voices count heavily with him, so pair the ask with those who back it.
do: Open with the people a bill would help, and name them
Give him room, since he pauses longer than most between phrases
Pair your ask with colleagues from both sides who back it
dont: Take his slower pace as a verdict on your ask
Expect a hearing exchange to stay polite
Joseph Morelle.warning_sign: By default he is sharp in hearings, so a firm tone there is normal for him. A sudden flat, quick reply means he is on guard, so pause and restate who the bill helps.
Joseph Morelle.follow_up: Within two days, send his office a short summary of who the bill helps and the names of colleagues who back it.
Joseph Morelle.personality: Morelle is a very curious member, and his work is carefully organized. Fluster comes slowly to him, far less than typical colleagues. He crosses the aisle more often than most, and his bills touch far more issue areas than typical members. Votes and bill follow through run well below typical levels. He draws less notice than his role would suggest, and in hearings he presses hard.
Joseph Morelle.speaks: His talk spreads across far more topics than typical speakers, so each answer tends to range widely. He keeps moving between themes rather than settling on one. In hearings he is markedly more combative than typical members, so his tone turns sharper there. Each exchange takes in several issue areas before it settles. Listeners hear a broad mix of subjects, and the hearing tone shifts as the topics widen.
Joseph Morelle.decides: Whether it changes the lives of people it names is the core of his judgment, and stories about who gains earn his attention. Outside pressure counts for a lot with him, so a coalition of voices from several sides carries more weight than a single push. His visibility runs a bit low, so a commitment from him holds when a named colleague checks it.

archetype.justification: His narrow issue range, few bills, and very low visibility fit a narrowly focused, practical member.

Josh Brecheen.bottom_line: Bring written, technical material ahead of time, and expect a civil exchange in hearings. Follow through is weak for him, so tie the next step to a named date.
do: Send the technical brief and sources before the meeting
In a hearing, keep questions civil and to the point
Tie the next step to a named date and owner
dont: Expect his low profile to carry the bill on its own
Assume a commitment will hold without a named check
Josh Brecheen.warning_sign: By default he weighs a request on its merits and keeps his replies tight. In hearings, when his questions suddenly turn sharp, he is on guard, so answer that fact directly and offer the written detail.
Josh Brecheen.follow_up: Within two days, send his office the written summary and the named date for the next step.
Josh Brecheen.personality: Brecheen stays a little reticent and a little practical, and he keeps his remarks to a narrow range of topics. His public words run heavy with feeling, far beyond typical colleagues. His bill list stays among the narrowest in the House. Following bills to passage is not a strength for him. His profile in the chamber is low, and his public exposure trails his role.
Josh Brecheen.speaks: He talks about a narrow set of issues, so his remarks stay in a small lane. His words carry strong feeling, and that shows in word choice. In hearings he rarely pushes, so his manner stays civil. His remarks rarely reach past the bill in front of him. Few of his remarks move beyond a single theme, and his feeling comes through in each one.
Josh Brecheen.decides: A request earns his attention when it matches the handful of topics he already takes on, and written technical evidence outweighs a broad appeal. His low visibility means few colleagues will push his name forward, so a clear ask needs its own advocates. Follow through is not his strong point, so a commitment from him holds only when someone checks the date.

archetype.justification: His very outgoing, very visible manner and warm word choice fit a sociable, out front member.

Josh Gottheimer.bottom_line: Bring a cross party coalition and a results case. Pressure from outside lands hard with him, so line up a visible partner and a dated step.
do: Lead with the results and the numbers behind them
Invite a colleague from the other party to colead
Keep the meeting moving, since he talks at length
dont: Count on a brief answer, since his replies run long
Assume a bill will advance on its own after the vote
Josh Gottheimer.warning_sign: By default he is very outgoing and talks at length, which is his usual pattern. When his replies cut off mid thought, he is on guard, so pause and ask the one question that matters.
Josh Gottheimer.follow_up: Within two days, write his office a short page naming the cross party colead and the dated next step.
Josh Gottheimer.personality: Gottheimer is a very outgoing member who is very agreeable and stays warm in tone. His public talk ranges across a far broader set of issues than nearly any colleague. He crosses party lines far more often than typical colleagues, and his bills span a very large mix of issues. Carrying bills through to passage is a weak spot for him. His answers run long, and the longest ones stretch well past typical length. His exposure runs well above his role, and in hearings he pushes harder than most.
Josh Gottheimer.speaks: His pace runs a bit quicker than typical colleagues. Volume varies much less than typical, and pitch rises and falls a bit more than typical. Answers run long, he trails off less than most, and speech is full of filler. He draws his argument from broad themes more than details, and his feeling is easy to hear. In hearings he pushes harder than most, and his tone shifts with the room.
Josh Gottheimer.decides: Before backing it he weighs whether colleagues from the other side join in, and a case built on results earns his time. Pressure from outside lands hard with him, so organized support from several sides carries more weight than one loud push. His follow through is weak, so a commitment from him needs a dated step to hold with a named owner.

archetype.justification: Crosses party lines far more often than most, and talks at a slower pace with longer pauses than nearly any colleague.

Josh Harder.bottom_line: Bring a clear, specific ask backed by outside voices, since they move him more than most members.
do: Bring people the policy would help and let them tell their stories
Agree a next step and its owner before he leaves
Bring a cosponsor from the other side who can speak to the ask
dont: Assume a verbal yes will carry the ask on its own
Fill his pauses with extra arguments before he answers
Josh Harder.warning_sign: By default hearings draw less fight from him than from most members. If he starts pressing his points hard in a hearing, he has stopped treating your ask as settled, so return to the facts and give him room.
Josh Harder.follow_up: Mail his office a brief written recap of the request, the next step, who owns it, and a target date.
Josh Harder.personality: Harder reads as somewhat reserved and a little practical, and he handles details more loosely than most. He is more easily stirred up than most, and his language is somewhat more charged than most. Crossing party lines and joining bills across the aisle comes more readily than most. The bills he carries cover a wider mix of topics than most, and he is less reliable than most about seeing bills through. He is a deliberate speaker in a room, which reads as careful rather than quick.
Josh Harder.speaks: His tempo is among the slowest in the House, and his pauses between phrases outlast nearly any colleague's. Volume and pitch vary more than nearly anyone's, so delivery moves up and down through a sentence. Most of his recorded speech comes from the House floor, where he sounds deliberate and varied rather than clipped. In hearings he runs less combative than most members, and he keeps a level tone when pressed.
Josh Harder.decides: Outside pressure moves him more than most members, so an ask backed by outside voices carries more weight. His bills cover a wider mix of issues than most, so he weighs an ask against the other areas it touches. Support from across the aisle can carry weight with him, since he reaches across the aisle beyond most colleagues. Bills get carried through less reliably than most, so any choice requires a named next step before it holds.

archetype.justification: Blue Jay fits: he is fairly outgoing, holds his ground when challenged, and his wording is sharper than nearly any senator's.

Josh Hawley.bottom_line: Open with the people a policy helps, and expect outside voices to weigh more heavily with him.
do: Make each point short, since his own answers run much briefer
In a hearing, answer each challenge in one line and move on
Bring a story about a family or town the policy helps
dont: Count on a long memo to carry the case
Take his sharp wording as a sign he is hostile
Josh Hawley.warning_sign: He usually talks fast, fires back when challenged, and fills his talk with filler. If he goes quiet and stops rebutting, he is on guard, so back off and offer him a concrete way to say yes.
Josh Hawley.follow_up: Mail his aides a brief page digest of the request within two days and seek a yes or no by a set date.
Josh Hawley.personality: Hawley is outspoken and fairly outgoing, and he digs in when pushed. His wording is sharper than nearly any senator's, and he keeps his talk to fewer subjects than others. He is far looser with details than colleagues are, and less reliable at votes and bills, yet visible for his role. In a room he argues hard and keeps answers short and direct.
Josh Hawley.speaks: He talks fast, and his pitch swings more sharply than nearly any senator's. Wording is blunt and forceful, and it reads a little cooler than others. He answers in brief runs, seldom trails off, and fills his talk with a lot of filler. Fewer subjects come up, and talk about his work carries less detail than others. His pauses are short, which keeps the pace quick.
Josh Hawley.decides: He gauges a request by how well it aids people in their towns. Skepticism is strong, and outside voices push him harder than they push others. Holding his ground when challenged, a challenge hardens his position rather than moving it. He stands out for his role, his bills span fewer areas than nearly any senator's, and he is less reliable at votes, so promises hold only when written.

archetype.justification: Among the most outgoing members in the House, and very curious, the facts that earn the Dolphin pick.

Josh Riley.bottom_line: Come with a question he can explore, and give him room to work it through out loud. Bring outside voices, since outside pushes land harder with him.
do: Ask him one curious question first and let him expand
Name the people outside the room who want the change
If he starts a long answer, let him finish before you reply
dont: Read his long pauses as hesitation or doubt
Assume his agreement holds if outside pressure drops off
Josh Riley.warning_sign: He usually leaves long pauses between phrases, and by default he stays curious rather than sharp in hearings. If he goes quiet and his volume climbs mid thought, he is weighing a new point, so leave space and ask what would make it fit.
Josh Riley.follow_up: Within a day, send him a short note with the question you explored, the people backing it, and the step each of you owns.
Josh Riley.personality: Riley brings a very outgoing style and is very curious, so he arrives eager to explore an issue out loud. He is careful and organized, and fairly reliable at seeing bills through. His bill coverage runs somewhat thinner than most, and his public account of his job is somewhat less careful and detailed than most. That combination makes him a curious explorer who still tends to finish what he starts.
Josh Riley.speaks: Pace runs at a somewhat slower clip than most, and his volume swings much more than most. Pauses between phrases run much longer than most, and his issue range runs somewhat narrower than most. His public account of his job is somewhat less careful and detailed than most. In hearings his manner runs somewhat less combative than the typical member.
Josh Riley.decides: A request earns his interest if it matches what he is curious about and can hold up to his follow up questions. Pressure from beyond the chamber shifts him far more than most members, so support can change where he lands. He is fairly reliable once he commits, so an ask he backs needs someone tracking each step to reach a vote.

archetype.justification: Her manner is outgoing, and she is fairly visible in her role, so a big idea with a shared role suits her.

Joyce Beatty.bottom_line: Lead with the big idea, then bring a joint role she can announce. She sees bills through much less reliably than most, so get commitments in writing.
do: Bring a new idea for the joint role, and present it face to face
Meet her words plainly when they run somewhat sharper than most
Skip sparring with her if you testify before her in a formal hearing
Close by naming the one person on her side who will carry the next step
dont: Assume a bill has moved because a meeting went well
Count on outside groups to carry the ask, since pressure shifts her less than most
Stack several asks into one first meeting with her
Joyce Beatty.warning_sign: In hearings she is usually more combative than most, and her questions land hard. If her hearing questions soften and she accepts short answers, she has stopped pressing that point. Drop that point for now, and go back to the question she still presses.
Joyce Beatty.follow_up: Send her chief of staff a written reply within a few days that restates the joint role and lists each step with its date.
Joyce Beatty.personality: Beatty ranks as one of the most outgoing figures in the House, and one of its most curious. She is fairly organized and fairly agreeable. Her public words are heavy with feeling, much more than most members. Getting worked up comes somewhat quicker to her than to most. Across party lines she builds less than most, and she is fairly visible in her role.
Joyce Beatty.speaks: Her public words carry strong emotion, more than most speakers do, so keep your own reply level. Delivery runs somewhat quicker than most, with shorter gaps between phrases. Her wording lands sharper than most, and her pitch sounds flatter than most. Formal replies call for crispness, since she is a notch more combative than most in hearings. Let her finish a full point before you answer, since her pauses are short.
Joyce Beatty.decides: Pushing from outside groups moves her less than most members, so build a case that can stand alone. She has spoken about a mentor who urged her past barriers, so mention help like that only where it honestly fits. Let her shape the wording of any shared credit before it goes public. Her follow-through runs much weaker than most members, so book a check-in to confirm each step moved.

archetype.justification: His more careful, detailed talk, wider bill range, and low visibility fit a studious, low key member.

Juan Ciscomani.bottom_line: Bring written, technical evidence early, since it suits how he weighs an ask. Pressure from outside moves him more, so line up the support first.
do: Share the technical detail and sources before you meet
Line up colleagues from the other side who have joined bills
Set a dated check on each commitment before you leave
dont: Fill his short pauses with extra argument
Assume more pressure will settle the question quickly
Juan Ciscomani.warning_sign: By default he keeps a practical tone, and he is a bit sharper in hearings. When his hearing questions turn sharp and he piles on detail, he is wary, so ask one plain question about the step he needs.
Juan Ciscomani.follow_up: Within two days, send his office a written summary of the sources and the dated check on each step.
Juan Ciscomani.personality: Ciscomani shows a fairly outgoing side and a little practical streak, and he is hard to rattle. He describes his work in precise terms, and his bills cover a wider mix of issues. Across the aisle, his work runs somewhat above typical members, and carrying bills to the finish is a clear strength. He draws a low profile, and in hearings he takes a sharper line than most.
Juan Ciscomani.speaks: He describes his work in precise terms, and his speech stays close to specifics. Points arrive with exact detail and few digressions. In hearings his tone sharpens, since he takes the point further than typical. His delivery is even and low key, so the content carries the point in every setting. Listeners get the substance first, and the framing follows.
Juan Ciscomani.decides: He reviews a request by the fit with the wider mix of issues he already handles, and a technical case earns his attention. Outside voices carry more force with him than a lone colleague does, so organized backing matters. He is among the most dependable at seeing bills through, but his profile is low, so a named colleague should watch each step closely.

archetype.justification: His quiet manner and low profile for his role stand out, with a fairly careful temperament and a fairly reliable record on votes and bills.

Juan Vargas.bottom_line: Keep the ask short and specific. A clear, direct case fits him better than a long pitch.
do: Bring the results and facts on one page, sent a few days ahead
Name members from both parties who already support the ask
Give each point its outcome first, then the fact behind it
Scope the ask to a first step he can carry through
dont: Build the plan around him fronting it in public
Let the ask lapse when the first meeting ends without a yes
Count on outside pressure alone to win his yes
Juan Vargas.warning_sign: In hearings he usually runs more combative than most members. If his tone turns even milder than that usual edge, he has stopped weighing the point. Drop it for now, and return with one result he can check.
Juan Vargas.follow_up: Send his legislative director a recap of the points you covered, with an owner for each next step, by Thursday.
Juan Vargas.personality: Vargas keeps a quiet, reserved manner, and he is quite hard to rattle. He is fairly orderly, and the bills he moves reach a somewhat broader set of areas. He crosses party lines as often as almost anyone in the House. In public words about the job, few colleagues are more careful and detailed. For his role, he is among the least seen members of the House. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee.
Juan Vargas.speaks: His volume swings far more than nearly any colleague's on the House floor. On the House floor, pace is somewhat slower than most. Few members use words with as little feeling as his, so keep the case to the substance. In hearings he runs more combative than most members, so hold your points to the facts. Let each point land before you add the next.
Juan Vargas.decides: Outside pressure moves his positions more than most, so a visible outside ask is worth the effort. His follow-through is fairly solid, so once he gives a yes, stop re-selling the case and keep the next meeting short. Results he can check himself carry more weight than broad promises. End by asking which claim he would most like to verify first.

archetype.justification: She talks across a very wide range of issues, her bills cover many areas, and she is very visible with a community focus.

Judy Chu.bottom_line: Bring the people her ask helps and pick one concrete step. Human stories about who benefits move her, so keep the next move tied to one of them.
do: Lead with a human story about who benefits
Keep one concrete step in view, since her replies come in quick bursts
Let her finish each thought before you add a point
dont: Count on a bipartisan pitch to carry her
Rush her with quick questions, since she needs time to answer
Judy Chu.warning_sign: She usually speaks slowly with long pauses and gives full answers in quick runs. If her pauses shorten and her pace picks up, she is on guard, so give her time and the facts in writing.
Judy Chu.follow_up: Afterward, mail a concise memo listing the next move, who owns it, and a date.
Judy Chu.personality: Chu is exacting and organized in her approach, and her public profile is very visible. Curious and fairly agreeable, she has a cooler style that still engages people. Answers run long in conversation and in interviews. Across the aisle she works much less than most, and in meetings she takes charge less than most, so others often lead. Her bills span a wide set of issues.
Judy Chu.speaks: Pace runs much slower than most, and pauses last much longer than most. Replies come in fast, brief clusters much more than most, and answer length is unusually level. Points stay short, and filler runs somewhat higher than most. Words carry a bit more charge than most. Turns arrive quickly, one after another. Pitch stays flatter than most. Filler and pauses both run high in her talk.
Judy Chu.decides: Who it helps and how it fits the broad set of issues she already carries is what she weighs. Community impact moves her, and she is very visible, so people notice when a request is backed. Her broad agenda means a narrow, named step fits her best. So a request sticks when the people it helps are visible and the next step has a set date.

archetype.justification: Very careful and organized, with a somewhat broader issue range and more detailed talk than most.

Julia Brownley.bottom_line: Offer her a shared announcement rather than pressure, since outside pressure moves her less than nearly any member.
do: Give her the lead on a visible step she can announce with you
In a hearing, expect much less combat than with most members
dont: Push for a public announcement before the details are checked
Julia Brownley.warning_sign: In hearings she is usually much less combative. If her questions turn sharp, she is on guard about something, so pause and ask her what the concern is.
Julia Brownley.follow_up: Send her office a short draft of the joint announcement with a named owner for the next step by Friday, then check in once.
Julia Brownley.personality: Brownley stays very careful and organized, and her public talk touches a little more ground than most. Her bills also reach a little further across issues, and she describes her own work in somewhat more detailed terms than most. She represents California. Together these make her a methodical presence in the room, with more ground covered than most. Her talk and her bills point the same way, toward broad but careful coverage.
Julia Brownley.speaks: Her talk about her own work runs somewhat more exact and detailed than most, and she covers a little more ground in public than most. In hearings, combat is much less common in her manner than among most members, so her questions usually read as direct rather than hostile. Her points are thorough rather than heated, and the substance stays at the center of her exchanges.
Julia Brownley.decides: A visible role she can share is her first test, and outside pressure carries less weight with her than with nearly any other member. Since pressure will not carry it, a decision holds for her only when the substance is ready before the public step is set. Her bills reach a little further across issues than most, so an ask fits best when it sits inside the issues her bills already cover.

archetype.justification: Her focus on who is helped, her hard to rattle temperament and her combative hearing manner fit the Bear.

Julia Letlow.bottom_line: Lead with who the policy helps, and back it with people who live the issue. Outside voices sway her less than most, so real stories still carry the ask.
do: Lead with stories of who is helped, not abstract figures
Bring the detail to her staff, since she follows bills through reliably
Brace for a somewhat sharper tone when the hearing starts
dont: Assume outside voices will settle the question for her
Push a hearing point too hard, since she is more combative in that setting
Julia Letlow.warning_sign: In hearings she usually runs a bit more combative than most members, so a sudden guarded tone from her signals she is on guard. Ease off, restate the ask in one plain sentence, and let her reply in her own time.
Julia Letlow.follow_up: Mail her office a brief note on the agreed next step, naming the staffer who follows up and the date due.
Julia Letlow.personality: Letlow is a little less practical than most, and her handling of detail runs looser than most. Rattling her is hard, and few colleagues are harder to unsettle. Her bills touch a far narrower set of topics than most, though she is fairly dependable in following bills through. In hearings she turns a bit more combative, and her public visibility sits a little lower than most.
Julia Letlow.speaks: Her wording carries extra emotional weight compared with most. She describes her work in broader, less exact terms than most, and she covers a narrower set of issues. Personal stories tend to carry her case rather than detailed policy math. In hearings she tends to be more combative than the typical member.
Julia Letlow.decides: Prior to any ask she considers who it helps and whether the people affected are visible. Her bills touch a narrow set of topics, so an ask in her existing areas fits. Outside voices sway her clearly less than most, so the case must come with people who stand behind it. So she moves when the stories are real and the next step is named.

archetype.justification: Her bills span far fewer areas than most, and her public talk stays on a narrow set of topics.

Julie Fedorchak.bottom_line: Bring the written technical file and one specific ask. Outside voices carry a little less pull on her, so let the facts carry the ask.
do: Send the written technical file before the meeting, since she is practical
Lead with what the bill delivers, since she follows bills through reliably
Give her time to pause, since her pitch stays much flatter than most
dont: Skip vague framing, since she is practical
Assume outside pressure alone will change her vote
Julie Fedorchak.warning_sign: In a hearing she usually stays somewhat less combative than most. If she turns sharp or pointed in a hearing, she is on guard. Pause, restate the point plainly, and let her answer.
Julie Fedorchak.follow_up: Within three days, mail her office a single page noting the evidence and the next step.
Julie Fedorchak.personality: Fedorchak is somewhat outgoing, and she is practical in her approach. Details come much looser to her than to most colleagues. Bills span far fewer areas than most, so her footprint stays narrow. Her public talk stays on a much narrower set of topics than most. She is reliable at votes and carrying bills, somewhat more than most colleagues. In hearings, her manner runs somewhat less confrontational than most members. Her focus stays on the bill in front of her.
Julie Fedorchak.speaks: Her talk stays on fewer subjects, much narrower than most. Her delivery runs a little slower than most. Pauses between phrases run somewhat longer than most. Loudness moves somewhat more than most. Her pitch stays much flatter than most. Hearing settings bring a somewhat less combative tone than most members. Her words keep to the bill and largely avoid digressions.
Julie Fedorchak.decides: What counts for her is how well a request fits the bill and the facts behind it. Outside pressure has a little less pull on her than on most. Votes and bills show a somewhat stronger record than most, so commitments tend to hold. Bills cover a narrow range of issues, so a request inside her lane fits. She backs asks that come with a clear next step and a practical plan. So a request that names owners and dates is the one she moves on.

archetype.justification: She talks and legislates on a narrow range of issues, with flat, even delivery and low visibility in the chamber.

Julie Johnson.bottom_line: Come with one specific, well documented ask and let her reach the conclusion. Public campaigns sway her less than most colleagues, so bring the substance, not the crowd.
do: Ask for private time, since her profile in public stays low
Let the written case make the argument, not a crowd
dont: Count on outside groups to bring her around for you
Julie Johnson.warning_sign: A general meeting will not tell you whether she has read the written terms or agreed to them. Before you leave, ask her to confirm the next step in her own words.
Julie Johnson.follow_up: Email her office a brief note that restates your request, names the next action and who handles it, and sets a date.
Julie Johnson.personality: Johnson keeps a narrow lane and stays in it. Her speech and her bills both cover few issues, and her words carry less charge and less detail than most colleagues. Visibility is a step below her peers, so her work reads quietly rather than loudly. Texas shapes her base, and her standing comes from focus on a few issues she knows well.
Julie Johnson.speaks: Her pitch barely moves, and her volume stays a little more level than most voices in the chamber. Breaks between phrases come quickly, so she tends to keep moving through a point. Her words carry less charge and less detail than most, and she keeps to the issues she already names. She keeps one register across most of what she says.
Julie Johnson.decides: She sizes a request by how snugly it aligns with the topics she already covers. Phone calls and rallies count for less to her than to most colleagues. She is less visible than most, so a proposal can stall unless someone in her office carries the work. A decision with her needs a named next step and an owner, so a yes in the room needs a written step to stick.

archetype.justification: Her words are a little warmer and a little sharper than most, and people-first cases fit her.

Kat Cammack.bottom_line: Put the people your plan reaches first, and keep the tone warm and direct. Her wording runs a little sharper than most, so keep the words plain.
do: Send a short write-up of the families the plan would reach, ahead of the meeting
Open warmly and name the human stakes in plain words
Separate her point from her phrasing before you answer it
Build the ask on a bill she has already seen through
dont: Re-run the same pitch after she has declined
Fill her silence with your own argument, since she holds the floor less than most
Pile several questions into one turn, since her answers run long
Kat Cammack.warning_sign: Her sentences usually land complete, and she rarely trails off. If her sentences start trailing off and her points go unfinished, she has stopped weighing the ask. Pause and ask what single point would move her next.
Kat Cammack.follow_up: Send her staff a brief note within two days, listing who owns each step and the day it is due.
Kat Cammack.personality: Cammack is very reliable on votes and bills, and very agreeable. Her wording sounds more careful and detailed than most. Her tone reads a touch warmer than most speakers do. Across party lines she builds a bit more than most, and she leans practical. Her answers run longer than nearly any other member of the House. Her words cut a bit sharper than most.
Kat Cammack.speaks: In interviews her longest answers stretch further than nearly any other member. Her replies swing between long and short more than almost any colleague's. Her replies arrive in fast bursts, much more than most. Sharper phrasing shows up more than most. Her filler is light, less than most speakers. Give her long answers room, and take one point at a time.
Kat Cammack.decides: Lean on her cross-party record, since she builds across the aisle somewhat more than most. Outside voices sway her somewhat less than most members, and the case must stand alone. She has told the story of bringing her daughter onto the floor during debate, and that is honest common ground where it fits. End by settling a decision date with her, in writing.

archetype.justification: She is very outgoing, her talk runs buoyant, and she flares up more easily than most.

Katherine Clark.bottom_line: Keep the ask brief and lively, since she is very outgoing. Lock the next step in writing, since bill follow through is weaker for her.
do: Open with the upside, since her talk runs buoyant
Let her finish a thought before you reply, since she trails off more than most
Confirm the dated next step in writing before the meeting closes
dont: Read her brisk replies as dismissal
Rely on one meeting to lock in a commitment
Katherine Clark.warning_sign: She usually answers in brisk runs with some thoughts left open, so that is normal for her by default. If her pauses lengthen and she goes quiet, she has stepped back, so restate the point in one sentence and ask what she needs.
Katherine Clark.follow_up: Send her a written note with the dated next step within two days, and ask her office to confirm it.
Katherine Clark.personality: Clark reads as very outgoing and flares up easily, more than most. Details come looser from her than from most colleagues, and her bills span somewhat fewer issue areas. Her words run more upbeat than most, and she is very visible in the House. She serves as the House whip for her party, a role that keeps her in front of colleagues.
Katherine Clark.speaks: Answers in interviews stretch somewhat longer than most; the longest replies run longer still. Trailing off happens somewhat more than most, and brisk runs of brief replies come somewhat more often too. Pauses between phrases run longer than most, though only somewhat. Words carry much more upbeat energy than most and somewhat more force. Taken together, the pattern is lively, with interruptions to her own thoughts more common than usual.
Katherine Clark.decides: She is very outgoing and a little skeptical, so a friendly approach gets a hearing but not an automatic yes. Her issue coverage in bills is somewhat narrower, so a request that stays inside the areas she already works on is easier to take up. Follow through on bills is weak for her, so a commitment only holds when it has a dated owner and a written step.

archetype.justification: Her wider bill range, looser detail work and quicker emotional reactions fit a wide-ranging style.

Kathy Castor.bottom_line: Offer a visible shared role, and put the next step on paper. She works across the aisle less than almost anyone, so a joint frame needs more backing.
do: Offer a shared role she can announce with a colleague
Put the next step on paper, since follow through is somewhat weaker than most
dont: Count on outside pressure alone to lock in her support
Assume a quick yes will hold once the meeting ends
Kathy Castor.warning_sign: A general meeting will not tell you how she handles a plan that slips, so ask someone who has worked with her for that read. Confirm the step in writing so there is a clear trace of what she agreed to.
Kathy Castor.follow_up: Send her a short written recap of the step, its owner and its date within two days.
Kathy Castor.personality: Castor is a little practical and open to a wide range of interests. Emotional charge sits a bit higher in her wording, and she reacts a bit faster when pressed. She is less careful with detail than almost anyone. Across the aisle she works less than almost anyone, and her bills cover a somewhat wider range than most. Her follow through is somewhat weaker than most colleagues'.
Kathy Castor.speaks: Her pace runs far slower than most, with pauses shorter than nearly any colleague's. Volume jumps far more than most, so her delivery has peaks. Emotional charge rides higher in her public words than most colleagues'. She is less careful with detail than almost anyone, so her talk runs looser. Her pauses are short, so she seldom leaves a silence before she moves on.
Kathy Castor.decides: She judges whether a request fits the areas she already works on. Outside pressure moves her less than most members, so a repeated request has less force. At carrying bills to passage she is a bit less dependable, so every choice needs a named owner. She works across the aisle less than almost anyone, so a joint bill needs more backing. Her choices hold when a written step carries a named owner and a due date.

archetype.justification: Her phrasing runs somewhat more social and gentler than most, and her language is far more emotionally charged than most, which fits the Hummingbird's expressive style.

Katie Britt.bottom_line: Bring the people the bill helps and outside voices who back the ask. Pressure has more pull on her than most, so pair the story with a written step.
do: Open with a story about the families the bill would help
Confirm each agreed step in writing and check it weekly
dont: Assume a warm first meeting will carry the commitment
Treat her quick pace as a sign she agrees
Katie Britt.warning_sign: She usually talks fast and keeps answers short, with pitch and volume that hold to one level. If she stretches her answers and her voice rises, she feels strongly about the point. Ask her what matters most to her, then respond to that.
Katie Britt.follow_up: Within two days, email her team a single written page covering the agreed step and its owner.
Katie Britt.personality: Britt is less practical than most and a little skeptical, and she is quicker to react than most colleagues. Her phrasing is more emotive than most, and somewhat gentler and more social than colleagues'. She spreads her bills across somewhat more areas than most, yet she is much less dependable at seeing them through. Cooperation across the aisle runs somewhat lower than most, and she draws less public attention than most.
Katie Britt.speaks: Tempo runs well quicker than most colleagues'. Pauses between phrases rank among the briefest in the chamber, and loudness stays much more level than most. Pitch barely moves, flatter than nearly any colleague's. Phrasing carries more emotive weight than most, and somewhat gentler than most. Answers run somewhat shorter than most, with fewer filler words. Her manner is fast and clipped, with little emphasis from the voice.
Katie Britt.decides: Who it helps is her test for a request, and pressure from outside counts for more with her than with most. Her bills reach across somewhat more areas than most colleagues', and she cooperates across the aisle less often than most. Conversations are led less by her than by most colleagues, and she is much less dependable when it comes to carrying bills forward. So a decision from her holds when a written next step has a named owner.

archetype.justification: His quick, short replies and flat wording stand out, and his work talk runs loose on detail.

Keith Self.bottom_line: Keep your points short and plain, since his answers arrive quickly and carry little filler.
do: Name who acts on each step, and by which date
Ask one question per turn, as his answers come back in brief runs
Hold the floor for your own points, since he rarely takes charge
Keep your voice level when the meeting turns formal
dont: Read his short, plain wording as doubt
Bank on one long answer to carry the point, since his longest replies run brief
Lead with warm small talk, because his tone runs much cooler
Keith Self.warning_sign: His answers usually end complete, and he rarely trails off as a rule. If he starts trailing off mid-thought, he has drifted onto another topic. Stop, and let him return to the point before you add anything.
Keith Self.follow_up: Send his legislative director a short memo of open questions by Wednesday, written in plain words.
Keith Self.personality: Self is quite practical, and his details run much looser than most. His words come across much cooler than most, and they are flatter than nearly any colleague's. In hearings he is one of the most combative members of the House. The bills he moves reach far fewer areas than most, and his public talk covers a narrow set of topics.
Keith Self.speaks: His pace on the House floor is much slower than most members. In interviews his answers run shorter than nearly any colleague's, and often arrive in quick, short runs. His speech carries little filler, and his words focus on what gets done more than nearly any colleague's. On the floor, his volume swings much more than most. Keep your questions short, since his replies come quickly and plainly.
Keith Self.decides: Outside voices shift his positions more than most, so repeated contact from groups can register. Put the next step first, since he takes charge of conversations much less than most. He answers in quick bursts much more than most, so note the point he settles on before you move on. End by asking which point he finds most useful, and why.

archetype.justification: She talks in careful detail, her bills cover few issues, and she reliably sees them through.

Kelly Morrison.bottom_line: Come with one specific ask and the detail behind it, then leave her room to answer. Her reserve means she thinks before she speaks.
do: Make the ask in person, since public attention rarely finds her
Give her time to answer before you follow up
Lead with the people the ask would help
Anticipate that she will press less hard than most at testimony
dont: Read a long pause as a refusal
Hurry her into a decision on the spot
Kelly Morrison.warning_sign: She usually stays low key, even in hearings, so any shift in that manner is the signal. When she turns sharp in tone, she is on guard, and more force will only harden her. Give her room and let the ask settle.
Kelly Morrison.follow_up: Send her office a single page written summary of the ask and its backing by the end of that week, asking staff to name the next step.
Kelly Morrison.personality: Morrison is reserved and rarely draws attention in the chamber. Public remarks from her keep to a tight range of topics, delivered in careful, detailed terms. Her bills cover few areas, yet she carries each one through. In hearings, she is noticeably less confrontational than her colleagues. Reserve means a few words from her carry weight in a room. Her seat on the Small Business committee fits that focus.
Kelly Morrison.speaks: She talks slowly and at a deliberate pace, with long pauses between phrases. Volume swings up and down more than nearly any colleague's, so emphasis comes in shifts rather than force. She frames issues in careful, specific terms and stays within a narrower set of topics. Under the formal pressure of a hearing she is noticeably less confrontational than most.
Kelly Morrison.decides: Her judgment rests on how neatly a request matches the handful of topics she already carries and on whether it can be completed. Outside voices shift her position more than they shift most colleagues, so the people who back an ask matter as much as the ask. Her reserve keeps her from committing until the path is clear. So a decision sticks only when people back home stand behind it and a next step is named.

archetype.justification: His careful detailed work, reserved manner and ties across the aisle fit a deliberate style.

Ken Calvert.bottom_line: Bring the facts ahead in writing and let him set the pace. He crosses party lines more than most, so a shared bill helps him commit.
do: Send the facts ahead in writing so he can read them first
In a hearing, expect an even tone and plan a follow up question
Agree a dated next step and put it on paper
dont: Treat a polite nod as a firm commitment before it is in writing
Ken Calvert.warning_sign: He usually keeps his replies even in length and rarely takes over a conversation. If he abruptly takes over the exchange and presses one point, read it as guarded, so slow down and check the next step with him.
Ken Calvert.follow_up: Mail him a single page recap listing the step, who owns it and the date.
Ken Calvert.personality: Calvert is a reserved, careful member who is hard to rattle and reaches bipartisan ground more than most. His talk about his work is far more precise than most colleagues. He leans a little toward the practical, and his public talk centers on a somewhat tighter field of topics than most, though his bills span somewhat more areas. In hearings he is among the least confrontational in the chamber. He is dependable on roll calls and in carrying bills forward.
Ken Calvert.speaks: His answers run a bit longer than most in interviews, with the longest stretches longer still. His words are flat without much upbeat energy. Filler words appear less often in his talk than in most colleagues' talk. He rarely trails off mid answer, so his points tend to finish. His turns come in long runs rather than quick bursts, with answer length that stays even. Hearings find him among the least combative members in the House.
Ken Calvert.decides: Before backing anything he checks how it fits the bills he already carries, which span a wider field than most. Work across the aisle makes him open to a shared deal, since he joins bills with the other party more than most. His follow through is dependable, so a plan written down tends to hold. So a decision holds with him when the next step is written down and clearly owned.

archetype.justification: He is fairly curious and fairly careful, and his bills span a wider set of issues than nearly any peer's.

Kevin Cramer.bottom_line: Bring a written, technical case and name the colleagues across the aisle who already back it. Outside voices sway him strongly, so trusted voices from home help.
do: Give the technical detail in the order the mechanism runs
Warm up the conversation with a personal word before the ask
Agree a next step and its date before the meeting ends
dont: Treat a quick nod as a settled commitment
Sharpen your tone when a hearing gets tense
Kevin Cramer.warning_sign: He usually talks fast and fills his sentences with filler words. If the filler drops out and his voice goes flat, he is weighing a concern, so hand him a single fact he can repeat.
Kevin Cramer.follow_up: Send a written summary of the agreed step, in a short memo naming its owner, to his legislative aide by Friday.
Kevin Cramer.personality: Cramer is very agreeable and warm in his manner, and he reaches across the aisle more than nearly any colleague. His bills span a wide set of issues, and he sees them through with dependable follow up. His public words carry strong emotional charge, and he is fairly forceful when he makes a point. In the chamber he stays fairly visible given his post, and he represents North Dakota.
Kevin Cramer.speaks: He talks very fast with short pauses, and his volume stays even while his pitch swings noticeably more than colleagues do. His answers in interviews are brief on average, though his longest ones run long, and he fills sentences with filler words more than almost anyone. Public words are warm and somewhat forceful, and they run gentler than most. In a hearing his tone runs far softer than his peers, so expect a civil exchange.
Kevin Cramer.decides: For him the technical facts must hold up, and whether a colleague from across the aisle already backs it counts as well. His bills span many issues, so an ask inside his areas tends to land. Pressure from outside weighs on him heavily, so a decision holds when trusted people from home support it and someone is named to follow through.

archetype.justification: Crossing into the opposing bloc he does much less than most, detail is loose for him, and his words are as emotionally charged as anyone's.

Kevin Hern.bottom_line: Lead with the outcome and keep the ask short. He builds across party lines much less than most, and outside calls carry less weight with him.
do: Bring a one-page results case that names the outcome in its first line
Ask early with one short question, since his answers arrive in brief bursts
Let his longer answers run, since his longest replies stretch somewhat past most
Leave room before he answers, since a push counts clearly less with him
dont: Bring the request back only with new facts in hand
Pitch the plan as a cross-party deal
Frame the plan as an ideal rather than a set of actions
Kevin Hern.warning_sign: He usually finishes his sentences, much more than most. If he starts leaving them unfinished, the point is not settled yet. Narrow to a single next step, and name what would close the question.
Kevin Hern.follow_up: By Wednesday, mail his office a short memo that spells out what the plan delivers, lists the next action and whoever owns it, and sets the due date.
Kevin Hern.personality: Hern counts among the most practical members in the House; he is much looser on specifics than most. His bills reach a slightly narrower set of issues, and across party lines he builds much less than most. He flares up quickly and runs hot much more than most colleagues. Publicly, his tone is much cooler than most. At hearings though he is a bit less combative than most colleagues.
Kevin Hern.speaks: His talk covers a narrower range of issues, and detail on his work is much thinner than most, so keep your own points concrete. Interviews show longer turns than most, yet he seldom takes charge of the talk and rarely trails off. His answers arrive in brief bursts, so let each answer finish before you add a point. In hearings he leans a little less hard into a point than colleagues do. On recordings his volume stays very even, and his pitch runs somewhat flatter than most, so keep your own tone even and end with one clear next step.
Kevin Hern.decides: Results are what fit his framing best, so set the outcome against what happens today without the plan, in numbers. Few members are more practical, so walk him through how the plan runs day to day. If it reaches a hearing, where he presses a bit less hard, have the same figures ready to hand, so he can check them on the spot.

archetype.justification: Fairly curious, careful and organized, and much more detailed than most when describing his work.

Kevin Kiley.bottom_line: Bring a detailed written case and a clear ask. Get the commitment in writing, as his record on bills ranks among the least reliable.
do: Bring a question he can explore, since he is fairly curious
Line up outside supporters, since outside voices reach him more than most
Confirm the next step in writing before you leave
dont: Cut off a long answer before he reaches the point
Assume his gentle tone means he has already agreed
Kevin Kiley.warning_sign: He usually gives wordy answers full of filler that trail off, by default. If his answers shorten and his pitch goes flat, he is on guard or losing interest. Stop, ask what part of the plan he is holding back, and wait for his reply.
Kevin Kiley.follow_up: Put the next step, plus its owner, in a written note for him inside two days, since his follow through is uneven.
Kevin Kiley.personality: Kiley is fairly curious and careful and organized, and much more detailed than most when describing his work. He is quite agreeable, and his words run much gentler than most. Across his bills he touches a few fewer topics than most, and he is less reliable at seeing them through than most. His role makes him very visible, and he uses a great deal of filler.
Kevin Kiley.speaks: He talks much longer in interviews than most, and his top answers run well past the usual length. Pitch swings far more widely than most, while his pace outruns almost every other member. He uses more filler than almost anyone, and his answers trail off more than most. What he says carries a little less emotion than most, and his manner stays gentle in the room.
Kevin Kiley.decides: He weighs an ask on the detail behind it. Pressure from outside gets through to him more than to most members, so outside voices can shift his view. Across his bills he touches a few fewer topics than most, so an ask fits best inside his own areas. A plain written case gives him something concrete to check. At finishing bills he sits among the weakest members, so a decision sticks only once the next step carries a name.

archetype.justification: Ox fits because his case stays on what the policy delivers, his bills reach fewer issues, and his delivery is slow and even.

Kevin Mullin.bottom_line: Lead with what the policy delivers, then ask for one step he can own. Outside groups carry little weight with him, so the reason must do the work.
do: Open with the result the policy produces, in a few direct sentences
Give him a short written summary he can check against the bill
Match his slower pace and leave room between points
In a hearing, expect civil questions and answer them plainly
dont: Assume a verbal yes will carry through without a written step
Count on outside pressure to change his position
Kevin Mullin.warning_sign: He usually presses gently, so a sharp edge in his questions is the signal. When he presses sharply, he is losing patience or getting on guard. Stop, ask what he needs, and offer a shorter step.
Kevin Mullin.follow_up: Email him a brief recap of the ask and the next step, naming who acts and by when.
Kevin Mullin.personality: Mullin keeps his talk brief and plain, and he rarely lingers on the detail of his own work. His bills reach fewer areas than most, and his follow through trails nearly everyone in the House. In hearings he is among the least combative members. Before entering politics he ran a local business and served as a district director. He wants facts to carry the case, not rhetoric.
Kevin Mullin.speaks: Delivery is slow and even, with a flat pitch and little rise in volume. Pauses between phrases run somewhat longer than most. Descriptions of his bills stay loose, with little detail. In hearings he is among the least combative members, so his questions come across evenly. Overall the manner is quiet and even, which suits a member who says less about the details of his own work.
Kevin Mullin.decides: Pitches get weighed on whether they deliver a clear result and sit within the few issue areas he already works on. A short direct case earns his attention faster than a long one. Pressure from outside groups carries less weight with him, so the case has to stand on its own. Follow through is among the weakest in the House, so a decision holds only when a named next step is set.

archetype.justification: Warm, social wording and heavy emotional charge fit a quick, lively speaker who answers in short bursts.

Kim Schrier.bottom_line: Open with who the plan helps, and bring outside voices who back it, since outside pressure moves her more than almost any member.
do: Put the human stakes first, in a few short sentences
Keep points brief, since she answers in quick bursts
Name the outside groups that back the ask
dont: Rely on a private push alone to move her
Mistake her warm tone for a firm commitment
Kim Schrier.warning_sign: She usually holds her position when pressed, and her replies come in quick bursts. If she goes quiet instead of pushing back, she is weighing the ask rather than rejecting it. Restate the one point and give her room.
Kim Schrier.follow_up: After the meeting, send her staff a short list of the groups backing the ask, with one next step and its date.
Kim Schrier.personality: Schrier is an organized member who is hard to fluster and rarely leads a conversation. Her public language runs far more charged than typical, and she explains her work in less detailed terms. Her bills cover a bit fewer issues, and she follows bills through somewhat less reliably than the typical member. Reserve shows in her manner, yet her public voice carries strong feeling.
Kim Schrier.speaks: Speech moves a bit faster than typical, with a voice that stays even and a pitch that stays flatter than most. Her words carry far more emotional charge than the usual speaker. Her wording is less forceful than nearly any colleague's. Tone stays open, and pitch varies less than most. Answers stay even in length, and she often defends a position when challenged.
Kim Schrier.decides: She looks at who a request helps, and outside voices press her harder than almost any member. Her follow through is somewhat less reliable than most, so a yes holds only when a named person owns the next step. Named allies behind an ask give her a reason to take it seriously. She defends her positions when challenged, so a decision lasts only if the case survives her questions.

archetype.justification: She is somewhat outgoing, very curious, and much more social in her public words than most members.

Kirsten Gillibrand.bottom_line: Lead with an ask that already has backers from the other party, since she works across party lines much more than most.
do: Bring a member from the other party to back the ask
If she pushes back, ask which part she doubts
Give her a visible role in announcing the ask
In a hearing, expect less combat than her public words suggest
dont: Treat her support as the end of the work
Push harder when she digs in on a point
Shut down a new idea before she has tried to act on it
Kirsten Gillibrand.warning_sign: She usually holds her ground when challenged and speaks in an even stream. When she begins repeating her stance again and again, she has turned guarded, so ask what worries her and allow her to finish.
Kirsten Gillibrand.follow_up: Send her staff a short note by Friday listing the backers from the other party and the next vote.
Kirsten Gillibrand.personality: Gillibrand is a very curious, sociable member who likes new ideas and gets worked up quickly, much more than most. She works across party lines much more than most, but she is a little less dependable at seeing bills through. In interviews her answers run much shorter than most, and when challenged she defends her position a little more than most colleagues. Taken together, she is an open dealmaker who holds her ground, so pushback tends to harden her rather than move her.
Kirsten Gillibrand.speaks: At a somewhat quicker clip than most, she keeps pauses between phrases a bit shorter and a volume far more even than most. Pitch stays among the flattest in the chamber, while public wording runs far more social than most but cooler than nearly anyone's. Interview answers run much shorter than most. When challenged, defending her position comes a little more readily than most colleagues.
Kirsten Gillibrand.decides: Who stands behind an ask is what she weighs, since she is far more bipartisan than most. Pushback hardens her position rather than moving it, and she is a little less dependable at seeing bills through. An ask inside areas she already works on fits her. So an ask missing backers from the other party tends to lose momentum with her.

archetype.justification: Her careful framing around people and her much faster delivery fit the Hummingbird's quick, personal style.

Kristen McDonald Rivet.bottom_line: Lead with the people the plan helps, then state the ask in one breath. Pressure from outside moves her more than most, so bring support early.
do: Open briskly with the people the plan helps, since she is fairly outgoing
Tie each point to a person the plan reaches
dont: Drop the people angle from the memo, and it loses her
Skip any plan that depends on one outside backer
Kristen McDonald Rivet.warning_sign: A general meeting will not tell you how she handles a plan once it reaches her staff. Ask for the staff's next written step before the meeting ends, and note the answer the same day.
Kristen McDonald Rivet.follow_up: Send her staff a one page note naming the people the plan helps, by Friday.
Kristen McDonald Rivet.personality: McDonald Rivet works with great care and keeps her material organized, and she gives her work somewhat more detailed treatment than most. Her public focus stays on a small set of subjects, much narrower than most. Somewhat outgoing, she has a people first lens from her background running Michigan Head Start. Her legislation also touches somewhat fewer areas than most colleagues.
Kristen McDonald Rivet.speaks: Her delivery runs much quicker than most colleagues, with shorter pauses between phrases, and her talk stays on a small set of subjects. She gives her work a somewhat more textured, specific account than most. Put together, she moves through a point briskly, pausing only briefly, and she returns to the same few themes rather than wandering across many topics.
Kristen McDonald Rivet.decides: She weighs a plan by the people it reaches, and her background running Head Start makes that lens second nature. Outside pressure moves her more than most. Her bills touch somewhat fewer areas than most, so a plan that serves one clear group with a narrow, concrete reach holds her attention. A plan that spreads across many groups loses her focus.

archetype.justification: Orca fits: she is very outgoing and easily stirred, and her words carry a heavier emotional load than most.

LaMonica McIver.bottom_line: Offer her something to announce together with you, then ask for one concrete step. Public pushing counts for more with her than with most, so a broad push helps.
do: Offer a joint announcement or event she can share with you
Ask for a clear commitment, since she follows through on most bills
Bring outside voices who back the ask before the meeting
dont: Rely on one argument alone, since public pushing counts for more with her
LaMonica McIver.warning_sign: She usually talks readily and is outgoing. When she goes quiet and clips a point short, that signals guardedness, so ask what worries her. In a hearing she is among the least combative, so watch for a sharp exchange.
LaMonica McIver.follow_up: Within three days, email her team a one sheet note on the shared plan, naming each step and its owner.
LaMonica McIver.personality: McIver shows very lively energy and gets roused fast, much more than most. Her words carry a heavier emotional load than most, and she covers a much narrower set of subjects. She is dependable at seeing bills through, yet her profile stays low, even for her role. Statements from her come across as direct and charged, even when her public visibility stays slight.
LaMonica McIver.speaks: Her talk covers a narrow set of subjects, and her words are somewhat less careful and detailed than most. Her words carry a heavier emotional load than most, so statements read as direct and heated. In a hearing she is among the least combative members, so her heat shows up in public statements instead.
LaMonica McIver.decides: Whether she has a new announcement to make with you is what she checks first. Her legislation touches only a few subject areas, so an ask inside those areas fits best. Public pushing counts for more with her, so a broad coalition can change her position. She is dependable at seeing bills through, so a decision holds once a named next step is attached.

archetype.justification: His talk covers somewhat fewer issues and he is very practical, so narrow, concrete asks fit him best.

Lance Gooden.bottom_line: Bring one narrow ask with the technical detail written ahead of time. Outside pressure moves him much more than private argument does.
do: Lead with the practical result before any broader framing
Send the technical case in writing before you meet
Tie the ask to outside voices he already hears from
In a hearing, expect sharp questions and answer them directly
dont: Lean on private argument alone, since outside voices move him more
Trade sharp lines with him in a hearing, where he is much more combative
Lance Gooden.warning_sign: In a hearing he usually turns combative and on guard, which is the change you will see. When pressed there, lower the stakes, ask one plain question, and let him finish before answering.
Lance Gooden.follow_up: After the meeting, send a single page written summary with the ask and the next step to his staff lead within two weeks.
Lance Gooden.personality: Gooden is a practical member who favors results over long frames, and he talks about a touch narrower range than most colleagues. He keeps a bit of reserve and runs far looser on details than most. Easily set off, he still reaches across the aisle far more than most. He also draws somewhat less notice than other members, so his narrow focus can go unnoticed.
Lance Gooden.speaks: He talks about a touch narrower range than most, and his wording shows a bit less feeling than most. His manner is plain and direct rather than heated. In a hearing his combative streak runs far above the usual level, and that is where his tone sharpens. Under that pressure he argues each point more fiercely. Witnesses in his hearings face pointed, pressing questions.
Lance Gooden.decides: Before he commits he checks whether it fits his narrow areas and whether it has written technical support behind it. Across the aisle he works much more than most, so a shared bill can win him over. Following bills through is less his strength than for most, and outside pressure moves him much more than argument does. Private assent can fade, so any yes he gives needs a named owner and date to hold.

archetype.justification: Her outgoing, upbeat style and fast, long answers fit a lively talker who keeps conversations moving.

Lateefah Simon.bottom_line: Lead with stories of who the bill helps and let her walk people through them, since outside voices weigh on her more than colleagues.
do: Bring stories of who the bill helps
Let her finish long answers before you reply
Put outside voices in the meeting with her, since she is outgoing
dont: Take her cool wording as a verdict on the bill
Lateefah Simon.warning_sign: Her answers usually come fast and full, so a full reply is normal. If she trails off mid thought and her pace drops, read it as guard rising, so slow down, name the concern, and let her pick the next point.
Lateefah Simon.follow_up: Following the session, send her a short note restating who the bill helps, naming outside supporters, and asking for a reply within two days.
Lateefah Simon.personality: Simon stands among the most outgoing members of the chamber and among its most curious, which makes her a lively, inquisitive presence.
