Beneath that energy she keeps a careful, organized streak, and her descriptions of her work are exacting and detailed. She gets worked up quickly, but her words carry little emotional charge. Her California seat and her Small Business committee role frame the work she describes.
Lateefah Simon.speaks: She talks fast with brief pauses between phrases, and her answers run long, so a conversation can become a long stretch of her speaking. She finishes her sentences rather than trailing off, and public language from her is upbeat and action focused. Gentleness marks her words rather than sharpness, and she gives plenty of detail on a handful of topics. Interview answers swing between long turns and quick runs of short ones, which shows a speaker who moves in bursts.
Lateefah Simon.decides: Requests get weighed by who they help, and outside backing counts for more with her than with colleagues. Follow through on bills is fairly dependable for her, so a commitment she makes tends to hold. She takes charge of a conversation and works a proposal through out loud with colleagues, so a decision needs a named next step to stick.

archetype.justification: Her outgoing manner, emotionally charged wording and fast, even talk fit a quick, sociable communicator.

Laura Friedman.bottom_line: Lead with stories of who the bill helps, because that framing fits her best and the rest of the case follows from it.
do: Bring the people your bill helps into the room
Name the vote she can count on and the date for it
Invite her into the conversation early, since she is outgoing
dont: Assume her lively tone means she has already committed
Go hard on her in a hearing setting
Laura Friedman.warning_sign: Her pattern is normally quick, even speech with short pauses, so speed alone is normal. If she turns combative in a hearing where she tends to run low key, that signals guardedness, so pause, name the concern, and give her room to answer.
Laura Friedman.follow_up: Once the talk concludes, mail her a note naming who the bill helps and the vote she can rely on, and request a reply within two days.
Laura Friedman.personality: Friedman is as sociable as almost anyone, and she gets worked up readily, which keeps her energy high. Her talk about her work is careful and detailed, so her answers come across as thorough. Her follow through on bills is fairly dependable, and her emotional charge marks her public voice. Representing California, she is quieter in public roles than her outgoing manner suggests.
Laura Friedman.speaks: Pace is among the fastest in the chamber, with brief pauses between phrases. Volume stays even to a degree few colleagues match, and pitch runs flatter than colleagues'. Words carry strong emotional charge, and her descriptions of work are careful and detailed. In hearings she is far less combative than colleagues. These are patterns in her public speech, and they describe delivery only.
Laura Friedman.decides: She weighs requests by whether people benefit, since human centered framing suits her best. Her follow through on bills is fairly dependable, so a commitment she makes tends to hold. Outgoing by nature, she engages best when an idea is put to her directly in conversation, so a decision needs a named step she can own. She tends to move when people-centered framing is clear.

archetype.justification: Her reserved manner, very narrow issue focus and slow speech with long pauses fit a slow, deliberate, low profile operator.

Laura Gillen.bottom_line: Bring one narrow ask framed around the people it helps, since outside voices carry more weight with her than with colleagues.
do: Lead with stories about who the ask helps
Keep the ask narrow and tied to the areas she already covers
Bring outside voices from her district to back the ask
dont: Treat her narrow focus as a reason to skip the detail
Push for a quick decision in the first meeting
Laura Gillen.warning_sign: She is normally slow, with long pauses between phrases, so pauses are not a warning. When she presses hard in a hearing where she is usually low key, caution sets in, so stop, name the concern, then give her one specific question.
Laura Gillen.follow_up: Once the session ends, email her a note on the people the ask helps and the outside backers, and ask for a reply by a set date.
Laura Gillen.personality: Gillen is reserved and among the narrowest members in the House when it comes to the range of her public talk and her bills. Her legislation focuses on a very small set of areas, and she is among the least visible members of the chamber. She keeps a reserved, cautious manner in public. In hearings she tends to be less combative than colleagues, and she represents New York.
Laura Gillen.speaks: Delivery is among the slowest in the House, with very long pauses between phrases and a voice that moves up and down more than nearly any colleague's. Pitch runs somewhat flatter than colleagues'. Recorded audio comes from House floor sessions, a setting that differs from interviews. In hearings she is less combative, and her public talk leans on a tight range of topics.
Laura Gillen.decides: She looks first at who benefits, since community impact fits her framing best. Her bills span a very small set of issues, so an ask has to sit squarely within those areas to get traction. Outside backing weighs heavily with her, so a decision needs backers who stay involved until it is settled. She tends to move when community stakes are clear.

archetype.justification: Her descriptions of her work are precise, and she sees bills through more reliably than nearly anyone.

Laurel Lee.bottom_line: Bring one clear result with its facts, in plain words. Since she is reliable on bills, a result she can verify carries weight.
do: Lead with the result the policy delivers, in one or two sentences
Bring the sources behind each figure to the meeting
dont: Push for a public stance before she has the figures
Treat her quiet manner as lack of interest
Laurel Lee.warning_sign: How much detail she needs before signing off will stay hidden in a broad first meeting. Ask early which figure she requires, and bring that figure in writing.
Laurel Lee.follow_up: Email her legislative assistant the agreed step in writing by the next morning, copying the figures used.
Laurel Lee.personality: Lee is reserved in public and practical in outlook, and a bit tougher to unsettle than most colleagues. Her account of her work is precise and thorough, and her language is far less emotional than most. Her bills cover fewer issues, and they are seen through very dependably. A lower public profile than colleagues in her role is kept.
Laurel Lee.speaks: Public talk from her centers on fewer topics than most colleagues use, and she explains her work with exact, thorough detail. Her language is far less charged than most colleagues', so she sounds businesslike. Answers stay within a few topics she knows well. She tends to lead with specifics rather than broad claims, which makes her public statements easy to check.
Laurel Lee.decides: Support from her goes to an ask whose facts are complete and which also fits the few areas she already works in. Her bills cover fewer issues, and a result she can check moves her more than a general appeal. Once convinced, she follows bills through. So a decision from her sticks only when the written record is complete.

archetype.justification: Few House members are as skeptical by default as she is, her public words run sharp, and she is much looser with the detail than most.

Lauren Boebert.bottom_line: Lead with the single result your policy delivers, in a short, direct case. Keep every claim sourced and checkable, since results and facts fit her best.
do: Bring a results case built on what the policy delivers, kept to one page
Let her take charge early, since she tends to steer the conversation
Pick one outcome figure she can verify, and leave out the rest of the totals
Time the pitch to fit one short sitting, and do not overrun it
dont: Let one cool reception end the ask, since pressure shifts her positions more than most
Take her skepticism as a verdict on the whole bill
Assume a hearing with her will stay polite
Lauren Boebert.warning_sign: She usually finishes her lines more cleanly than nearly anybody in the House. If she starts breaking off mid-sentence, that is a change from her usual pattern. Stop, name the one result you need her to weigh, and send a written summary.
Lauren Boebert.follow_up: Within a day, send her staff a short results summary, with the owner of each next step.
Lauren Boebert.personality: Boebert is skeptical and one of the most practical members of the House. She is much more easily stirred up than most House members, and her public talk stays on somewhat fewer topics than most. With the detail, she is much looser than most House members, and few members sponsor bills across a narrower set of topics. Her public language is much more charged than most, and she stays very visible in the House.
Lauren Boebert.speaks: In interviews her answers run shorter than those of nearly anyone. Filler is rare, and she finishes her lines cleanly. Her public words are more upbeat than most, and her wording is far more social than most. Even her longest answers are shorter than almost any other House member's. Quick bursts of reply come more often than most. Keep your own replies short, and let her set the energy in the room.
Lauren Boebert.decides: Pressure from outside moves her clearly more than most, and a clear ask that holds its shape carries weight. Name one ask per meeting, and bring it back at each stage. A result she can check in one line will move her faster than a long explanation. Make your opener short, too. Close with the one vote you need from her, in a sentence.

archetype.justification: She is among the least social members, and her wording is much less charged than most.

Lauren Underwood.bottom_line: Offer a shared role to announce the ask together, and bring the outside voices that move her.
do: Line up outside groups that already support the request
Give her a shared role in announcing the outcome
Lead with facts, since her manner runs cool and flat
dont: Skip small talk, since she does not warm to it
Press her with sharp questions, since her words run somewhat gentler than most
Lauren Underwood.warning_sign: She usually leans on filler words more heavily than almost anyone. When her answers suddenly come out brief and clean, she is on guard. Pause, ask one open question, and let her finish the thought.
Lauren Underwood.follow_up: Within three days, give her office a single sheet naming each outside group that backs the request.
Lauren Underwood.personality: Underwood leans a little reserved, and her public talk covers a far wider field of topics than most colleagues. Yet her bills span far fewer areas than most colleagues do. She is among the least social members, and her words come across as cool. Filler in her answers runs at a level few colleagues match. She keeps her footing somewhat better than most in a tense exchange.
Lauren Underwood.speaks: In conversation, her replies run a little shorter than most. Her wording reads as cool and somewhat flat, with little interest in small talk. Pauses between phrases run much longer than most. Her pitch holds much flatter than most speakers do. Across interviews, answers vary in length somewhat less than most. Her descriptions of her own work come with somewhat less precise detail than most.
Lauren Underwood.decides: She gauges how neatly a request matches the areas she already works in. Backing from outside groups weighs much more on her than on most colleagues. A visible shared role gives her a reason to commit. Being a little reserved, she tends to take in an argument quietly rather than debate it. So a request sticks only when outside backers stand behind it.

archetype.justification: Her bills take in far more issues than most, and her public words describe her work in far less exact detail than most.

Linda Sánchez.bottom_line: Bring one specific ask with a written next step and owner. Her record at seeing bills through is much less dependable than most, and outside voices sway her less.
do: Limit the ask to one bill and its specific change
Confirm which office holds each step before you meet
Check the bill status before the meeting, not after
dont: Count on a yes from the room to hold without a written step
Rely on outside pressure to keep the bill moving
Linda Sánchez.warning_sign: You cannot learn from a general meeting how she handles a bill that has stalled, so ask her staff for its status before you go in. Then name one concrete step, such as the next committee date, and put it in writing before you leave.
Linda Sánchez.follow_up: Send one written step with its owner and date within the same day, then check the bill status a week later.
Linda Sánchez.personality: Sánchez takes on a wide set of bills, and she is much less reliable at seeing each one through. Her public accounts are much thinner in detail than most, and her tone runs somewhat cooler than most. For her role, visibility is somewhat lower than most, and her interests are wide ranging. Her attention runs across many bills, so follow through depends on someone tracking each one.
Linda Sánchez.speaks: Her public accounts are far less exact in detail than most, and her public tone runs somewhat cooler than most. Her language is therefore general and low in heat, and the specifics usually come from a document rather than from her. Generalities leave room for others to supply the detail. She describes the goal more than the mechanics of a bill.
Linda Sánchez.decides: She weighs an ask against the many bills she already carries, and an ask inside her existing work fits her. Because outside pressure sways her less than it sways most members, the merit of the ask has to carry it alone. Her follow through is much less reliable than most, so a verbal yes stays weak until a written step is attached. Commitments slip without a named owner and due date behind them, so an ask that carries both has the best chance with her.

archetype.justification: Very outgoing and much more agreeable than most, with bills across many issues and talk that stays on results.

Lisa Blunt Rochester.bottom_line: Bring an ask with support from across the aisle, backed by outside voices. Her view shifts more readily under outside force, so the coalition behind the ask matters.
do: Meet her in person with a short case on what the policy delivers
Name a colleague on the other side who could sign on as cosponsor
Bring a question she can explore, since she is fairly curious and reliable
dont: Mistake her mild tone for a firm commitment
Leave the coalition unattended after the first meeting
Lisa Blunt Rochester.warning_sign: She usually keeps an even, flat delivery with short pauses and gentle wording. When the pauses stretch out, her volume shifts, and her words sharpen, she is on guard about the ask, so slow down and ask which part worries her.
Lisa Blunt Rochester.follow_up: Then forward her team a one page recap of the results, and ask whether the colleague across the aisle will cosponsor before the month closes.
Lisa Blunt Rochester.personality: Blunt Rochester is very outgoing and much more agreeable than most, and she bridges the aisle somewhat more than the usual member. Her bills touch a far wider spread of issues than most, and she is fairly dependable at seeing them through. Much less charge runs through her words than most, and they run somewhat gentler than most. She reacts a little more readily to friction than most, and she draws much less attention than most.
Lisa Blunt Rochester.speaks: Her delivery is even, with a pitch that stays flat and short pauses between phrases. Ranging across somewhat more topics than most is typical of how she speaks, and her words run gentler than most and much less charged. Manner stays low key, and a position comes across without heat. The volume stays even as a point develops, so listeners follow the words more than the voice.
Lisa Blunt Rochester.decides: She weighs a request by what it delivers and by the people standing behind it. Her bills reach across a broad set of issues, much wider than most, and she is fairly dependable at seeing bills through once she commits. Outside voices tug at her more than most colleagues, and she keeps a low profile, so her support follows the coalition rather than attention she draws. So her support tends to hold when the ask arrives with real outside backing.

archetype.justification: She is quite skeptical, holds firm when pressed, and keeps her votes and bills on track.

Lisa McClain.bottom_line: Bring a checkable plan and let her test it. She holds firm when pressed, so give her room to push back on the details.
do: Lead with the result the policy delivers and stop there
Name the bills she has carried through the chamber
If she challenges a claim, answer it with the source
dont: Treat her long pauses as agreement with the ask
Push a second round of asks before the first one lands
Expect her to accept a claim without testing it
Lisa McClain.warning_sign: Her long pauses between phrases are normal for her, so a silence alone is not a warning. Should she begin defending a point hard while her pauses disappear, she has gone on guard, so step back and concede the small detail.
Lisa McClain.follow_up: Send her a short note with the sources and the next dated step within a day.
Lisa McClain.personality: McClain is quite skeptical and holds firm when pressed. She talks about her own work with careful, detailed attention, and she is very dependable at keeping her votes and bills on track. Bills she carries reach a somewhat wider set of topics than most, and she serves on House Financial Services. Her wording holds much less emotion than most, yet she flares up much more readily than most. She represents Michigan in Congress.
Lisa McClain.speaks: Her wording is careful and detailed, and it carries far less emotion than most. Talking slowly, she pauses well beyond the usual length, so her delivery feels deliberate. Answers come in brisk bursts of brief replies and sometimes cut off, and she holds firm when challenged. Her volume and pitch rise and fall more than most. She keeps answers focused on the case in front of her.
Lisa McClain.decides: She weighs an ask on whether the bill she has carried is in good shape and whether it holds up when she tests it. Reaching across the aisle comes somewhat more readily to her than to most, so shared backing helps. Pressure from outside reaches her less than most members, so a pitch from home counts for less with her. Her bills span a wider set of issues than most, so a request that touches several of them gets a closer look. A commitment from her holds only when the next step is named and checked.

archetype.justification: She reaches across the aisle more than almost anyone, and she carries far more force than the typical member.

Lisa Murkowski.bottom_line: Bring the written evidence early and make the ask one she can carry to the other party. She holds her ground, so let the detail land first.
do: Send the written analysis ahead of the meeting
Name the other members who already back the ask
If she holds the floor, let her finish before you reply
dont: Mistake her upbeat tone for a done deal
Press a second point before she has answered the first
Count her agreeable manner as support already won
Lisa Murkowski.warning_sign: She usually finishes her thoughts and rarely trails off. If she goes quiet mid answer or starts to trail off, she is losing interest, so stop pressing and ask one plain question.
Lisa Murkowski.follow_up: Send her staff a dated list of steps, with the owner and date for each one.
Lisa Murkowski.personality: Murkowski is careful in her habits and hard to fluster. Outgoing and curious, she is also among the most agreeable members of the Senate. Her wording carries far more feeling than most, and she digs in harder than most when challenged. In conversation she holds the floor and keeps replies compact. Alaska is her state, and she is fairly visible.
Lisa Murkowski.speaks: Upbeat and forceful, her wording is cooler than most in warmth. Careful, detailed terms mark how she discusses her own work, and her feeling runs high. Turns come out briefer than nearly any colleague's. When challenged she digs in harder than nearly anyone, yet her wording stays gentle. The focus stays on her record and on the points she has already made.
Lisa Murkowski.decides: She weighs an ask on the written evidence and on whether it can win across the aisle. She reaches across the chamber more than nearly anyone, so a deal she backs tends to get done. Commitments from her hold, as she ranks among the most reliable members at seeing bills through. Pressure from outside moves her more than most members do, so a push from people she trusts counts for a great deal. A commitment from her holds when the next step is written and checked against the evidence.

archetype.justification: Stories of the people a bill reaches move her most, and hearings bring out a sharper edge than typical.

Lizzie Fletcher.bottom_line: Open with the people a bill helps and give her an ask she can check. Her follow through is dependable, so a clear step she owns will hold.
do: Bring stories of the families a bill would help
Agree a named next step and who owns it
In a hearing, expect her to argue her points hard
Match her quick pace and keep points brief
dont: Count an early no as final once outside groups weigh in
Treat her lively, rising voice as a sign she has agreed
Lizzie Fletcher.warning_sign: Her usual pattern is fast, lively talk in which she is quick to engage. When her answers turn sharper than usual in a hearing, she is on guard, so slow down and ask which part worries her.
Lizzie Fletcher.follow_up: Send a short note after the meeting naming the step you agreed and who owns it, dated for the following week.
Lizzie Fletcher.personality: Fletcher is a reserved member who is somewhat curious about new ideas. Reliable at seeing bills through, she still keeps her bills to fewer issues than most. Her wording is much less emotionally charged than typical members, and she gets worked up with a bit more ease. Her public profile sits lower than most in the chamber, and hearings draw a sharper edge from her than private talks do.
Lizzie Fletcher.speaks: Her speech runs fast with short pauses between phrases, and her pitch and volume shift a great deal. She describes her work in less detailed terms than most, and her wording carries much less emotional charge. Delivery from her is quick and lively rather than dense. In hearings, she brings a combative streak that is above typical. Quick turns, not long arguments, define how she takes the floor.
Lizzie Fletcher.decides: She weighs an ask by who it helps and whether the next step is clear. Her record of seeing bills through means she follows up once she commits. Bills from her span fewer issues than typical, so an ask that sits inside her areas fits best. Outside voices weigh on her more than most members do, so a yes can shift as they weigh in. Commitments from her tend to hold when each next step has a named owner.

archetype.justification: Bear fits because his case centers on who is helped, and hearings bring out a combative side that few colleagues match.

Lloyd Smucker.bottom_line: Lead with the people your ask helps and say it briskly. Outside groups carry less weight with him, so the case itself has to do the work.
do: Say the ask briskly, in a few plain sentences
Bring people from his own community who back the ask
In a hearing, expect hard questions and answer them directly
dont: Assume he will follow through on a verbal yes
Ask him to open up at length, since he is quite reserved
Lloyd Smucker.warning_sign: In a hearing he usually presses hard, so a drop in that force is the signal. When he goes quiet and stops pressing, he is losing interest or on guard. Pause, name the concern, and offer a smaller next step.
Lloyd Smucker.follow_up: Send him a brief written note with the ask and a single next step, naming who acts and by when.
Lloyd Smucker.personality: Smucker stays quite reticent and a little less practical than most colleagues. He talks about a wider set of issue areas in public, while his bills touch a narrower set of issues. Follow through on bills trails most colleagues. A Pennsylvania member, he spent several years on a township planning commission before serving as a township supervisor. Under questioning he ranks as one of the fiercest voices in committee, yet few members are less visible in their role.
Lloyd Smucker.speaks: Talk arrives quickly, with loudness that climbs and drops much more than most, and a tone that stays flatter than nearly every colleague. Public words touch a broader mix of topics than most, and emotion runs a bit lower in their wording. In a hearing he is among the most combative members, and his delivery turns sharper to match. Outside that setting, delivery stays brisk.
Lloyd Smucker.decides: Reaching the people it serves and fitting a brief roster of topics he already handles are the tests he applies to proposals. Outside groups carry less weight with him, so the case must stand on its own. A plain case with a named beneficiary moves him faster than a long memo. Carrying things through is less dependable for him than most, so each choice needs a designated owner to hold.

archetype.justification: Focused on action, warm, and easily stirred, with less careful detail and slow, flat delivery.

Lois Frankel.bottom_line: Lead with a shared framing that gives her something to announce together. Pair it with a short, plain point, because she trails off more than most.
do: Give her something to announce together with you
Keep your points short so she can land each one
Prepare for her to be somewhat more combative than most in hearings
dont: Count on warm words alone to carry the decision, since she is focused on action
Assume a decision will be carried through without anyone tracking it
Lois Frankel.warning_sign: Her usual pattern is long, slow answers that trail off, so that alone is normal for her. Watch for her finishing each sentence crisply, which usually means she has settled the question for herself.
Lois Frankel.follow_up: Send a brief written summary after the meeting, in plain bullet form, with the one ask you need from her office.
Lois Frankel.personality: Frankel is fairly outgoing, curious, and agreeable, and she is easily stirred more than most. Warmth shows in her word choice, and her phrasing leans toward doing things more than nearly any colleague's. Her record of seeing bills through is somewhat weaker than most, and in hearings she leans harder into the exchange than the typical member. Taken together, she is a warm, engaged operator who responds to people and to concrete action, and the gap is in carrying projects to the finish.
Lois Frankel.speaks: Delivery is slow, slower than most, and volume swings somewhat more than most. Her pitch is somewhat flatter than most, even when the wording turns intense. She trails off well beyond most speakers, and her gaps are padded with much more filler than most speakers use. Answers run somewhat longer than most, though she often breaks them into rapid runs of clipped replies.
Lois Frankel.decides: Having something to announce with others is what draws her in, so shared framing wins her over. She is fairly agreeable, so she is inclined to say yes in the room, though seeing bills through is harder for her than for most. A decision with her holds when people she trusts keep the ask alive after the meeting, so allies who stay engaged matter as much as her vote.

archetype.justification: She is fairly curious and very careful, and a visible shared role suits her, though her bill follow-through is much weaker than most.

Lori Trahan.bottom_line: Give her a visible shared role on the ask, and keep the follow-up in your own hands, since her bill follow-through is much weaker than most.
do: Propose a joint announcement she can front alongside you
Name the one part of the ask you need changed before the meeting
Ask whether her office holds the bill text before you leave
dont: Mistake her curiosity for commitment to the ask
Count on press coverage alone to carry the ask
Send another push on the ask, since pressure counts for a little less with her
Lori Trahan.warning_sign: A pleasant or quiet meeting does not tell you whether she will act on the ask afterward. Before you leave, ask her office for the one date by which it will confirm the next step.
Lori Trahan.follow_up: Within a day, mail her office a one page memo that restates the ask, the shared role, and the date for each step.
Lori Trahan.personality: Trahan is fairly curious and very careful, and somewhat reserved in manner. She gets worked up readily, more than most members do. Public words carry a bit less feeling than most, and she bridges the aisle with somewhat more reach than most. Her bills touch more issue areas than most. Follow-through on bills falls well short of most colleagues, and her account of her work is less detailed than nearly any colleague's. Her public profile sits a bit lower than most colleagues'. She has spoken about growing up in the area she now represents, near Lowell National Parks.
Lori Trahan.speaks: On the House floor, pauses between her phrases come much shorter than most's in the chamber. Her pace runs well ahead of most colleagues, with little silence after each point. Her volume and pitch both move up and down somewhat more than most. Every clip in the record is a floor speech, so the pattern holds for floor speeches only.
Lori Trahan.decides: A visible shared role she can front with you fits how she responds. Her follow-through on bills runs well short of most members, so check which of her earlier bills are still moving. Before you go in, ask her office which part of the shared role she wants to front, and keep that role to one clear task. A narrow role is easier for her office to track between meetings.

archetype.justification: She is very outgoing, and in hearings she is a touch more pointed than most.

Lucy McBath.bottom_line: Lead with the people a bill helps, and let a shared announcement carry the ask. She holds her view hard once challenged, so give her a role to share credit.
do: Offer a shared announcement she can front with you
Let her finish her point before you reply
Expect her to push back firmly in hearings
Give her a warm, direct opening that names the people
dont: Assume her early yes will hold when outside pressure builds
Mistake her forceful pushback for a closed door
Lean on a long, dense case to win her over
Lucy McBath.warning_sign: Her usual pattern is warm, lively talk with a voice that rises and falls a great deal. When her pauses come more often and her pitch and volume swing wider, she is digging in, so acknowledge her point and offer a share of the credit.
Lucy McBath.follow_up: Send a short written note within a week naming the shared step, the lead, and the date for the next check.
Lucy McBath.personality: McBath counts with the most outgoing members in the chamber and stays very agreeable. Somewhat curious and somewhat careful, her wording is among the warmest in the chamber. Fired up more readily than nearly anyone in the chamber, she defends her position hard when challenged. Her talk ranges across fewer topics than most, and her descriptions of her work are a little less detailed. Visible enough, she pushes back somewhat more than most colleagues when hearings run.
Lucy McBath.speaks: Her pace runs a bit slow, and her pitch barely moves, among the flattest in the chamber. Volume rises and falls a great deal, and she pauses somewhat longer than most between phrases. Her wording is among the warmest in the chamber, and her speech carries a bit more force than typical. In conversation she keeps hold of the discussion more firmly than nearly everyone, and her sentences rarely trail off. Her answers vary in length from one turn to the next, and she uses less filler than most.
Lucy McBath.decides: Her yardstick is whether a request can become a shared win that folks in her district will notice. An agreeable streak means she is open to a fair hearing, so an ask that stays clear and fair can win her. She holds her view hard once challenged, so a pushback becomes a test of the case rather than a closed door. Outside pressure moves her far more than most members, so a single outside push can shift her view.

archetype.justification: Stories about the people a bill helps and very reliable follow through fit a protective Bear.

Luis Correa.bottom_line: Open with one real person the bill helps, then close with the dated step your bill team will own.
do: Start with one real family the bill would change
Pitch the bill across the aisle, and wait out his volume swings
dont: Speed up to fill long pauses before he finishes
Expect a hearing to settle the ask in one exchange
Luis Correa.warning_sign: By default he leans toward a somewhat more combative stance in hearings, so a silence is not a no. In a hearing, a sharper manner means he is on guard. Give him room, then restate the one ask.
Luis Correa.follow_up: Put the dated next step and the staff member who will carry it into a written note for him once the meeting ends.
Luis Correa.personality: Correa is fairly outgoing, yet his profile for his role sits very low among his House colleagues. His public words span many more issues than most colleagues, and he frames them with somewhat more careful detail than most colleagues do. His bills are carried through with very reliable follow through, and he works across party lines much more than most. Few colleagues match that mix.
Luis Correa.speaks: His pace runs among the slowest in the chamber, with pauses longer than nearly any colleague's. His volume swings across a wide range, more than nearly any colleague's. Public words cover many issues, and he frames them with extra detail compared with most colleagues. Unhurried and deliberate, he rarely speeds up to fill a silence. Each phrase lands with room around it, so the floor stays open.
Luis Correa.decides: The questions he asks of a request are who it helps and whether a named person stands behind it. Follow through is very dependable for him, so a yes from him usually holds. Pressure from the people affected shifts him more than it shifts most colleagues, so their voices should be in the room. A decision sticks only with a named next step and a set date.

archetype.justification: Her detailed, careful talk about her work and fairly reliable voting fit a diligent legislator who runs on details.

Luz Rivas.bottom_line: Come with a shared role and a clear brief, and leave with one named next step. Follow through on bills is fairly solid for her, so commitments tend to hold.
do: Offer her a joint announcement she can front
Confirm the vote date and who will track it
In a hearing, expect civil questioning and an even exchange
dont: Read her gentle tone in hearings as agreement
Luz Rivas.warning_sign: Usually she stays on the details of one bill and is among the least combative members in hearings. If she starts moving between subjects and goes quiet, she is closing the topic, so slow down and cover the one point she has not heard.
Luz Rivas.follow_up: Send her staff a one page note listing the shared role, the vote date, and who tracks it within two days.
Luz Rivas.personality: Rivas, from California, goes deep on her own work, with more careful detail than most colleagues. Her public focus stays on fewer issues than most, and she keeps her votes and bill follow up fairly solid. At hearings she comes off less combative than almost anyone, which fits a careful, low key manner. Her habit of detailed talk sets her apart, so she reads as a thorough presence rather than a showy one.
Luz Rivas.speaks: She talks at a slower pace than most, and her pitch varies a fair amount. Her volume moves across a wide range, with variation near the top in the chamber. In hearings she is one of the least confrontational voices, and her questions come across as civil and even. She treats her own work as the main subject, which keeps her talk on substance.
Luz Rivas.decides: She judges a request on how neatly it suits a visible joint role that she can help shape. Follow through on votes is fairly solid, so she tends to keep a commitment once made. She works best from a shared role, so a plan that lets her front the result gets further than a broad appeal to a wide audience.

archetype.justification: Her warmth and high energy stand out, she talks at length and works across the aisle more than most.

Madeleine Dean.bottom_line: Bring a clear ask and let her talk, since she takes long turns. Pressure from voters at home has some pull, so give her room to test the ask.
do: Open warmly and match her upbeat tone before making the ask
If she runs long, pick out the one point you need and return to it
Bring a joint bill and name the other party's cosponsor
dont: Take her high energy as a sign the ask is settled
Expect a sharp defense and do not treat it as opposition
Madeleine Dean.warning_sign: She usually talks at length, warmly, and defends her case hard. When she gives noticeably shorter answers than usual, her engagement with the argument has dropped, so stop pressing and ask what would help.
Madeleine Dean.follow_up: After the meeting, email her staff the joint bill text and the cosponsor you agreed, by Friday.
Madeleine Dean.personality: Dean is among the House's most outgoing members, with a warm, upbeat style. She reacts quickly and strongly, more than most, and she ranges widely across policy areas. Her cross aisle work runs ahead of most, and she is very visible, so she is a member people notice. When challenged she digs in, and she gives longer answers than most.
Madeleine Dean.speaks: She speaks at length in a warm, upbeat tone, and her answers stretch longer than nearly everyone else's. She rarely trails off or fills gaps with filler, and her language runs emotionally charged, more than most. In hearings she is far more confrontational than most members, and she digs in more than most. She often leads a conversation more than most do.
Madeleine Dean.decides: Her judgment of a request turns on how well it crosses lines, since reaching across lines is something she does more than most. Pressure from home has some pull on her, so local voices carry weight in her view. When challenged she defends her position more firmly than most, so a direct challenge hardens her view. So the ask lands best when she can shape the next step herself.

archetype.justification: Her pace is much slower than most members, and she sees bills through fairly reliably.

Maggie Goodlander.bottom_line: Lead with the result and the facts in a short, direct case. She is quite skeptical, so back each claim with a plain source.
do: Send the supporting facts in writing ahead of the meeting
Open with what the policy delivers in practice, then make the ask
Limit a hearing to two points she must carry out, given her slow pace
Close by confirming the next call date, since she sees bills through
dont: Match her sharp tone with sharper points in return
Stack extra figures on top of the main result
Let one outside push rewrite the plan, since she shifts under pressure more than most
Maggie Goodlander.warning_sign: Her public words are usually much sharper than most. If they turn sharper still, she has already made up her mind on the point. Stop pressing, and ask her which part of the case she still doubts.
Maggie Goodlander.follow_up: Call her staff within a day to confirm who owns each next step and its deadline.
Maggie Goodlander.personality: Goodlander is one of the most practical members in the House, and she is very careful with detail. She is quite skeptical, and her public language has much more edge than most. She is a little quicker to get heated than most members. Public language from her carries much more feeling than most, and her bills cover much narrower ground than most. She follows bills through more reliably than most, and at hearings she is a bit less combative than most. After law school she clerked for a federal chief judge.
Maggie Goodlander.speaks: Her pace, on the House floor, is much slower than most members, and her pauses are much shorter than most. Her tone barely varies, and her volume stays fairly even. Few members in the House pause so briefly, and few keep so flat a pitch. Answer in complete sentences, and leave a clear pause before you start each new reply.
Maggie Goodlander.decides: Pressure from outside sways her more than most members, and a second push with new facts can carry weight. Results with the facts behind them fit her best, so tie every figure to its named source in the room. She sees bills through fairly reliably. Point to an earlier step that has already moved before you ask for the next one.

archetype.justification: She rarely takes charge of a conversation and speaks slowly on the House floor, and her reserved manner sets her apart from more outgoing members.

Marcy Kaptur.bottom_line: Pressure moves her less than most, so a clear ask beats a hard push. Give her time to weigh the case before you follow up.
do: Send the written evidence a few days ahead
Ask her open questions so she has a clear turn to speak
Speak slowly and leave a pause after each point
Confirm the next step and its date before the meeting ends
dont: Push for an answer in the first meeting
Read her gentle, soft wording as a weak stance
Mistake her quiet manner for a yes
Marcy Kaptur.warning_sign: She usually defers to others and seldom takes charge of a conversation. If she starts taking charge, she has settled on her answer. Stop, boil her point down to one line, and ask what she needs next.
Marcy Kaptur.follow_up: Send her office a one-page note no later than Friday that restates the decision and the next date.
Marcy Kaptur.personality: Kaptur brings a very curious mind and a fairly agreeable manner to the House, though her manner is a little reserved. She runs much hotter than most members. Few members take the lead in a conversation less than she does. Her bills touch somewhat fewer policy areas than most, and she follows through on bills somewhat less than most. She has spoken with pride about her family's long record of military and public service.
Marcy Kaptur.speaks: On the House floor her delivery runs somewhat slower than most, with somewhat longer pauses between phrases. Her volume rises and falls much more than most, and her pitch changes less than most. Her answers run much longer than most, so give her room to take her full turn. Words from her are a little cooler than most, and they carry much less force than most colleagues. Keep your own voice even while she takes the time she needs.
Marcy Kaptur.decides: Written, technical detail suits her better than a spoken pitch. Pressure from outside groups reaches her somewhat less than most members. Few House members lead a conversation less than she does, so do not wait for her to steer toward a yes. Her record of seeing bills through trails most, so check on progress with her staff a few weeks after a yes.

archetype.justification: She is warm in her wording, and her public talk ranges across far more issues than most.

Margaret Hassan.bottom_line: Lead with the people the bill helps, since she is among the most moved by outside voices in the Senate.
do: Open with the people the bill helps, and keep the tone personal
Match her warmth with a personal opening, since her wording is warm
Give her room to finish, since she speaks much faster and trails off
dont: Skip cold framing, since warmth is her natural register
Assume a short answer will settle it, since her replies stretch somewhat longer than most
Margaret Hassan.warning_sign: She usually leaves filler out of her answers and speaks at a fast pace. If filler creeps in and she trails off more, she is on guard. Give her a pause, name the concern, and offer one concrete fix.
Margaret Hassan.follow_up: Within three days, hand her office a memo naming the people helped and the next step.
Margaret Hassan.personality: Hassan comes across as a little reserved, and she is somewhat curious. Her talk covers far more ground than most, and she is careful and organized. Her bills span a narrow set of issues. Votes and bills show a very strong record, and she is warm in manner. Her words carry a good deal of emotional charge. Her words lean toward action, somewhat more than most. When pressed, she takes a firm line, and her wording is far more forceful than most.
Margaret Hassan.speaks: Speech runs at a much quicker clip than most colleagues. Her pauses between phrases run somewhat shorter than most. Her pitch stays much flatter than most. Volume varies somewhat less than most. In interviews, replies stretch somewhat longer than most. Her longest replies stay somewhat longer than most. Answers vary in length much more than most colleagues. Warm and forceful, her wording takes a firm line when pressed. Emotional charge runs high, and her words carry much of it.
Margaret Hassan.decides: She judges a request on how well it serves the people it names. Outside voices sway her among the most of anyone in the Senate, so a broad coalition matters. Her track on votes and bills is very strong, so commitments tend to hold. An ask inside her core areas fits, since her bills cover a narrow field of topics. Her visibility runs somewhat lower than most colleagues, so a shared role helps. So she backs a request that names owners and dates, and she follows through.

archetype.justification: Lightly skeptical and dependable, she sees bills through more reliably than nearly any colleague in the Senate and talks in detailed terms.

Maria Cantwell.bottom_line: Open with a person the policy helps, then bring the bill status in writing. Public pressure moves her more, so back the ask with real supporters.
do: Tell one concrete story about who the policy reaches
If she asks for detail, send the bill text and the vote record
dont: Push her to commit before the written detail arrives
Treat a hearing as a place for hostile questioning
Maria Cantwell.warning_sign: She usually speaks in sharp, cool, even stretches and often leaves sentences unfinished. When her answers grow shorter and her words sharpen further, she is on guard, so stop, ask one direct question, and offer the detail in writing.
Maria Cantwell.follow_up: After the meeting, send her staff the bill status and vote record in writing, with a date for their reply.
Maria Cantwell.personality: Cantwell is a lightly skeptical member whose bills and votes are very dependable. Her public talk on policy is precise and detailed, well beyond most, and strongly focused on action. She is curious, and her language has somewhat heavier feeling than most, while it stays cool yet unusually social. In hearings she is among the least combative members, so she reads as direct rather than fiery.
Maria Cantwell.speaks: Short pauses mark her delivery, and its volume is more even than most. Replies run a bit shorter than most, and the longest turns stay brief. Often she leaves sentences unfinished, which reads as fast thinking rather than polish. Language is cool but action focused, and in hearings she is among the least combative members. Pitch stays flat, so the emotional weight comes from word choice more than from delivery.
Maria Cantwell.decides: She weighs an ask by who it helps and how concrete the stories are. Her hearing manner is among the least combative in the Senate, so a hearing rarely turns on tone. Organized outside support moves her more than most, so backing can shift her. She talks less than most in a meeting, so a request needs a dated written follow up to hold.

archetype.justification: Her wording runs much warmer than most and she is very agreeable, though her talk is among the least detailed in the chamber.

Maria Salazar.bottom_line: Bring written technical evidence early, and invite her to make the case. Lock in a dated next move, since carrying bills forward is much harder for her.
do: Walk through the facts step by step, since she is very curious about them
Let her finish each point, since she often trails off mid thought
Keep your answers short, since her answers run somewhat shorter than most
In a hearing, expect sharp questions and answer each one directly
dont: Count on her visibility alone, since follow through is much less reliable
Maria Salazar.warning_sign: In a hearing she usually turns combative and her answers trail off mid thought. Hold the pace, let her finish, and ask one short question that needs a direct answer.
Maria Salazar.follow_up: Afterward, send a short written summary with the people affected and one dated next step to her office.
Maria Salazar.personality: Salazar ranks among the most outgoing members in the chamber, and her wording runs much warmer than most. She is very curious and very agreeable, but a little looser on specifics than most. Her public profile runs higher than usual for the role, and her work talk ranks at the bottom of the chamber for precision. Wording is among the least emotionally charged in the chamber, and her tone is gentle.
Maria Salazar.speaks: Her wording reads much warmer than most, and somewhat more action focused. Her words run somewhat flatter than most, and a touch more forceful than most. The pauses between her phrases are far briefer than is typical, and her pitch stays much flatter than most. She trails off well beyond most, and her answers run somewhat shorter than most. In a hearing she is among the most combative members in the chamber.
Maria Salazar.decides: Whether it gives her a visible stage and a people focused result is her test for any request. Bills from her reach somewhat wider than most, so a broader ask can work for her. Seeing bills through is a much weaker point for her than for most, which means she needs firm dates to follow. Pressure from outside pulls on her a bit more than most members, so local voices can tip the balance.

archetype.justification: Her detailed talk about results and her dependable handling of bills fit the Bee's industrious style.

Mariannette Miller-Meeks.bottom_line: Lead with delivered results and show where the other party already backs the plan. Outside voices sway her more than most, so line up support early.
do: Put the policy's results on one page with sources
Keep your pace brisk and move through the agenda quickly
Name a colleague across the aisle who already backs it
dont: Skip long pauses, since she moves quickly between phrases
Relying on one outside voice to carry the plan backfires
Mariannette Miller-Meeks.warning_sign: In a hearing she usually keeps her challenges mild and her tone courteous. If she turns openly combative, she is on guard, so cut the detail and ask which choice she needs to make.
Mariannette Miller-Meeks.follow_up: Send her legislative director a one page results summary with the cosponsor names, by Friday.
Mariannette Miller-Meeks.personality: Miller-Meeks is somewhat outgoing and careful with organization, and she holds up under pressure a little better than most. Her talk about results is much more detailed than most, and her public words carry somewhat less charge than most. She covers a somewhat broader set of issues than most, and covering that ground, her bills span more issue areas than almost anyone's in the House. Public visibility runs much lower than most colleagues, and she represents Iowa.
Mariannette Miller-Meeks.speaks: She speaks more rapidly than most, with brief gaps between phrases and a pitch that stays flatter than most. Careful, detailed framing marks each policy point she makes, far more than most, while her range of issues runs somewhat wider than most. Answers move briskly through the agenda, which suits a fast pace. Her delivery leaves less room for long silences between points.
Mariannette Miller-Meeks.decides: The results an ask delivers matter to her, as does how many colleagues across the aisle already back it. Her bills span more issue areas than almost anyone's in the House, so an ask that connects to several areas can find a home. A commitment from her arrives once backing is visible, since pressure from beyond the room sways her more than most. Written results make that base easier to see.

archetype.justification: Her strong work with the other side, somewhat wider issue range and gentle words earn the Beaver label.

Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.bottom_line: Lead with the cooperative case and bring a credible outside voice. Outside pressure moves her more than most, so others backing it helps.
do: Frame the ask as a bill she can sign with members across the aisle
Let long answers finish before you respond
Bring a local voice from her district to the meeting
dont: Treat a warm reply as proof the vote is secured
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.warning_sign: Usually she talks at length, fills pauses with filler words and takes a while to land on her point. When her answers get short and she stops giving reasons, she is guarded and holding back. Pause, then ask one closed question.
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.follow_up: Within the week, email her a plain summary of agreed points with the next step and the staffer who owns it.
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.personality: Gluesenkamp Perez is a very outgoing, curious and agreeable member who works with the other side more than almost anyone. She is careful in her approach and less easily flustered than most. She talks about her issues across a somewhat wider range, and her words are very gentle. Speech runs long, with many filler words and long answers. Follow through runs somewhat behind most colleagues.
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.speaks: She speaks in a gentle, orderly way, and she sounds fairly careful when she covers her work in detail. Answers run long for her and vary less than almost anyone's. She often leans on filler words and pauses for long stretches between phrases. Her volume and pitch rise and fall more than most. In formal hearings she is less combative than most members.
Marie Gluesenkamp Perez.decides: Fit with a shared, cooperative bill matters most to her, and her record of working across the aisle keeps her receptive to it. Her follow through is less reliable, so a verbal yes is only a start. Outside voices carry extra weight with her, more than most, so one credible advocate can tip her. Her backing holds only once the plan is in writing, with a responsible person and a deadline attached.

archetype.justification: Few House members are less inclined to lead a conversation, and her replies are shorter than nearly anyone's.

Marilyn Strickland.bottom_line: Narrow the ask to one clear point. Backing from others carries weight with her, so line it up first.
do: Send written technical evidence ahead of the first meeting
Keep the meeting small, with only the people who must decide
Ask one question at a time and wait through her short answers
Frame each point as a concrete step she can take
dont: Start with the headline outcome before the details
Fill the first minutes with small talk before the ask
Pile on upbeat excitement, since her own wording is flatter than nearly anyone's
Marilyn Strickland.warning_sign: She usually lets others hold the floor. If she takes charge of the conversation, she has stopped leaving room for your point. Stop, restate the ask in one sentence, and wait for her next question.
Marilyn Strickland.follow_up: Send her staff a one-page written summary within a week, with the next step and its date.
Marilyn Strickland.personality: Strickland carries a quiet, low-key presence, and she is a bit harder to rattle than most. Her public profile runs lower than most, and few House members are less willing to take the lead in a conversation. She builds ties across the aisle somewhat more than most, and her bills touch a bit more policy areas than most. Follow-through on bills trails most colleagues a little. Her public talk about her work is a bit less detailed than most, and her public words hold a little less feeling than most.
Marilyn Strickland.speaks: On the House floor her pace is slower than most, and her pauses between phrases run much longer than most. Her volume swings more than nearly everyone's in the House. In interviews her replies are shorter than nearly anyone's, and they arrive in brisk bursts much more than most. Her wording carries less excitement than nearly anyone's, so keep your own pitch restrained.
Marilyn Strickland.decides: Repeated backing from outside voices can carry real weight with her, since she responds to it more than most. She joins bills from the other party a bit more than most, so ask whether she would sign on to this one. Her follow-through trails most colleagues a little, so a yes is only a beginning, and you should put the next step in writing before she commits.

archetype.justification: Bear fits: he pushes harder in formal exchanges, and his loudness swings more widely than nearly any colleague's.

Mario Diaz-Balart.bottom_line: Bring a practical case with a dated next step, since follow through on bills runs well behind. Public pushing counts for more with him, so a broad coalition counts.
do: Bring a practical plan with the costs and results spelled out
Get a dated commitment in writing, since follow through runs well behind
Build a broad coalition of groups who back the ask
dont: Leave the follow up open ended, since his record on bills is weak
Treat a sharp hearing reply as settled, since his volume swings and bills stall
Mario Diaz-Balart.warning_sign: In a hearing, he usually sharpens noticeably, so watch his tone there. Behind closed doors, if his answers shrink and he goes quiet, he is holding back, so ask what he still needs settled.
Mario Diaz-Balart.follow_up: Send his staff a written summary with one dated next step, then check on it within three days.
Mario Diaz-Balart.personality: Diaz-Balart leans firmly practical and is a little reserved. He does not rattle easily, and his public words carry a touch more heat than most. His public range of topics ranks among the narrowest, and his legislation covers few areas. Follow through on bills lags well behind colleagues, so his record is uneven. Taken together, these traits make his public manner plain and direct.
Mario Diaz-Balart.speaks: His delivery runs a notch slower than most, and his loudness swings more widely than nearly any colleague's. His public range of topics ranks among the narrowest, and his words carry a touch more heat than most. Pace and volume give his public talk a lively, uneven rhythm. Language stays focused on a few policy areas, so the rhythm carries the emphasis.
Mario Diaz-Balart.decides: He values a practical payoff, and he wants a dated plan to come with the ask. Legislation touches few policy areas, so an ask inside those areas fits him best. Public pushing counts for more with him, so a broad coalition can change his position. Follow through is weak on his bills, so a decision stays firm only when a named person keeps checking it.

archetype.justification: He is very outgoing and agreeable, talks in much more careful detail than most, and digs in when someone pushes back.

Mark Alford.bottom_line: Bring the written technical evidence ahead of time and let the detail carry the ask. He digs in when challenged, so be ready with the detail for each objection.
do: Bring written technical evidence ahead of time
Ask for a dated next step in writing
Be ready with the detail for each objection
Let him take the lead on the technical walk through
dont: Rely on a warm tone alone to carry the ask
Bring the technical case late in the process
Read his clean, filler-free answers as full agreement
Mark Alford.warning_sign: Usually his answers come full and tidy. If he stops digging in when challenged and concedes a point, he is reconsidering, so ask which point gave him pause.
Mark Alford.follow_up: Send him a written technical summary with sources and a dated next step within a week.
Mark Alford.personality: Alford is outgoing and agreeable, and his public voice is gentle. He speaks in much more careful detail than most, and his interest is practical and social. Digging in when someone pushes back is his habit, and filler words barely appear. He is a detail oriented member who engages when the technical case is strong and the sources check out.
Mark Alford.speaks: His answers run long, and his longest replies stretch far past what most colleagues give. Pauses are a little longer than average, and he trails off more than most. Filler is almost absent from his speech. He digs in once someone pushes back, and rapid strings of brief replies come from him much less often than from most. His tone stays gentle while his words stay focused on what gets done.
Mark Alford.decides: An ask rises or falls on its technical support and the results it delivers. Pressure from outside the room carries a little less weight for him, and he digs in when challenged. So a decision needs written technical support and a dated next step to hold. He values sources he can check himself, and he expects the same care from the people who make the case.

archetype.justification: Highly curious, he talks about a wide range of issues and is less dependable than most at carrying bills forward.

Mark DeSaulnier.bottom_line: Put the written case before him and agree the next step before you leave. He is less dependable than most at seeing bills through, so give the commitment an owner.
do: Send the written technical case ahead of the meeting
Bring a partner from the other side who has joined his bills
In a hearing, expect a civil and restrained exchange
Bring the broader questions he will want to explore
dont: Read a polite hearing as agreement with your ask
Assume a missed step means he has refused
Mark DeSaulnier.warning_sign: In a hearing he is usually among the least combative members, so a firmer line from him is the change to watch. That usually means he grows guarded, so ask what he needs to see.
Mark DeSaulnier.follow_up: Once the meeting ends, send his office the written case with the commitments listed, and name the staffer who will chase each one.
Mark DeSaulnier.personality: DeSaulnier is highly curious, with a reserved edge and a fairly careful, organized streak. He ranges widely across issues, and his words carry strong feeling, yet he goes into detail less than many colleagues. Working across the aisle, he does so somewhat more than most, while his bills cover a bit more ground. Less dependable in finishing bills, he is far less combative in hearings than most. He is less visible than most, and he represents California.
Mark DeSaulnier.speaks: He talks about a wide range of issues, with strong feeling in his words and less careful detail than many colleagues. Pace is among the slowest in the chamber, with long pauses, and his volume swings a great deal. His pitch also moves noticeably. When hearings begin he stays among the least combative figures, so his manner reads as courteous rather than forceful.
Mark DeSaulnier.decides: Prior to any choice he asks whether he can carry it across the aisle, since he deals with the other side somewhat more than most. He is less dependable at seeing bills through, so a written commitment with a named owner holds him better than a verbal one. Outside pressure counts for slightly less with him, so the record matters more than volume. A decision needs a named owner and a written record to stick.

archetype.justification: He follows his bills to the finish much more reliably than most, and few House members speak with his level of precision.

Mark Harris.bottom_line: Lead with the results your ask delivers, since a results case is the frame that fits him best.
do: Bring a sourced account of the results, with the bill history attached
Open with the outcome in one plain sentence, before any background
Keep your wording gentle and direct, since his words run gentler than most
Confirm the meeting length with his office before you arrange the room
dont: Pile on reminders after he agrees, since he finishes bills much more reliably than most
Press for a commitment before he has the full documentation
Pitch the case as a sweeping vision for the whole chamber
Mark Harris.warning_sign: He usually keeps his wording gentle and plain. If it turns sharper than that, he is weighing whether your case holds. Put the open question to him plainly, and ask him to name the one point he still doubts.
Mark Harris.follow_up: Send his staff a short results summary within a few days, listing the next step and its date.
Mark Harris.personality: Harris is a legislator whose bills reach the finish much more reliably than most. When he discusses his work, his terms are among the most careful and exact in the House, and he explains each step with care. His public talk covers much narrower ground than most members in the House. He also casts his roll-call votes much more dependably than most.
Mark Harris.speaks: His public words stay gentle, and they carry a bit less charge than most. His public remarks lean mild and plain, with fairly gentle wording compared with most members. Keep your own wording plain and direct, and lay out each of your points in order. When he raises a doubt, answer in plain sentences rather than with a sharper point.
Mark Harris.decides: He decides on results, so show concrete outcomes early. Once he commits, his follow-through is much stronger than most, so his commitments hold up well over time. Keep the comparison plain, with the status quo set beside your proposal and each cost named. End by asking which result he would want to see first, and confirm the date for it.

archetype.justification: His language runs clearly upbeat and more action oriented than most colleagues, with careful organization behind it.

Mark Kelly.bottom_line: Lead with what the policy delivers and back it with allies, since pressure from outside moves him more than most members.
do: Show which members across the aisle already back the ask
Give his short turns room, and let him finish when a sentence trails off
Match his upbeat tone with a concrete plan
dont: Assume his upbeat tone and forceful phrasing mean he has already committed
Treat his filler words as hesitation
Mark Kelly.warning_sign: He usually answers in somewhat shorter turns. When a challenge lands and sentences trail off unfinished, read it as guard going up, so stop pushing and give him one clear point to answer.
Mark Kelly.follow_up: By Friday, ask his office to confirm, and send him a single page listing results and the bipartisan cosponsors.
Mark Kelly.personality: Kelly shows a fairly outgoing and curious side, and his manner is careful and orderly. Public tone runs cool, yet his language is clearly upbeat and focused on getting things done. He is harder to rattle than colleagues, and he deals with the other side more than most. In conversation he steps back a little more than most, and he is far more visible than his role would suggest.
Mark Kelly.speaks: His language carries strong emotional charge, and his phrasing is a little more forceful than colleagues. He answers in somewhat shorter turns than most. On the floor, pitch swings more than nearly any colleague does, and delivery pauses a little longer between phrases than most. His sentences trail off a little more than most. On the floor loudness swings somewhat more than most.
Mark Kelly.decides: Results an ask delivers, along with the facts behind it, matter most to him, since they fit well with how he frames issues. Pressure from beyond sways him more than most colleagues, and he reaches out across lines somewhat more than most. He dominates talk a little less than most, so a yes from him tends to follow strong outside support.

archetype.justification: His pace runs much slower than most colleagues', his pauses run long, and hearings draw less sharpness from him.

Mark Messmer.bottom_line: Keep any formal session plain and short, since hearings draw less combat from him than from most members. Let each point land before you add the next.
do: Describe the step in the bill's own words in formal settings
Match his slower floor pace in formal settings, then name one step he can finish
Let his long pauses end in formal settings, then ask for a yes that holds
Check his recent roll-call record before you make the ask
dont: Expect outside groups to carry the ask for you
Pitch a broad new vision before the practical steps
Read his gentle hearing questions as support for the ask
Mark Messmer.warning_sign: He usually keeps a mild tone in hearings, so narrow, pointed questions stand out. When his questions narrow to one point, he is testing that point, not the whole ask. Narrow the next step to that point alone.
Mark Messmer.follow_up: Email his office a recap of the next step, in a page or less, within a few days.
Mark Messmer.personality: Messmer is a little reserved by nature, and practical concerns shape his approach more than ideas do. Careful detail is not where he shines. His bills stick to a narrow set of topics, and he gets his bills through the process more reliably than most. He has talked publicly about his Catholic faith. Few members of the House are as practical as he is.
Mark Messmer.speaks: Across House-floor speeches, his pace runs far slower than most colleagues', and his pauses run much longer than most. His volume swings widely, much more than most colleagues. His tone stays mild in a hearing, and he is less combative there than most members. In formal settings, wait out each long pause before you respond, and keep your questions short. Expect his answers to come slowly, so let each one finish before you take the next turn.
Mark Messmer.decides: Outside pressure moves him somewhat less than most members do, so each ask has to stand on its own. Tie each ask to a bill he has already moved through the process, since he tends to see bills through. Name that bill in the very first line of the ask. End by asking him which step he is ready to approve.

archetype.justification: Few colleagues are as curious as he is, and his bills reach well beyond the usual areas.

Mark Pocan.bottom_line: Bring a visible shared role for him to lead and agree a single next step before you leave.
do: Offer him a joint announcement, since he is curious and very publicly exposed
Keep turns short and quick, since he answers in fast runs of brief replies
Confirm the next step with his staff, since his follow through runs well below typical
dont: Expect long pauses from him, since his pauses run short and bills lag
Let a single long reply set the pace, since his replies come back fast
Hammer one ask across many meetings, since public objections sway him somewhat less
Mark Pocan.warning_sign: He usually answers in quick bursts of turns, so a stretch of silence from him stands out. If he suddenly gives long answers or turns combative in a hearing, he is on guard, so ask one question and let him finish.
Mark Pocan.follow_up: Send his office a short sheet listing agreed steps, each with an owner and a date, by Friday.
Mark Pocan.personality: Pocan is somewhat sociable and curious beyond nearly everyone. He keeps details looser than most, and he gets worked up a bit more easily. Across public remarks he covers a wide range of topics, but his wording carries modest emotional charge. His public exposure sits far above what his role would suggest. His bills cover much wider ground than most colleagues' bills.
Mark Pocan.speaks: His delivery runs a little slower than most, and his pauses are much shorter than typical. His volume stays even from phrase to phrase, and his pitch stays flatter than most colleagues. Brief bursts of turns are his norm, and even his longest answers run shorter than typical. His public talk is very social and flat in tone, with little assertive force. When a hearing turns adversarial, he presses witnesses far more than typical.
Mark Pocan.decides: He gauges requests by how neatly they align with the many fields his bills touch, since his bills range widely. A visible shared role appeals to him, since his public exposure runs well above his role. Outside pressure moves him somewhat less than most members, so an ask must rest on its own merit. Follow through lags far behind norms, so a yes requires a named check on progress.

archetype.justification: Reserved more than almost anyone, careful and organized, with among the longest interview answers.

Mark Takano.bottom_line: Bring a careful written case and leave with a named next step. He follows bills through reliably, so a clear commitment will hold.
do: Bring the written case before the meeting, since he follows bills closely
Give him room to finish, since his answers run long
Confirm the next step in writing before you leave
dont: Fill silences, since he rarely takes charge of the talk
Read his reserved manner as having no view on the bill
Mark Takano.warning_sign: He usually answers in quick bursts, by default. If the bursts stop and he goes quiet, he is on guard or losing interest. Ease off, shorten your point, and let him set the pace.
Mark Takano.follow_up: Within two days, give his office a written summary that names the owner of the next step.
Mark Takano.personality: Takano is reserved more than almost anyone in the House, and fairly curious in his interests. He is careful and organized, and he covers a wider set of topics than most. Descriptions of his work carry far more care and detail than most, and his bills show very reliable follow through. In conversation he takes charge less than almost anyone, and his long answers often trail off before the end.
Mark Takano.speaks: He talks somewhat slowly, and his volume varies far more widely than most. Answers come in quick bursts of brief replies, and words come across cooler than almost anyone's anywhere in the House. He is much less forceful in his phrasing and gives longer answers when he does settle in. Filler appears somewhat more than most in his speech. He trails off before the end of a sentence.
Mark Takano.decides: He weighs an ask on its written detail and on whether it fits bills he already follows. Across his bills he touches a few more topics than most, so a new ask has to connect to them. Pressure from outside gets less of a grip on him than on most members. A commitment he makes tends to stick, so a decision with a named owner and date holds.

archetype.justification: He is somewhat curious and agreeable, covers much wider ground than most, and is very visible in public.

Mark Warner.bottom_line: Lead with the angle that crosses party lines, because outside pressure moves him more than nearly any member.
do: Open warmly, since he is outgoing and his public words run gentler than most
Pin down a dated next action, since he is much less dependable on bills
In a hearing expect pointed questioning and prepare firm answers
dont: Assume a private ask alone will carry him
Bury him in process talk when he wants the next action
Read his agreeable tone as a yes already given
Mark Warner.warning_sign: Usually he trails off, so an unfinished answer is his normal style. If he suddenly finishes each point cleanly and then goes silent, he is on guard or losing interest. Give him room, then pick up the thread with a single plain question.
Mark Warner.follow_up: Within two days, email his staff the next action and its date in writing, so nothing drifts.
Mark Warner.personality: Warner is a vice chair in his party's Senate leadership, sits on Banking, and represents Virginia. Somewhat outgoing and somewhat curious, he carries an agreeable streak that shows in his public words. Among the most careful and organized members, he is far less easily rattled than the typical colleague. Across a far broader set of topics than the average colleague, his public words carry among the most emotional charge in the chamber. A bit more willing than most to reach across party lines, his record of seeing bills through is much less dependable.
Mark Warner.speaks: His pace runs a notch quicker than most colleagues, with slightly longer pauses and a pitch that moves a bit more than usual. Action, not social talk, fills his words, and his wording stays somewhat gentler than most. Interview answers run somewhat shorter than most and often trail off. In hearings, his manner turns far more combative, while his public words carry among the highest emotional charge in the Senate.
Mark Warner.decides: Asks are weighed on whether they can win over colleagues on both sides. He is far more ready to move when outside voices press him than when a private case is made alone. Because he is much less dependable at seeing bills through, his yes needs a dated next step to hold. In a hearing he turns sharper, so he will test an ask there. So a decision from him sticks only when it has an owner and a date attached.

archetype.justification: His reserved manner, long answers and slow, pausing speech fit a slow, deliberate operator who takes his time.

Marlin Stutzman.bottom_line: Bring written technical evidence and a narrow, clear ask, since outside voices carry less weight with him and he needs time to work through a case.
do: Share the full technical record before the meeting
Hold your reply until his long answer is fully done
Ask one narrow question at a time
dont: Mistake his quiet manner for a closed door
Count on cross aisle warmth to bring him along
Marlin Stutzman.warning_sign: He is normally slow and talks at some length, so length alone is normal. If his answers suddenly get clipped and he presses his point, he is wary, so slow down, name the concern, and give him time before you answer.
Marlin Stutzman.follow_up: After the meeting send him the full technical record with one narrow question, and ask him to reply with a time for a follow up call.
Marlin Stutzman.personality: Stutzman carries a little reserve and is less exacting about details than his peers. Cross party work is rare for him, one of the lowest levels in the House. He rarely takes charge of a conversation and lets others lead. Public talk from him stays on a slightly tighter set of subjects than colleagues do. He is fairly visible, sits on the Financial Services committee, and represents Indiana.
Marlin Stutzman.speaks: Answers from him run far longer than colleagues', and in interviews they run longer still. Sentences often trail away before they finish, more than nearly any colleague's. Answer lengths stay even across turns, and words carry more filler than nearly anyone's. Public language is flatter in excitement and much less forceful than colleagues', and it stays gentler than colleagues'. Speech is slow, with long pauses between phrases and a voice that moves up and down more than nearly anyone's.
Marlin Stutzman.decides: He reads an ask through how carefully the technical record holds up, since technical framing fits him. Cross party backing counts for little with him, since such ties are rare in his record. He rarely takes the lead in a room, so any motion must name an owner who will set the next step. Outside backing weighs less with him, so the case itself has to carry the decision.

archetype.justification: Butterfly fits because she is fairly outgoing, fairly visible, and her details are looser than most.

Marsha Blackburn.bottom_line: Keep the ask short and tied to a checkable claim, and expect a sharp challenge. Pressure from outside groups moves her more than most, so backers help.
do: Bring evidence she can check, since she is quite skeptical
