Outside voices move her more than most, so a push from them can change where she lands.

archetype.justification: She is reserved and one of the most detail-minded members, and she talks at one of the slowest paces in the House with long pauses.

Valerie Foushee.bottom_line: Give her room to answer, since she is quite reserved, and name the one result you want.
do: State the date you need her answer before the meeting starts
Open by stating your ask in one sentence
Allow long pauses before you speak, then name the step she will own
Keep your tone level in hearings, where she ranks among the least combative
dont: Mistake her reserve for disinterest
Read her mild manner in hearings as a yes
Count on outside pressure to close the ask for you
Valerie Foushee.warning_sign: In hearings she is usually among the least combative, so an edge would stand out. If she turns openly sharp with a witness, the point has struck a nerve. Ask which part touched it, and answer that part first.
Valerie Foushee.follow_up: Within a week, send her staff the detail in writing, with one dated step to follow.
Valerie Foushee.personality: Foushee is one of the most practical members in the House. Quite reserved, she is careful and organized, and among the most detail-minded members in the House. Her bills reach a few fewer issues than most, and she is fairly dependable about seeing them through. The range of issues she talks about is one of the narrowest in the House. Her hearing manner is among the mildest in the House.
Valerie Foushee.speaks: Her pace is one of the slowest in the House, and her pauses run longer than most. Volume stays one of the most even in the House, and her pitch is one of the flattest. She describes her work in one of the most careful, detailed ways in the House, so bring the detail with you. Her volume and pitch stay so flat that a rising tone will not tell you much.
Valerie Foushee.decides: Her follow-through on bills is fairly reliable, so judge the ask by bills she has already seen through. Bring a few of those finished bills, each with what it changed in one line, and let her compare your ask with them. Put the finished bill closest to yours first, so the comparison comes before any other detail in your handout, and keep the first page to that bill alone.

archetype.justification: Few colleagues are as practical as he is, and his public profile stays low.

Vern Buchanan.bottom_line: Keep the case brief and concrete, since public pressure shifts him far less than his colleagues.
do: Frame the ask around results he can see on the record
Send the detailed bill text ahead so he can read it on his own time
Give him time to decide, since he rarely reacts quickly to pressure
Leave room for his long pauses, and check each bill step with his staff
dont: Read his silences as a verdict, since his votes and bills lag his colleagues
Count on him to front a public push, since he stays much less visible
Push him for a quick decision before he has weighed the case
Vern Buchanan.warning_sign: A general meeting will not show how he handles a direct challenge or a hard question. Ask a colleague who has worked with him in committee how he responded last time.
Vern Buchanan.follow_up: Send him a one page summary of the decision and its next step by Friday.
Vern Buchanan.personality: Buchanan is a little reserved, and he is hard to fluster, more so than most colleagues. His public wording runs a notch more emotional than most, and he gives less detail about his own work. Follow through on bills and votes runs far lower than most colleagues. His public profile sits far below what his role would suggest. Florida is his home base.
Vern Buchanan.speaks: His gaps between phrases run well past typical, so a conversation moves at his speed. His pitch stays among the flattest in the chamber, and his volume varies much less than most. When he describes his own work, his coverage runs narrower than nearly any colleague's. His wording carries a notch more charge than his flat delivery suggests. Taken together, his delivery feels deliberate rather than quick.
Vern Buchanan.decides: He weighs an ask by its practical payoff, since few colleagues match his practical bent. Public pressure shifts him far less than his colleagues, so an ask must win on its merits. His record on bills and votes lags most colleagues, so a decision needs a named owner to hold. He keeps a low public profile, so credit for shared wins rarely lands on him.

archetype.justification: Warm and people focused, with community impact as her frame and an emotional, highly visible public voice.

Veronica Escobar.bottom_line: Let her steer the talk, since she takes charge more than most, then fix one concrete next step before you leave.
do: Lead with the community the ask helps, since her words are less sharp than most
Open with a warm, personal account of the people affected
In a hearing, expect sharper questioning than usual
dont: Rush her to a decision before outside voices have weighed in
Read her warmth as agreement with your ask
Veronica Escobar.warning_sign: She usually steers the talk and often trails off mid sentence. If she finishes her sentences and stops steering, she is on guard, so ask her to name the one thing she needs.
Veronica Escobar.follow_up: Send a short written summary of the next step, with the names of the people who will join it and a date to check back.
Veronica Escobar.personality: Escobar is very outgoing and very visible. Her words are warm and emotionally charged, more so than most colleagues'. Conversations tend to bend her way somewhat more than most. She trails off mid sentence much more than most members. Getting worked up comes more readily to her than to most, and it shows in her public words. Her bills reach a slightly wider set of topics than most. Her description of her work is much less detailed than most.
Veronica Escobar.speaks: Her public words are warm and emotionally charged. Her description of her work is much less detailed than most. In conversation her answers come out somewhat short, and she often trails off mid sentence. Her delivery runs slower than most, and her pitch barely moves, though her volume holds fairly even. In hearings she tends to be more combative than most.
Veronica Escobar.decides: She weighs an ask by how it serves the people in her district. It also has to fit the issues she already works on. Outside voices sway her a little more than most, so a local coalition carries weight with her. Her bills reach a slightly wider set of topics, so an ask inside her areas fits best. A decision needs a named next step to stick.

archetype.justification: Skeptical, sharper than most in her words, and much less social, she gives long answers and works on her own terms.

Victoria Spartz.bottom_line: Start with the payoff of the policy, stated in one plain line. Outside pushback moves her more, so one clear case holds up better.
do: Put the outcome in one direct sentence before any background
If she gives a long answer, let her finish before you respond
dont: Repeat the same point with more force after she objects
Assume a hearing will stay civil with her
Victoria Spartz.warning_sign: She usually answers in stacked, rapid turns and defends her view when challenged. When she stops stacking turns and speaks through one unbroken reply, she is on guard, so stop pressing and offer a dated written summary.
Victoria Spartz.follow_up: After the meeting, send her office a short written summary of the one result and the date she should reply by.
Victoria Spartz.personality: Spartz is a skeptical member who is less practical than most and gets worked up readily and speaks with heavy emotional weight. She covers a narrow range of issues in long, detailed answers and fills them with filler words. Her manner is much less social, and her words lean away from action, so she reads as intense and independent rather than warm. In the room she keeps to her lane and holds her ground.
Victoria Spartz.speaks: Her answers are long and detailed, and her words carry heavy emotional weight with some edge. She fills them with filler words and pauses only briefly between phrases, so she sounds fluent rather than halting. Pace is slow, and her pitch stays flat, so the weight comes from word choice, not delivery. When challenged she defends her view somewhat more than most and keeps her ground.
Victoria Spartz.decides: She tests an ask with skepticism and wants the case argued, not assumed. She leads conversations less often than most, so she rarely drives a discussion to its own close. A visible chorus of outside voices moves her more than most. Because she is less reliable at seeing bills through, commitments need a dated written record, so an ask unargued in writing struggles in her review.

archetype.justification: He talks and sponsors bills across a narrow range, and his details run looser than most.

Vince Fong.bottom_line: Bring one specific ask he can announce with you, because pressure moves him much less than most members.
do: Propose a practical joint announcement or event he can front
In a hearing, expect him to press hard and stay combative
dont: Lean on outside groups to push him toward a yes
Vince Fong.warning_sign: He is usually a little reserved in the room. In a hearing, a jump to combative questioning means he is pressing hard, so keep your points short and concrete rather than argue back.
Vince Fong.follow_up: Send him a written one page summary with the single ask and who will announce it with him, and set a date for his reply.
Vince Fong.personality: Fong is a little reserved and much less exact with specifics than most colleagues. He keeps his talk and his bills within a narrow range of issues, fewer than almost anyone in the House. He is among the most combative members in hearings. Reserve and narrow focus make him a figure who keeps to what he knows best in the room and stays within it.
Vince Fong.speaks: He describes his work in somewhat looser terms than most colleagues, and his talk stays on a narrow set of issues rather than wandering. In a hearing he turns combative and presses each point hard. His points stay on one subject in the room. Hearing manner and room manner are really different things with him. His public words stay narrow too.
Vince Fong.decides: He weighs a request by how neatly it sits inside his own narrow lane, and he judges it mainly on that fit rather than on its scale. A shared public role on his item gives him a clear reason to commit. Pushes from outsiders sway him far less than most members, so an outside push alone will not carry a choice with him in the end.

archetype.justification: Somewhat reserved, she is very dependable on votes and bills, and on the floor she speaks slowly and pauses at length.

Virginia Foxx.bottom_line: Lead with results and let her take the time she needs, since outside pressure moves her much less.
do: Open with what the policy delivers in a few plain sentences
Point to her record of seeing bills through
Let her long pauses run before you fill the silence
dont: Count on a crowd of allies to tip her decision
Rush her through a long list of points
Virginia Foxx.warning_sign: A general meeting will not show how she handles a bill that goes sideways. Ask a staffer who has worked a hard bill with her what she did when it stalled, and plan around that.
Virginia Foxx.follow_up: After the meeting, send her office the results on one page, so the facts are on file before the next vote.
Virginia Foxx.personality: Foxx is a little reserved and a little practical, with careful and organized habits that show in her detailed talk about her work. Among colleagues, she is somewhat more easily stirred up than the typical one. Her talk ranges over a somewhat narrower set of topics, while her bills span a much smaller set of issues. Very dependable on votes, she also sees her bills through. In her first term, she represents North Carolina.
Virginia Foxx.speaks: On the floor she speaks slowly, with long pauses between phrases, and her volume rises and falls somewhat more than most. When she talks about her own work, her answers are careful and detailed. Her range of issues is somewhat narrower than the typical colleague's, and she tends to build each answer from specifics rather than wide themes. This delivery comes from floor speech only, so it is not a measure of how she sounds in interviews.
Virginia Foxx.decides: She weighs an ask on what it delivers and on the facts behind it, so a short, plain case gets further with her than a loud campaign does. Outside pressure moves her much less than it moves the typical member. Her bills span a much smaller set of issues, so she judges an ask by its fit with the work she already does. Once she commits, she is very dependable about votes and bills, so the yes she gives tends to stick.

archetype.justification: His very curious outlook, wide bill range, and long answers fit a curious, wide ranging member.

Warren Davidson.bottom_line: Expect long replies, and make the ask stick through the discussion. Pressure from outside moves him much less, so the case itself must hold.
do: Give him room to answer fully before you respond
In a hearing, keep your facts ready, since he presses hard
Let his visibility carry the message to colleagues
dont: Read his long answers as a lack of focus
Rely on outside pressure to move him
Warren Davidson.warning_sign: By default he is very curious and talks at length, which is his usual style. In hearings, when his answers suddenly turn short and clipped, he is on guard, so ask the one question that matters and let him finish.
Warren Davidson.follow_up: Within two days, send his office a short summary of the bill's status and the next step with a date.
Warren Davidson.personality: Davidson is a highly curious member, with fairly careful and organized habits. He is hard to rattle, well beyond typical colleagues, and his words come across as somewhat gentler. His talk stretches beyond the bill at hand, and his bills reach far more issues than nearly anyone. Answers run long and full, and in hearings he presses hard. His exposure is high for someone in his position, so colleagues notice him.
Warren Davidson.speaks: Pace runs slightly quicker than typical colleagues. Pauses are a bit shorter than most, and pitch barely moves. Volume stays fairly even, and answers run long, well past what typical colleagues give. Words are very active, and he uses plenty of filler as he talks. Public words run warm, though he speaks with less force than typical colleagues. The overall rhythm holds from one setting to the next.
Warren Davidson.decides: He weighs an ask by whether it sits within the broad mix of issues he already takes up, and a full discussion helps him decide. Outside pressure moves him much less, so a push from others does not change his position on its own. His visibility is high, so a stance he has voiced in public carries weight with colleagues. He tends to answer at length, so a decision from him takes time to be heard.

archetype.justification: He ranks among the most outgoing colleagues, and his curiosity runs very high.

Wesley Bell.bottom_line: Lead with the question you need answered, since he is very curious about the detail. Keep it civil, since outside pressure carries a little less weight with him.
do: Bring the detail behind each bill, since he is very curious and follows bills through
Invite his input early, since he is among the most outgoing
Lead with the ask, since outside pressure carries a little less weight with him
dont: Skip soft framing, since his own wording runs somewhat sharper than most
Assume outside pressure alone will settle the question
Wesley Bell.warning_sign: He usually keeps his phrasing somewhat sharper than most. If his wording turns noticeably softer, he is on guard. Slow down, name the concern, and offer one concrete fix.
Wesley Bell.follow_up: Send him a short written summary of the open questions and the next step, within three days.
Wesley Bell.personality: Bell is outgoing and talks freely with colleagues. He is very curious and somewhat careful and organized. Being somewhat agreeable, he is also somewhat quicker to get heated than most. His wording is much less charged than most, and his phrasing runs somewhat sharper. Talk about his work runs somewhat more careful and detailed than most. He is somewhat stronger on votes and bill follow through than most colleagues. In hearings he is not combative and keeps his tone civil.
Wesley Bell.speaks: Delivery runs at a somewhat slower pace than most. His pitch stays somewhat flatter than most, and it moves somewhat less across a sentence. His wording reads as much less charged than most. Phrasing runs somewhat sharper than most, and his manner stays direct. In hearings he is not combative and keeps a civil tone. He describes votes and bills with somewhat more care than most. Emotional heat stays low in his speech, which keeps the focus on facts.
Wesley Bell.decides: He weighs an ask by how curious he is about the detail behind it. Being outgoing, he responds well to direct conversation with the people involved. Outside pressure carries a little less weight with him, so the case must rest on its own. His record on votes and bills is somewhat stronger than most, so a clearly outlined plan earns his time. So he commits when the question is clear and the next step is named.

archetype.justification: His reserved manner, careful organization and low visibility for his role fit the Tortoise.

Wesley Hunt.bottom_line: Come with a clear, specific ask and give him time to weigh it. Outside pressure counts for less with him, so the case itself must carry the ask.
do: Give him time to weigh the ask before any decision
Confirm each step in writing, since follow through is less reliable for him
In a hearing, expect him to be somewhat less combative
dont: Assume his low profile will draw support for the ask on its own
Read his reserve as opposition to the ask
Wesley Hunt.warning_sign: He usually keeps his views private in open rooms. In hearings he is less confrontational than most, so any firmer tone from him there signals he is weighing the ask. Confirm each step in writing rather than pushing for a quick answer.
Wesley Hunt.follow_up: Send his office a short written note of the agreed next step, naming the staffer who follows up and the date due.
Wesley Hunt.personality: Hunt is quite reserved and fairly careful and organized. His talk covers a far narrower set of issues than most, and his wording has very little emotional charge. Bills he carries touch a smaller set of topics than nearly anyone's, and follow through on them runs a little less dependable. He draws a little less public notice than most, and outside pressure counts for less with him.
Wesley Hunt.speaks: His manner is reserved, and his talk stays within a narrow set of issues. His wording carries very little emotional charge, so his points come across as matter of fact. In hearings he runs less confrontational than most colleagues. He tends to stay with the matter at hand rather than widen the discussion, and he speaks in a restrained way.
Wesley Hunt.decides: He weighs an ask by how cleanly it fits the few areas he already covers. Follow through on bills runs a bit less dependable for him, so a decision needs a written next step to stick. Outside pressure counts for less with him, so the case itself must carry the ask. So he commits only when the written step is clear and the case holds up alone.

archetype.justification: His reserved, careful manner and lower visibility than most earn the Tortoise label.

William Keating.bottom_line: Bring a short case on what the policy delivers. He moves more under outside pressure, so an ally who vouches for it helps.
do: Lead with the outcome the policy delivers in plain terms
Bring a colleague from the other side who backs the bill
If the setting is a hearing, expect firm questioning and answer directly
dont: Treat his quiet reserve as a sign of agreement
Count on his follow through alone to settle a stalled vote
Expect a low public profile to change his vote
William Keating.warning_sign: Usually he is combative in hearings, so sharp questioning is normal for him there. When his sharp questions fade and his answers turn guarded, he is holding back his view. Step back, restate the facts, and give him room to answer.
William Keating.follow_up: After the meeting, send him a short note with the bill's status, the facts that answer his question, and the date of the next vote.
William Keating.personality: Keating is a reserved and careful member who follows bills through with fair reliability. He is less easily rattled than most, and he gives fuller detail on his work than most colleagues. His bills span a broader set of topics than most, and he works across the aisle more than most. Emotional charge in his words is lower than almost anyone's. He is less visible than most. In hearings he is much more combative than most members.
William Keating.speaks: He speaks in a plain and reserved way, and the charge in his words is lower than almost anyone's. He gives a detailed account of his work and leans on specifics rather than broad themes. Conversation with him covers a narrow range of topics. In hearings he becomes much more combative, and his tone turns sharp. His manner is direct and businesslike, with little ornament.
William Keating.decides: Facts that stand up and a fit with what he already supports decide how he weighs an ask. He follows bills through with fair reliability and works across the aisle more than most, so a clear, shared bill can move him. Outside voices sway him more than most members, so a constituent or ally backing the ask will tip him. His support lasts only while those backers stay engaged.

archetype.justification: His frequent cross aisle work, wide range of bills and detailed talk about his work earn the Beaver label.

William Timmons.bottom_line: Bring a results focused case that speaks to shared ground, since he works across the aisle. Outside voices sway him more than most, so back the ask with trusted voices.
do: Build the ask around shared ground with members across the aisle
Match his fast pace with a brisk, tight summary
In a hearing, expect him to be somewhat more combative
dont: Mistake his quiet manner for a lack of interest in your ask
Assume outside voices will settle the question for him
William Timmons.warning_sign: Hearings usually bring out a sharper edge from him, so a firmer tone there signals he is on guard. Ease off, restate the ask in one plain sentence, and let him answer on the facts.
William Timmons.follow_up: Send his office a short written note of the agreed step, naming the staffer who will follow up and the date due.
William Timmons.personality: Timmons is one of the most reserved members in the House, yet he reacts with heat a little more readily than most. His talk reaches into a broader set of issues than most, and his work comes across with granular, exacting detail, well beyond most colleagues. Bills span more issue areas than nearly anyone's, and cross aisle work is a habit with him. He keeps a fairly low public profile for his role, though he is cooperative in tone.
William Timmons.speaks: Words come out fast, quicker than most colleagues, and his pitch runs somewhat flatter than most. Every recording of him comes from the chamber floor, so that delivery is the clearest guide. His talk about policy is more detailed than most, and his arguments reach into a broader set of issues. In hearings he runs a bit more combative, and his sharper edge shows there.
William Timmons.decides: He weighs an ask by whether it can be shared across the aisle and by the results it promises. His bills span more issue areas than nearly anyone's, so an ask inside his areas fits. Outside voices sway him more than most, so the ask needs trusted backers. So he commits when a cross aisle group stands behind the ask and the results are plain.

archetype.justification: Her skeptical outlook, easily worked up manner, and narrow set of issues fit a guarded, pointed member.

Yassamin Ansari.bottom_line: Bring one ask with solid sourcing and a local partner who backs it. She tests claims closely, so the evidence has to carry the case.
do: Put the evidence and sources in front of her before the meeting
Pair the ask with a shared role she can announce
If a hearing comes up, keep the exchange civil and brief
dont: Read a brief, civil exchange as proof she is persuaded
Count on outside pressure to change her view
Yassamin Ansari.warning_sign: By default she is quite skeptical, yet in hearings she stays noticeably less combative than most. When that hearing tone suddenly sharpens, she is on guard, so slow down and ask one question that gives her the next step.
Yassamin Ansari.follow_up: Within two days, send her office the sources you cited with a short summary of the ask.
Yassamin Ansari.personality: Ansari is a skeptical member who tests claims closely and reacts quickly when pressed. She is a bit more outgoing than most colleagues, and she is among the quickest to get worked up. Talk stays on a small set of issues and carries extra emotional weight. Bills show fairly good follow through, and public exposure runs a little above the role.
Yassamin Ansari.speaks: Her words cover a narrow set of issues and carry extra emotional weight, so her manner reads as animated. In hearings, combativeness runs noticeably lower than typical, so her tone shifts with the setting. Across the topics she names, the feeling in her words stays visible from the first sentence to the last. The change is visible to anyone who watches both settings closely.
Yassamin Ansari.decides: She weighs an ask by testing its claims, and a case that holds up under that testing carries real weight with her. Pressure from outside moves her only slightly, so a shared role she can announce matters more than a push from others. A decision from her sticks when the evidence is in hand and the shared role is clear, so she is hard to move with pressure alone.

archetype.justification: She is quietly reserved and careful, and among the most dependable on votes and bills, so a thorough, low-key case suits her.

Young Kim.bottom_line: Lead with what the plan delivers, and state it in one plain sentence before any figures. Few members match her reliability on bills, so a dated commitment still matters.
do: Confirm every figure in the outcome line against the plan text before you meet
Open with the outcome in one sentence, then offer the details
Check with her before naming her in any public material
Ask her how she would vote on the plan as written
dont: Promise more than the paper can back
Book the meeting with no set end time
Hand her a rough draft with open questions still in it
Young Kim.warning_sign: A short, general meeting does not show how she weighs the ask, so do not read a pleasant tone as a commitment. Thank her for the time and wait for her to raise the open point.
Young Kim.follow_up: Send her staff a brief written note by Friday, with the outcome, the dates, and one owner named.
Young Kim.personality: Kim is careful and organized, somewhat more than most. Her record on votes and bills ranks among the most dependable in the House. Her description of her work runs more careful and detailed than almost anyone's. A little reserved, she is also somewhat harder to rattle than most. Few members keep as low a profile in the House. Earlier in her career she worked in banking and then manufacturing finance.
Young Kim.speaks: In interviews her pace runs well slower than most, with brief gaps between phrases. Her language carries far less feeling than most. Her volume shifts up and down a bit more than most. Match her unhurried pace rather than rushing your points. Give her room to finish, and keep every point tight. Use her brief gaps to add one concrete result, not a second argument.
Young Kim.decides: Tie each part of the ask to one result the plan delivers, so each step stands on its own. Let her choose which result to test first, and answer that one fully, with no new figures, before she moves on to the rest of the plan. Before the meeting ends, name the one open risk yourself, and say plainly how you would close it.

archetype.justification: Her volume swings are among the largest in the House, and she is very reserved.

Yvette Clarke.bottom_line: Share the announcement with a colleague, since outside voices carry a little less pull on her.
do: Share the announcement with a colleague, since she is very reserved
Prepare for a hearing with clear talking points, since she runs somewhat more combative there
Give her room, since her volume swings are among the largest in the House
dont: Skip rapid questions, since her pace runs somewhat slower than most
Assume a quick yes, since outside voices sway her a little less than most
Yvette Clarke.warning_sign: In a hearing she usually sounds somewhat more combative than in a meeting. If her tone turns sharp and pointed in a hearing, she is on guard. Pause, restate the point plainly, and let her answer.
Yvette Clarke.follow_up: Send her office a short written note with the evidence attached, within two days of the meeting.
Yvette Clarke.personality: Clarke is very reserved, yet her curiosity runs very high. Her public talk covers somewhat wider ground than most. Her bills take in somewhat more areas than most colleagues. Descriptions of her own work are somewhat less exact than most. Her phrasing runs somewhat hotter than most colleagues. Public profile runs somewhat lower than most colleagues, even for her role. In hearings, her manner runs somewhat more confrontational than most members.
Yvette Clarke.speaks: Her talk ranges somewhat wider than most, across several areas. Her answers about her work come across somewhat less precise than most. Pauses between phrases run somewhat longer than most. Her pace runs somewhat slower than most. Her pitch rises and falls somewhat more than most. Volume moves up and down across a single answer. Emotional charge runs somewhat higher in her phrasing than most. Hearing settings bring out somewhat more combative edges than most members.
Yvette Clarke.decides: She weighs an ask by how well it fits the issues she already follows. Outside voices carry a little less pull on her than on most colleagues. A visible shared role gives her a reason to commit, since her public profile is somewhat lower than most. Being very reserved, she takes in an argument before she responds. So she commits only when a shared announcement and a named next step are in place.

archetype.justification: He is fairly outgoing and very curious, though his bills see much less follow-through than most.

Zachary Nunn.bottom_line: Get the decision early, since his follow-through is much weaker than most and a verbal yes can drift.
do: Ask early, with the results in your first message
Keep the case short and about what the policy does
Come back to the ask if the first meeting ends without a yes
Follow up through his staff, since his own follow-through needs prompting
dont: Pile extra asks onto the first one
Take his outgoing style as a promise he will follow through
Assume a skipped roll call means he opposes the bill
Zachary Nunn.warning_sign: A quiet meeting does not tell you he has agreed to anything. Wait for his reply in writing before you treat a point as settled.
Zachary Nunn.follow_up: Give his office a brief written summary with one next step and a date by Friday.
Zachary Nunn.personality: Nunn comes across as fairly outgoing and very curious, though his bills see less follow-through than most. He is a bit hard to rattle. His public talk covers more ground than nearly any colleague's. Few members' bills reach as many areas as his. His public detail on the work is a little looser than most. Emotion runs a bit higher in his wording than in most colleagues'. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee.
Zachary Nunn.speaks: His pauses between phrases run a little longer than most. His volume swings a bit more than most, while his pitch varies somewhat more than most. Pauses matter in his talk, so leave room before you answer. Put one question to him per turn, and let each answer end before you add more. His pauses are only a little longer than most, so do not read silence as the end of his point.
Zachary Nunn.decides: He gives outside pressure a little more weight than most members do, which is a tilt rather than a sure thing. He serves on House Financial Services, so if the bill touches that committee, ask his office which colleague there should see the case first. Let that colleague walk him through the specifics directly and in plain terms, one question at a time.

archetype.justification: Very curious and very careful, with a wide issue range and public words gentler than most.

Zoe Lofgren.bottom_line: Come ready for detailed questions and point to bills she has joined across the aisle, since she works with the other side more than almost anyone.
do: Come with answers ready to defend, since she pushes back when challenged
Point to bills she has joined with members across the aisle
Plan for a visible room, since she draws attention for her role
dont: Read her gentle tone as a sign she has no objections
Assume her curiosity means she will accept your ask without questions
Zoe Lofgren.warning_sign: By default her replies come in quick runs, and she defends her position hard once challenged. If she stops defending and starts saying less, she is losing interest or on guard, so stop and ask which point she doubts.
Zoe Lofgren.follow_up: Email her staff a brief summary stating the ask, its next step, and when she will answer, within two days.
Zoe Lofgren.personality: Lofgren is very curious and very careful, and she is hard to rattle under pressure. Reserve shows in her manner, though she is fairly agreeable beneath it. Her public talk covers issues far more widely than most, and her words come across as gentle. She works with the other side more than almost anyone, and her visibility stands out in the chamber. When challenged she defends her position much more than most.
Zoe Lofgren.speaks: She speaks very fast, and her pitch swings more than nearly anyone's. Pauses between her phrases run among the briefest in the chamber. Volume varies somewhat more than most. Public language reads as cooler than most and somewhat more forceful. In hearings she turns a bit less combative than most members, so questions come with less heat. Under challenge she defends her ground at length.
Zoe Lofgren.decides: She weighs an ask by whether it holds up under challenge, since she defends her position hard when pressed. Bills she has joined across the aisle show where she is willing to work, so pointing to them shapes her view. She defends a position once she has taken it, so her public challenge is the test that matters. A decision holds only when she has tested the ask and found it sound.
